{{BLP sources|date=December 2008}}
'''Scout Tufankjian''' is an [[Armenians|Armenian]]-[[United States|American]] [[photojournalist]] and author based in [[Brooklyn, New York]]. She is well known for her photos of American President [[Barack Obama]] during his campaign leading up to his presidency. She is also known for her photojournalism work on the [[Armenian diaspora]].

== Early life and education ==
She was born in [[Boston]], [[Massachusetts]] to an Armenian-American father, Allan, a lawyer, and an Irish-American mother, Betty. She grew up in the south shore towns of [[Whitman, Massachusetts|Whitman]] and [[Scituate, Massachusetts|Scituate]], both in Massachusetts.<ref name="ARMENIANWEEKLY11212014">Janbazian, Rupen, [http://armenianweekly.com/2014/11/21/interview-tufankjian/ "There is Only the Earth: An Interview with Photojournalist Scout Tufankjian"], ''The Armenian Weekly'', November 21, 2014.</ref>

She attended and earned a B.A. in Political Science and Government from [[Yale University]] in 2000.

== Career ==
From 2006 to 2008 she covered Senator [[Barack Obama]]'s [[Barack Obama presidential campaign, 2008|campaign for President of the United States]], and was the only independent journalist to follow him from the run up to his announcing his candidacy through his victory on election night.<ref name="PUB">{{cite news|first=Lynn |last=Andriana |authorlink= |coauthors= |title=PowerHouse Sells Out First Printing of Obama Book |url=http://www.publishersweekly.com/article/CA6615644.html |work=[[Publishers Weekly]] |publisher=[[Reed Business Information]] |date=18 November 2008 |accessdate=15 December 2008 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20091126033627/http://www.publishersweekly.com/article/CA6615644.html |archivedate=26 November 2009 }}</ref> Tufankjian took more than 12,000 photographs throughout the campaign.<ref>{{cite news |first=Ronald |last=Nurwisah |authorlink= |coauthors= |title=Scout Tufankjian: Eyewitness to Obama's historic run| url=http://network.nationalpost.com/np/blogs/posted/archive/2008/11/05/scout-tufankjian-eyewitness-to-obama-s-historic-run.aspx|work=[[National Post]] |publisher=[[Canwest]] |date=5 November 2008 |accessdate=15 December 2008 }}</ref> She released a book featuring a selection of the photographs titled ''Yes We Can: Barack Obama's History-Making Presidential Campaign'' in December 2008, which sold out its initial 55,000 copy run a month before it was released.<ref name="PUB"/>

In August 2012, Tufankjian took a photo of Michelle Obama and President Barack Obama hugging each other, and the Obama campaign staff sent this picture out on the official Obama Facebook and Twitter accounts the night of [[United States presidential election, 2012|the election]], Nov. 6, 2012. This picture became the most liked photo on [[Facebook]] and most retweeted [[Tweet (Twitter)|tweet]] in history.<ref>http://www.slate.com/blogs/future_tense/2012/11/07/facebook_photo_of_barack_obama_hugging_michelle_is_most_liked_most_retweeted.html</ref><ref>https://gizmodo.com/5959053/exclusive-the-story-behind-the-internets-most-popular-photo</ref>

==Works==
*''Yes We Can: Barack Obama's History-Making Presidential Campaign'' (2008)
* ''There Is Only the Earth: Images from the Armenian Diaspora Project'', Melcher Media, 2015. A photojournalist's study of the Armenian diaspora on its 100th anniversary.

== Personal life ==
In 2010, Scout Tufankjian married Nate Schenkkan who is also a Yale and Columbia graduate and former journalist.<ref name="WICKEDLOCALNY">[http://www.wickedlocal.com/article/20100826/News/308269731 "Tufankjian –Schenkkan engagement", ''Wicked Local'', August 26, 2010.]</ref>

==References==
{{Reflist}}

== Further reading ==
* Gonzalez, David, [http://lens.blogs.nytimes.com/2014/04/24/following-armenias-global-diaspora/?_r=0 "Following the Global Armenian Diaspora"], ''The New York Times'', April 24, 2014

* [http://news.am/eng/news/129171.html "Armenian roots and traveling with Obama – interview with photojournalist Scout Tufankjian"], ''news.am'', November 19, 2012

Motion Pictures]] | country = United States | language = English | budget = | gross = }} '''''Christopher Robin''''' is an upcoming American [[Comedy-drama film|comedy-drama]] [[adventure film]] directed by [[Marc Forster]], with a screenplay written by [[Tom McCarthy (director)|Tom McCarthy]], [[Alex Ross Perry]], and [[Allison Schroeder]]. The film is inspired by [[A. A. Milne]]'s book ''[[Winnie-the-Pooh (book)|Winnie-the-Pooh]]'' and a live-action remake of the Disney franchise [[Winnie the Pooh (franchise)|of same name]]. The film will star [[Ewan McGregor]] and [[Hayley Atwell]]. It is scheduled to be released on August 3, 2018 by [[Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures]] in the United States. ==Plot== [[Christopher Robin]], the little boy from the Winnie-the-Pooh stories, is now all-grown-up and has lost all sense of imagination. Pooh and his friends reenter Robin's life to help him find it once again. ==Cast== *[[Ewan McGregor]] as [[Christopher Robin]] *[[Hayley Atwell]] as Evelyn, Christopher's wife *[[Mark Gatiss]] as Giles, Christopher's boss *Bronte Carmichael as Madaline, Christopher's daughter ===Voice cast=== *[[Jim Cummings]] as [[Winnie the Pooh (Disney character)|Winnie the Pooh]] *[[Nick Mohammed]] as [[Piglet (Winnie-the-Pooh)|Piglet]] *[[Brad Garrett]] as [[Eeyore]] *[[Kristen Anderson-Lopez]] as [[List of Winnie-the-Pooh characters#Kanga|Kanga]]{{cite web|url=https://disneyfilmfacts.com/2017/09/17/kristen-anderson-lopez-and-wyatt-dean-hall-join-christopher-robin-voice-cast/|title=Kristen Anderson-Lopez and Wyatt Dean Hall join Christopher Robin voice cast|author=Skyler Shuler|publisher=Disney Film Facts|date=September 17, 2017|accessdate=September 17, 2017}} *Wyatt Hall as [[Roo]] ==Production== ===Development and casting=== On April 2, 2015, [[Walt Disney Pictures]] announced that a [[List of Disney live-action remakes of animated films|live-action adaptation]] based on the characters from the ''[[Winnie the Pooh (franchise)|Winnie the Pooh]]'' franchise is in development which would take a similar pattern to 2010's ''[[Alice in Wonderland (2010 film)|Alice in Wonderland]]'', 2014's ''[[Maleficent (film)|Maleficent]]'' and 2015's ''[[Cinderella (2015 film)|Cinderella]]'', with [[Alex Ross Perry]] hired to write the script and Brigham Taylor to produce the film, about an adult boy [[Christopher Robin]] returns to the [[Hundred Acre Wood]] and spend time with [[Winnie-the-Pooh|Pooh]] and the gang.{{cite news|author=Mike Fleming Jr|title=Disney Sets Live-Action ‘Winnie The Pooh’ Film; Alex Ross Perry To Write|url=http://deadline.com/2015/04/winnie-the-pooh-disney-live-action-feature-alex-ross-perry-1201392427/|accessdate=September 17, 2017|website=[[Deadline.com]]|date=April 2, 2015}} On November 18, 2016, it was reported that the studio had hired [[Marc Forster]] to direct the film, titled ''Christopher Robin,'' and the project would have "strong elements of magical realism as it seeks to tell an emotional journey with heartwarming adventure."{{cite news|author=Borys Kit|title=Marc Forster to Direct Live-Action Movie About Winnie the Pooh's Pal, 'Christopher Robin' (Exclusive)|work=The Hollywood Reporter|url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/marc-forster-direct-disneys-live-action-winnie-pooh-movie-948831|accessdate=September 17, 2017|date=November 18, 2016}} On March 1, 2017, [[Tom McCarthy (director)|Tom McCarthy]] was hired to rewrite the existing screenplay.{{cite web|url=http://variety.com/2017/film/awards/spotlight-tom-mccarthy-disney-christopher-robin-movie-1202000303/|author=Dave McNary|title=‘Spotlight’s’ Tom McCarthy to Re-Write Disney’s Live-Action ‘Christopher Robin’|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=March 1, 2017|accessdate=September 17, 2017}} The following month, [[Ewan McGregor]] was announced to play the title character and that [[Allison Schroeder]] would do additional work on the script.{{cite news|author=Silas Lesnick|title=Ewan McGregor Will Headline Disney’s Christopher Robin Movie|url=http://www.comingsoon.net/movies/news/842055-ewan-mcgregor-christopher-robin-movie|accessdate=September 17, 2017|website=[[Comingsoon.net]]|date=April 26, 2017}}{{cite news|author=Rebecca Ford|author2=Borys Kit|title=Ewan McGregor to Star in Disney's 'Christopher Robin' (Exclusive)|url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/ewan-mcgregor-star-disneys-christopher-robin-997556|accessdate=September 17, 2017|work=The Hollywood Reporter|date=April 26, 2017}}. On June 22, 2017, it was revealed that [[Gemma Arterton]] had been in negotiations to portray the wife of the titular character but, ultimately, she passed on the role.{{cite news|url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/gemma-arterton-no-longer-talks-join-christopher-robin-1016138|author=Borys Kit|title=Gemma Arterton No Longer In Talks to Join 'Christopher Robin'|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=June 22, 2017|accessdate=September 17, 2017}} In August and September 2017, [[Hayley Atwell]] and [[Mark Gatiss]] were cast as Evelyn, Christopher Robin's wife and Giles, Christopher Robin's boss, while [[Jim Cummings]], [[Kristen Anderson-Lopez]], and Wyatt Hall are set to reprise their voice roles of [[Winnie the Pooh (Disney character)|Winnie the Pooh]], [[List of Winnie the Pooh characters#Kanga|Kanga]], and [[Roo]] with [[Brad Garrett]] and [[Nick Mohammed]] cast as [[Eeyore]] and [[Piglet (Winnie-the-Pooh)|Piglet]], respectively. [[Alan Tudyk]] is currently interested in voicing [[Tigger]], though it should also be noted that Cummings has been the voice of Tigger, occasionally since 1990, starting with the 2000 film ''[[The Tigger Movie]]'', so it is possible that he could end up doing the voice for the character, despite Alan Tudyk's desire to voicing the character, however it is unknown if Tudyk or Cummings will ever Motion Pictures]] | country = United States | language = English | budget = | gross = }} '''''Christopher Robin''''' is an upcoming American [[Comedy-drama film|comedy-drama]] [[adventure film]] directed by [[Marc Forster]], with a screenplay written by [[Tom McCarthy (director)|Tom McCarthy]], [[Alex Ross Perry]], and [[Allison Schroeder]]. The film is inspired by [[A. A. Milne]]'s book ''[[Winnie-the-Pooh (book)|Winnie-the-Pooh]]'' and a live-action remake of the Disney franchise [[Winnie the Pooh (franchise)|of same name]]. The film will star [[Ewan McGregor]] and [[Hayley Atwell]]. It is scheduled to be released on August 3, 2018 by [[Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures]] in the United States. ==Plot== [[Christopher Robin]], the little boy from the Winnie-the-Pooh stories, is now all-grown-up and has lost all sense of imagination. Pooh and his friends re-enter Christopher's life to help him find it once again. ==Cast== *[[Ewan McGregor]] as [[Christopher Robin]] *[[Hayley Atwell]] as Evelyn, Christopher's wife *[[Mark Gatiss]] as Giles, Christopher's boss *Bronte Carmichael as Madaline, Christopher's daughter * Kumud Pant as Train Passenger ===Voice cast=== *[[Jim Cummings]] as [[Winnie the Pooh (Disney character)|Winnie the Pooh]] *[[Nick Mohammed]] as [[Piglet (Winnie-the-Pooh)|Piglet]] *[[Brad Garrett]] as [[Eeyore]] *[[Kristen Anderson-Lopez]] as [[List of Winnie-the-Pooh characters#Kanga|Kanga]]{{cite web|url=https://disneyfilmfacts.com/2017/09/17/kristen-anderson-lopez-and-wyatt-dean-hall-join-christopher-robin-voice-cast/|title=Kristen Anderson-Lopez and Wyatt Dean Hall join Christopher Robin voice cast|author=Skyler Shuler|publisher=Disney Film Facts|date=September 17, 2017|accessdate=September 17, 2017}} *Wyatt Hall as [[Roo]] ==Production== ===Development and casting=== On April 2, 2015, [[Walt Disney Pictures]] announced that a [[List of Disney live-action remakes of animated films|live-action adaptation]] based on the characters from the ''[[Winnie the Pooh (franchise)|Winnie the Pooh]]'' franchise is in development which would take a similar pattern to 2010's ''[[Alice in Wonderland (2010 film)|Alice in Wonderland]]'', 2014's ''[[Maleficent (film)|Maleficent]]'' and 2015's ''[[Cinderella (2015 film)|Cinderella]]'', with [[Alex Ross Perry]] hired to write the script and Brigham Taylor to produce the film, about an adult boy [[Christopher Robin]] returns to the [[Hundred Acre Wood]] and spend time with [[Winnie-the-Pooh|Pooh]] and the gang.{{cite news|author=Mike Fleming Jr|title=Disney Sets Live-Action ‘Winnie The Pooh’ Film; Alex Ross Perry To Write|url=http://deadline.com/2015/04/winnie-the-pooh-disney-live-action-feature-alex-ross-perry-1201392427/|accessdate=September 17, 2017|website=[[Deadline.com]]|date=April 2, 2015}} On November 18, 2016, it was reported that the studio had hired [[Marc Forster]] to direct the film, titled ''Christopher Robin,'' and the project would have "strong elements of magical realism as it seeks to tell an emotional journey with heartwarming adventure."{{cite news|author=Borys Kit|title=Marc Forster to Direct Live-Action Movie About Winnie the Pooh's Pal, 'Christopher Robin' (Exclusive)|work=The Hollywood Reporter|url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/marc-forster-direct-disneys-live-action-winnie-pooh-movie-948831|accessdate=September 17, 2017|date=November 18, 2016}} On March 1, 2017, [[Tom McCarthy (director)|Tom McCarthy]] was hired to rewrite the existing screenplay.{{cite web|url=http://variety.com/2017/film/awards/spotlight-tom-mccarthy-disney-christopher-robin-movie-1202000303/|author=Dave McNary|title=‘Spotlight’s’ Tom McCarthy to Re-Write Disney’s Live-Action ‘Christopher Robin’|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=March 1, 2017|accessdate=September 17, 2017}} The following month, [[Ewan McGregor]] was announced to play the title character and that [[Allison Schroeder]] would do additional work on the script.{{cite news|author=Silas Lesnick|title=Ewan McGregor Will Headline Disney’s Christopher Robin Movie|url=http://www.comingsoon.net/movies/news/842055-ewan-mcgregor-christopher-robin-movie|accessdate=September 17, 2017|website=[[Comingsoon.net]]|date=April 26, 2017}}{{cite news|author=Rebecca Ford|author2=Borys Kit|title=Ewan McGregor to Star in Disney's 'Christopher Robin' (Exclusive)|url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/ewan-mcgregor-star-disneys-christopher-robin-997556|accessdate=September 17, 2017|work=The Hollywood Reporter|date=April 26, 2017}}. On June 22, 2017, it was revealed that [[Gemma Arterton]] had been in negotiations to portray the wife of the titular character but, ultimately, she passed on the role.{{cite news|url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/gemma-arterton-no-longer-talks-join-christopher-robin-1016138|author=Borys Kit|title=Gemma Arterton No Longer In Talks to Join 'Christopher Robin'|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=June 22, 2017|accessdate=September 17, 2017}} In August and September 2017, [[Hayley Atwell]] and [[Mark Gatiss]] were cast as Evelyn, Christopher Robin's wife and Giles, Christopher Robin's boss, while [[Jim Cummings]], [[Kristen Anderson-Lopez]], and Wyatt Hall are set to reprise their voice roles of [[Winnie the Pooh (Disney character)|Winnie the Pooh]], [[List of Winnie the Pooh characters#Kanga|Kanga]], and [[Roo]] with [[Brad Garrett]] and [[Nick Mohammed]] cast as [[Eeyore]] and [[Piglet (Winnie-the-Pooh)|Piglet]], respectively. [[Alan Tudyk]] is currently interested in voicing [[Tigger]], though it should also be noted that Cummings has been the voice of Tigger, occasionally since 1990, starting with the 2000 film ''[[The Tigger Movie]]'', so it is possible that he could end up doing the voice for the character, despite Alan Tudyk's desire to voicing the character, however it is unknown if Tudyk or Cummings will ever On June 22, 2017, it was revealed that [[Gemma Arterton]] had been in negotiations to portray the wife of the titular character but, ultimately, she passed on the role.{{cite news|url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/gemma-arterton-no-longer-talks-join-christopher-robin-1016138|author=Borys Kit|title=Gemma Arterton No Longer In Talks to Join 'Christopher Robin'|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=June 22, 2017|accessdate=September 17, 2017}} In August and September 2017, [[Hayley Atwell]] and [[Mark Gatiss]] were cast as Evelyn, Christopher Robin's wife and Giles, Christopher Robin's boss, while [[Jim Cummings]], [[Kristen Anderson-Lopez]], and Wyatt Hall are set to reprise their voice roles of [[Winnie the Pooh (Disney character)|Winnie the Pooh]], [[List of Winnie the Pooh characters#Kanga|Kanga]], and [[Roo]] with [[Brad Garrett]] and [[Nick Mohammed]] cast as [[Eeyore]] and [[Piglet (Winnie-the-Pooh)|Piglet]], respectively. [[Alan Tudyk]] is currently interested in voicing [[Tigger]], though it should also be noted that Cummings has been the voice of Tigger, occasionally since 1990, starting with the 2000 film ''[[The Tigger Movie]]'', so it is possible that he could end up doing the voice for the character, despite Alan Tudyk's desire to voicing the character, however it is unknown if Tudyk or Cummings will ever Joe Thomas ''(1st team)'' | shortnavlink = Browns seasons }} The '''[[2009 NFL season|2009]] [[Cleveland Browns]] [[List of Cleveland Browns seasons|season]]''' was the team's 61st season as a professional sports franchise and its 57th season as a member of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). The team placed fourth in the [[AFC North]] with a record of 5–11, improving upon its [[2008 Cleveland Browns season|2008]] record of 4–12. This season marked [[George Kokinis]] and [[Eric Mangini]]'s first seasons as the team's [[general manager]] and [[head coach]], respectively; however, Kokinis was fired on November 2 during the team's Week 9 bye week.{{cite web|author=Mortensen, Chris and Adam Schefter |date=November 2, 2009 |title= Browns GM Kokinis ousted|work=ESPN|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=4616312|accessdate=November 2, 2009| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20091105035109/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=4616312| archivedate= 5 November 2009 | deadurl= no}} The Browns played all of their home games at [[Cleveland Browns Stadium]] in [[Cleveland, Ohio]]. The Browns missed the playoffs for the seventh straight season, tying a record set between 1973–79. {{TOC limit|limit=4}} == Offseason == === Personnel changes === On December 29, 2008, the Cleveland Browns announced that the team had fired general manager [[Phil Savage]] and head coach [[Romeo Crennel]] after spending four seasons together in Cleveland.{{cite web|title=Browns announce changes |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9338 |work=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=December 29, 2008 |accessdate=April 26, 2009 |archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/5hgJSXQKM?url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9338 |archivedate=June 20, 2009 |deadurl=no |df= }} Crennel, who joined the Browns with Savage in 2005, left Cleveland with a record of 24–40 (.375) and an 0–8 record against the division rival [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. The team's best record under Crennel was 10–6 during the [[2007 Cleveland Browns season|2007 season]]. On January 7, 2009, the Browns announced that the team had found its replacement for Crennel and that it had reached a contractual agreement with former [[New York Jets]] head coach [[Eric Mangini]], who was fired after three seasons in New York.{{cite web|title=Browns, Mangini reach agreement |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9357 |work=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=January 7, 2009 |accessdate=April 26, 2009 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090218075525/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9357 |archivedate=February 18, 2009 }} Mangini, who joined the Jets in 2006, left New York with a record of 23–25 (.479), including a 10–6 record and a playoff appearance in his [[2006 New York Jets season|first season]]. On January 14, the Browns announced that Mangini had named his coordinators: [[Brian Daboll]] was hired as the offensive coordinator; [[Rob Ryan]] as the defensive coordinator; and [[Brad Seely]] as the special teams coordinator and assistant head coach.{{cite web|author=Jackson, Zac |date=January 22, 2009 |title=Mangini names coordinators |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9371 |work=ClevelandBrowns.com |accessdate=April 26, 2009 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090429101119/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9371 |archivedate=April 29, 2009 |deadurl=yes }} Daboll was most recently the quarterbacks coach for the Jets from 2007–2008; Ryan was the defensive coordinator for the [[Oakland Raiders]] from 2004–2008; and Seely was the special teams coach for the [[New England Patriots]] from 1999–2008. All three worked with Mangini from 2000–2003 as members of New England. Daboll, Ryan, and Seely replace [[Rob Chudzinski]], [[Mel Tucker]], and [[Ted Daisher]], respectively. On January 22, the Browns hired five assistant coaches: [[Bryan Cox]] was hired as the defensive line coach; Andy Dickerson as the defensive quality control coach; [[Jerome Henderson]] as the defensive backs coach; [[Rick Lyle]] as an assistant strength-and-conditioning coach; and [[Carl Smith (American football)|Carl Smith]] as the quarterbacks coach.{{cite web|author=Jackson, Zac |date=January 22, 2009 |title=Browns announce hiring of 5 assistants |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9384 |work=ClevelandBrowns.com |accessdate=April 26, 2009 }}{{dead link|date=April 2017|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Cox, Dickerson, Henderson, and Lyle spent the past three seasons with Mangini in New York. Smith was the Browns' quarterbacks coach from 2001–2003 and was most recently the offensive coordinator for the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] from 2005–2006. On January 25, the Browns hired former [[Baltimore Ravens]] director of pro personnel [[George Kokinis]] as general manager.{{cite web|title=Browns announce hiring of Kokinis |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9385 |work=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=January 25, 2009 |accessdate=April 26, 2009 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090414054503/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9385 |archivedate=April 14, 2009 |deadurl=yes }} Kokinis spent five seasons in the Browns' scouting department from 1991–1995, and after the team moved to Baltimore, he was a member of the Ravens' scouting department from 1996–1999. He was the Ravens' assistant director of pro personnel from 2000–2002 and was the director of pro personnel from 2003–2008. On February 4, the Browns hired three more assistant coaches: [[Alan DeGennaro]] was hired as an assistant strength-and-conditioning coach; [[Tom Myslinski]] as the strength-and-conditioning coach; and George Warhop as the offensive line coach.{{cite web|title=Browns name 3 coaches |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9397 |work=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=February 4, 2009 |accessdate=April 26, 2009 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090414170254/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9397 |archivedate=April 14, 2009 |deadurl=yes }} On February 11, the |archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/5hgJWAujb?url=http://www.ohio.com/sports/zips/48112542.html |archivedate=June 20, 2009 |deadurl=no |df= }} |} === Legal troubles for WR Stallworth === On March 14, Browns wide receiver [[Donté Stallworth]] was involved in a fatal accident in which he struck and killed pedestrian Mario Reyes with his car in the early morning in [[Miami]], [[Florida]].{{cite web|author=Associated Press|date=March 14, 2009|title=Stallworth involved in fatal accident|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=3980182|work=ESPN.com|accessdate=April 27, 2009| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20090317094141/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=3980182| archivedate= 17 March 2009 | deadurl= no}} Stallworth then stopped his vehicle and called 9–1–1. Reports showed that Stallworth was driving under the influence; his blood-alcohol level was 0.12%, above Florida's legal limit of 0.08%.{{cite web|author=Associated Press|date=April 2, 2009|title=Stallworth charged in man's death|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=4033632|work=ESPN.com|accessdate=April 27, 2009| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20090413151241/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=4033632| archivedate= 13 April 2009 | deadurl= no}} He was charged with DUI manslaughter and a warrant was issued for his arrest on April 1 and he surrendered to police on April 2. On June 16, Stallworth pleaded guilty. He was sentenced to 30 days in prison, two years' house arrest, and eight years probation.{{cite web|author=Anderson, Curt |date=June 16, 2009 |title=WR Stallworth pleads guilty, gets 30 days in jail |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/news;_ylt=Ag03K74khn3mP_D7G55jtBU5nYcB?slug=ap-stallworth-pedestriankilled&prov=ap&type=lgns |accessdate=June 16, 2009 |archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/5hgJVlEno?url=http://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/news?slug%3Dap-stallworth-pedestriankilled%26prov%3Dap%26type%3Dlgns |archivedate=June 20, 2009 |deadurl=no |df= }} Many believed that the sentence Stallworth received was too lenient{{Citation needed|date=June 2009}} as he could have served up to 15 years in jail. Stallworth also reached an undisclosed financial settlement with the victim's family. On June 18, the NFL suspended Stallworth indefinitely{{cite news|author=Smith, Joe |date=June 18, 2009 |title=Browns WR Stallworth suspended indefinitely by NFL |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/news;_ylt=ArPmU93kTVuOTqFy0pAd0GY5nYcB?slug=ap-browns-stallworthsuspended&prov=ap&type=lgns |agency=Associated Press |accessdate=June 18, 2009}} On August 13, the NFL officially suspended Stallworth for the entire 2009 season, and made plans to reinstate him after the Super Bowl. === Uniform changes === In 2009, the Cleveland Browns wore brown pants for games in which they wear white jerseys. These were worn in the 2008 pre-season. After trading field goals in the first quarter, RB [[Adrian Peterson]] scored the first touchdown of the game, giving Minnesota a 10–3 lead. But K [[Phil Dawson]] kicked his second field goal and WR Josh Cribbs returned a punt for a touchdown and the Browns took a 13–10 lead into halftime. However, the second half was controlled completely by the Vikings, with QB [[Brett Favre]] connecting with WR [[Percy Harvin]] for Favre's first touchdown pass as a Viking. In the 4th quarter, QB [[Brady Quinn]] completed a touchdown pass to TE [[Robert Royal]], the first touchdown by Cleveland's offense since the 4th quarter of Week 11 in 2008, ending a span of 416 offensive plays without a touchdown. With the loss, Cleveland fell to 0–1. ==== Week 2: at Denver Broncos ==== {{Americanfootballbox| |Road=Browns |R1=6||R2=0||R3=0||R4=0||RT=6 |Home='''Broncos''' |H1=7||H2=3||H3=3||H4=14||HT=27 |stadium= [[Invesco Field at Mile High]], [[Denver, Colorado]] |time= 4:15 pm [[North American Eastern Time Zone|EDT]]/2:15 pm [[Mountain Time Zone|MDT]] |weather= 82 °F (Partly Cloudy) |attendance= 73,931 |referee= [[Pete Morelli]] |TV=[[NFL on CBS]] |TVAnnouncers= [[Bill Macatee]] & [[Steve Beuerlein]] |titlestyle=background-color: #DE6108; color: white; |scoring= '''First quarter''' * 12:25 CLE – [[Phil Dawson|Dawson]] 22-yard field goal 3–0 CLE * 8:07 DEN – [[Tony Scheffler|Scheffler]] 2-yard pass from [[Kyle Orton|Orton]] ([[Matt Prater|Prater]] kick) 7–3 DEN * 1:53 CLE – Dawson 47-yard field goal 7–6 DEN '''Second quarter''' * 11:45 DEN – Prater 23-yard field goal 10–6 DEN '''Third quarter''' * 10:43 DEN – Prater 38-yard field goal 13–6 DEN '''Fourth quarter''' * 12:22 DEN – [[Peyton Hillis|Hillis]] 2-yard run (Prater kick) 20–6 DEN * 8:35 DEN – [[Correll Buckhalter|Buckhalter]] 45-yard run (Prater kick) 27–6 DEN }} Hoping to rebound from their home loss to the Vikings, the Browns flew to [[Invesco Field at Mile High]] for a Week 2 duel with the [[Denver Broncos]]. After recovering a fumble on the opening kickoff, the Browns started with a short field but couldn't capitalize, settling for a 22-yard field goal by kicker [[Phil Dawson]]. Broncos quarterback [[Kyle Orton]] would complete a 2-yard touchdown pass to tight end [[Tony Scheffler]] for the game's first touchdown, and after a 47-yard field goal by Cleveland, the game was 7–6 after the first quarter. However, Cleveland's offensive struggles continued. Meanwhile, in the second and third quarter, kicker [[Matt Prater]] gave Denver a 23-yard and a 38-yard field goal. Afterwards, in the fourth quarter, the Broncos took control with touchdown runs by [[Peyton Hillis]] and [[Correll Buckhalter]]. With the loss, the Browns fell to 0–2. ==== Week 3: at Baltimore Ravens ==== {{Americanfootballbox| |Road=Browns |R1=0||R2=0||R3=0||R4=3||RT=3 |Home='''Ravens''' |H1=10||H2=10||H3=7||H4=7||HT=34 |stadium= [[M&T Bank Stadium]], [[Baltimore, Maryland]] |time= 1:00 pm [[North American Eastern Time Zone|EDT]] |weather= 72 °F (Partly Cloudy) |attendance= 70,950 |referee= [[Terry McAulay]] |TV=[[NFL on CBS|CBS]] |TVAnnouncers= [[Gus Johnson (sportscaster)|Gus Johnson]] & [[Steve Tasker]] |titlestyle=background-color: #DE6108; color: white; |scoring= '''First quarter''' * 10:19 BAL – [[Willis McGahee|McGahee]] 7-yard run ([[Steven Hauschka|Hauschka]] kick) 7–0 BAL * 1:21 BAL – Hauschka 36-yard field goal 10–0 BAL '''Second quarter''' * 5:42 BAL – Hauschka 33-yard field goal 13–0 BAL * 1:01 BAL – McGahee 15-yard run (Hauschka kick) 20–0 BAL '''Third quarter''' * 7:38 BAL – [[Ray Rice|Rice]] 9-yard run (Hauschka kick) 27–0 BAL '''Fourth quarter''' * 15:00 CLE – [[Billy Cundiff|Cundiff]] 29-yard field goal 27–3 BAL * 8:18 BAL – [[Derrick Mason|Mason]] 72-yard pass from [[Joe Flacco|Flacco]] (Hauschka kick) 34–3 BAL }} Hoping to rebound from their road loss to the Broncos, the Browns flew to [[M&T Bank Stadium]] for a Week 3 AFC North duel with the [[Baltimore Ravens]]. Cleveland would trail early in the first quarter as Ravens running back [[Willis McGahee]] got a 7-yard touchdown run, followed by kicker [[Steven Hauschka]] getting a 36-yard field goal. The Browns' deficit would increase in the second quarter as Hauschka nailed a 33-yard field goal, while McGahee got a 15-yard touchdown run. In the third quarter, things continued to get worse for the Browns as running back [[Ray Rice]] got a 9-yard touchdown run. In the fourth quarter, Cleveland would manage to get on the board as kicker [[Billy Cundiff]] made a 29-yard field goal. Afterwards, Baltimore closed out the game as quarterback [[Joe Flacco]] completed a 72-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver [[Derrick Mason]]. With the loss, the Browns fell to 0–3. Starting quarterback [[Brady Quinn]] (6 of 8, 34 yards, 1 INT) was benched after a dismal first half performance, while [[Derek Anderson (American football)|Derek Anderson]] (11 of 19, 92 yards, 3 INTs) did not perform much better. ==== Week 4: vs. Cincinnati Bengals ==== {{Americanfootballbox| |Road='''Bengals''' |R1=7||R2=7||R3=0||R4=6||R5=3||RT=23 |Home=Browns |H1=0||H2=7||H3=7||H4=6||H5=0||HT=20 |stadium= [[Cleveland Browns Stadium]], [[Cleveland, Ohio]] |time= 1:00 pm [[North American Eastern Time Zone|EDT]] |weather= 58 °F (Cloudy) |attendance= 69,844 |referee= [[Scott Green (American football official)|Scott Green]] |TV=[[NFL on CBS|CBS]] |TVAnnouncers= [[Ian Eagle]] & [[Rich Gannon]] |titlestyle=background-color: #DE6108; color: white; |scoring= '''First quarter''' * 0:40 CIN – [[Chad Ochocinco|Ochocinco]] 5-yard pass from [[Carson Palmer|Palmer]] ([[Shayne Graham|Graham]] kick) 7–0 CIN '''Second quarter''' * 14:26 CIN – [[Robert Geathers|Geathers]] 75-yard fumble return (Graham kick) 14–0 CIN * 1:33 CLE – [[Steve Heiden|Heiden]] 1-yard pass from [[Derek Anderson (American football)|Anderson]] ([[Billy Cundiff|Cundiff]] kick) 14–7 CIN '''Third quarter''' * 1:44 CLE – Anderson 1-yard run (Cundiff kick) 14–14 '''Fourth quarter''' * 15:00 CLE – Cundiff 26-yard field goal 17–14 CLE * 6:38 CLE – Cundiff 31-yard field goal 20–14 CLE * 2:02 CIN – Ochocinco 2-yard pass from Palmer 20–20 '''Overtime''' * 0:07 CIN – Graham 31-yard field goal 23–20 CIN }} Still looking for their first win of the season, the Browns went home for a Week 4 AFC North duel with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in Round 1 of 2009's [[Battle of Ohio (NFL)|Battle of Ohio]]. Due to quarterback [[Brady Quinn]]'s poor performance in the season thus far, head coach [[Eric Mangini]] named quarterback [[Derek Anderson (American football)|Derek Anderson]] the starter. Cleveland would trail early in the first quarter as Bengals quarterback [[Carson Palmer]] completed a 5-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver [[Chad Ochocinco]]. The Browns would continue to struggle in the second quarter as defensive end [[Robert Geathers]] returned a fumble 75 yards for a touchdown. Cleveland would respond with Anderson completing a 1-yard touchdown pass to tight end [[Steve Heiden]]. The Browns would tie the game in the third quarter with Anderson's 1-yard touchdown run. Afterwards, Cleveland would take the lead in the fourth quarter with a 26-yard and a 31-yard field goal from kicker [[Billy Cundiff]]. However, Cincinnati answered with Palmer hooking up with Ochocinco again on a 2-yard touchdown run (with a blocked PAT). In overtime, both teams went back and forth with their possessions. In the end, the Bengals emerged victorious with kicker [[Shayne Graham]] kicking the game-winning 31-yard field goal. With the loss, the Browns fell to 0–4. ==== WR Edwards traded ==== [[File:20090806 Braylon Edwards.jpg|upright|thumb|Edwards (shown in 2009 training camp) was traded to the [[New York Jets]] during the season.]] On October 7, the Browns traded WR [[Braylon Edwards]] to the [[New York Jets]] for WR [[Chansi Stuckey]], LB [[Jason Trusnik]], and third- and fifth- round selections in the [[2010 NFL Draft]]. The third-round selection would have become a second-round selection based on Edwards met certain performance criteria with the Jets this season, but he did not meet those criteria.{{cite web|author=McMorrow, Kyle |date=October 7, 2009 |title= Cleveland Deals Troubled Wide Receiver Braylon Edwards to New York Jets|work=Bleacher Report|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/267934-cleavland-deals-troubled-wide-receiver-to-the-new-york-jets |accessdate=October 7, 2009}} ==== Week 5: at Buffalo Bills ==== {{Americanfootballbox| |Road='''Browns''' |R1=0||R2=3||R3=0||R4=3||RT=0 |Home=Bills |H1=0||H2=0||H3=3||H4=0||HT=0 |stadium= [[Ralph Wilson Stadium]], [[Orchard Park (town), New York|Orchard Park, New York]] |time= 1:00 pm [[North American Eastern Time Zone|EDT]] |weather= 47 °F (Mostly Sunny) |attendance= 70,526 |referee= [[Jerome Boger]] |TV=[[NFL on CBS|CBS]] |TVAnnouncers= [[Don Criqui]] & [[Randy Cross]] |titlestyle=background-color: #DE6108; color: white; |scoring= '''Second quarter''' * 7:31 CLE – [[Billy Cundiff|Cundiff]] 24-yard field goal 3–0 CLE '''Third quarter''' * 10:15 BUF – [[Rian Lindell|Lindell]] 36-yard field goal 3–3 '''Fourth quarter''' * 0:26 CLE – Cundiff 18-yard field goal 6–3 CLE }} After a heartbreaking loss to the Bengals, the Browns headed to Buffalo, the site of their last win in Week 11 of the 2008 season, and trying to avoid tying a franchise record 11 straight losses. In very windy conditions, the Browns' hero was punter [[Dave Zastudil]] who pinned the Bills within their 5-yard line 3 times. After trading field goals in the 2nd and 3rd quarters, the Browns recovered a fumble on a punt return by WR [[Roscoe Parrish]], and kicker [[Billy Cundiff]] secured the victory with a short field goal. The Browns won despite QB [[Derek Anderson (American football)|Derek Anderson]] completing only 2 of 17 passes (11.8%) for 23 yards, setting a record for lowest completion percentage in a win since the [[AFL-NFL merger]]. This also marked [[Eric Mangini]]'s first win as head coach of the Browns. With the win, the Browns improved to 1–4. Zastudil was named the AFC special teams player of the week.[http://www.woio.com/global/story.asp?s=11314816 Dave Zastudil Named AFC Player Of The Week]{{dead link|date=September 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ==== Week 6: at Pittsburgh Steelers ==== {{Americanfootballbox| |Road=Browns |R1=0||R2=7||R3=7||R4=0||RT=14 |Home='''Steelers''' |H1=0||H2=17||H3=7||H4=3||HT=27 |stadium= [[Heinz Field]], [[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania]] |time= 1:00 pm [[North American Eastern Time Zone|EDT]] |weather= 41 °F (Cloudy) |attendance= 64,398 |referee= [[Walt Anderson (American football)|Walt Anderson]] |TV=[[NFL on CBS|CBS]] |TVAnnouncers= [[Kevin Harlan]] & [[Solomon Wilcots]] |titlestyle=background-color: #DE6108; color: white; |scoring= '''Second quarter''' * 11:35 PIT – [[Heath Miller|Miller]] 8-yard pass from [[Ben Roethlisberger|Roethlisberger]] ([[Jeff Reed (American football)|Reed]] kick) 7–0 PIT * 4:38 PIT – [[Hines Ward|Ward]] 52-yard pass from Roethlisberger (Reed kick) 14–0 PIT * 4:28 CLE – [[Josh Cribbs|Cribbs]] 98-yard kickoff return ([[Billy Cundiff|Cundiff]] kick) 14–7 PIT * 0:10 PIT – Reed 32-yard field goal 17–7 PIT '''Third quarter''' * 11:43 CLE – [[Lawrence Vickers|Vickers]] 1-yard pass from [[Derek Anderson (American football)|Anderson]] (Cundiff kick) 17–14 PIT * 8:39 PIT – [[Rashard Mendenhall|Mendenhall]] 2-yard run (Reed kick) 24–14 PIT '''Fourth quarter''' * 5:47 PIT – Reed 39-yard field goal 27–14 PIT }} After securing their first win of the season, the Browns went on the road to take on their archrival [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. The Browns came into the game having lost their last 11 games against the Steelers. The Steelers struck first with two touchdown passes from [[Ben Roethlisberger]] in the 2nd quarter. [[Josh Cribbs]] ran a kickoff back 98 yards for a touchdown, and got the Browns within 7. However, the Browns could never close the gap, and fell to the Steelers, 27–14. With the loss, the Browns fell to 1–5. ==== Week 7: vs. Green Bay Packers ==== {{Americanfootballbox| |Road='''Packers''' |R1=0||R2=21||R3=3||R4=7||RT= |Home=Browns |H1=0||H2=3||H3=0||H4=0||HT= |stadium= [[Cleveland Browns Stadium]], [[Cleveland, Ohio]] |time= 1:00 pm [[North American Eastern Time Zone|EDT]] |weather= 50 °F (Sunny) |attendance= 69,797 |referee= [[Don Carey (official)|Don Carey]] |TV=[[NFL on Fox|Fox]] |TVAnnouncers= [[Ron Pitts]] & [[John Lynch (American football)|John Lynch]] |titlestyle=background-color: #DE6108; color: white; |scoring= '''Second quarter''' * 14:58 CLE – [[Billy Cundiff|Cundiff]] 22-yard field goal 3–0 CLE * 12:11 GB – [[Spencer Havner|Havner]] 45-yard pass from [[Aaron Rodgers|Rodgers]] ([[Mason Crosby|Crosby]] kick) 7–3 GB * 7:01 GB – [[Donald Driver|Driver]] 71-yard pass from Rodgers (Crosby kick) 14–3 GB * 1:56 GB – [[Ryan Grant|Grant]] 1-yard run (Crosby kick) 21–3 GB '''Third quarter''' * 3:34 GB – Crosby 18-yard field goal 24–3 GB '''Fourth quarter''' * 9:42 GB – [[James Jones (wide receiver)|Jones]] 5-yard pass from Rodgers (Crosby kick) 31–3 GB }} Hoping to rebound from their road loss to the Steelers, the Browns went home for a Week 7 interconference duel with the [[Green Bay Packers]]. After a scoreless first quarter, Cleveland began the second quarter with kicker [[Billy Cundiff]]'s 22-yard field goal. However, the Packers would take charge with quarterback [[Aaron Rodgers]] completing a 45-yard touchdown pass to tight end [[Spencer Havner]] and a 71-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver [[Donald Driver]], followed by a 1-yard touchdown run by running back [[Ryan Grant]]. Afterwards, Green Bay pulled away in the second half with kicker [[Mason Crosby]] booting an 18-yard field goal in the third quarter and Rodgers finding wide receiver [[James Jones (wide receiver)|James Jones]] on a 5-yard touchdown pass. With the loss, the Browns stumbled to 1–6. ==== Week 8: at Chicago Bears ==== {{Americanfootballbox| |Road=Browns |R1=0||R2=0||R3=6||R4=0||RT=6 |Home='''Bears''' |H1=6||H2=10||H3=7||H4=7||HT=30 |stadium= [[Soldier Field]], [[Chicago, Illinois]] |time= 1:00 pm [[North American Eastern Time Zone|EST]]/12:00 pm [[North American Central Time Zone|CST]] |weather= 50 °F (Mostly Cloudy) |attendance= 62,262 |referee= [[Alberto Riveron]] |TV=[[NFL on CBS|CBS]] |TVAnnouncers= [[Kevin Harlan]] & [[Solomon Wilcots]] |titlestyle=background-color: #DE6108; color: white; |scoring= '''First quarter''' * 2:25 CHI – [[Robbie Gould|Gould]] 37-yard field goal 3–0 CHI * 1:18 CHI – Gould 29-yard field goal 6–0 CHI '''Second quarter''' * 8:48 CHI – Gould 32-yard field goal 9–0 CHI * 2:00 CHI – [[Matt Forté|Forté]] 1-yard run (Gould kick) 16–0 CHI '''Third quarter''' * 10:35 CLE – [[Derek Anderson (American football)|Anderson]] 1-yard run 16–6 CHI * 1:49 CHI – Forté 10-yard run (Gould kick) 23–6 CHI '''Fourth quarter''' * 3:25 CHI – [[Charles Tillman|Tillman]] 21-yard interception return (Gould kick) 30–6 CHI }} Trying to snap a two-game losing streak, the Browns flew to [[Soldier Field]] for a Week 8 interconference duel with the [[Chicago Bears]]. The Browns' defense held up well early, limiting the Bears to three field goals by kicker [[Robbie Gould]] (a 37-yard & a 29-yard in the first quarter and a 32-yard in the second). However, the Browns could not manage to get on the board and Chicago RB [[Matt Forté]] scored on a 1-yard run, putting the Browns down 16 at the half. The Browns struck first in the third quarter on a one-yard run by QB [[Derek Anderson (American football)|Derek Anderson]], but the PAT was blocked. Forté scored again in the third with a 10-yard touchdown run and the Bears put the Browns away with a 21-yard interception return for a touchdown by CB [[Charles Tillman]] in the fourth quarter. Late in the fourth, Derek Anderson was benched for [[Brady Quinn]] after going 6 of 17 (35.2%) for 76 yards and 2 interceptions. With the loss, the Browns went into their bye week at 1–7. ==== GM Kokinis fired ==== On November 2, the Browns fired general manager [[George Kokinis]] after getting off to a disappointing 1–7 start. The Browns' statement said that Kokinis "is no longer actively involved with the organization." Owner [[Randy Lerner]] reportedly asked for his resignation, and when Kokinis refused, sought a dismissal "for cause." Head coach [[Eric Mangini]] was told by Lerner that his job was safe for the moment. ==== Week 10: vs. Baltimore Ravens ==== {{Americanfootballbox| |Road='''Ravens''' |R1=0||R2=0||R3=16||R4=0||RT=16 |Home=Browns |H1=0||H2=0||H3=0||H4=0||HT=0 |stadium= [[Cleveland Browns Stadium]], [[Cleveland, Ohio]] |time= 8:30 pm [[North American Eastern Time Zone|EST]] |weather= 46 °F (Chilly) |attendance= 69,023 |referee= [[Carl Cheffers]] |TV=[[Monday Night Football|ESPN]] |TVAnnouncers= [[Mike Tirico]], [[Ron Jaworski]], [[Jon Gruden]] & [[Michele Tafoya]] |titlestyle=background-color: #DE6108; color: white; |scoring= '''Third quarter''' * 12:35 BAL – [[Ray Rice|Rice]] 13-yard run ([[Steven Hauschka|Hauschka]] kick) 7–0 BAL * 12:20 BAL – [[Dawan Landry|Landry]] 48-yard interception return 13–0 BAL * 7:25 BAL – Hauschka 44-yard field goal 16–0 BAL }} The Browns came out of their bye week with [[Brady Quinn]] as the starting quarterback again and looking to turn around their disappointing season. They hosted the [[Baltimore Ravens]] on [[Monday Night Football]]. Both teams played a scoreless first half, the first scoreless half in the NFL this season and only the ninth ever in 620 Monday Night Football games. The Ravens took over in the third with two touchdowns in 15 seconds (a 13-yard touchdown run from running back [[Ray Rice]] and safety [[Dawan Landry]]'s 48-yard interception return for a touchdown). Kicker [[Steven Hauschka]] would add a 44-yard field goal, and the Browns could not score. This was the Browns' first shutout of the year. With the loss, the Browns fell to 1–8. ==== Week 11: at Detroit Lions ==== {{Americanfootballbox| |Road=Browns |R1=24||R2=3||R3=2||R4=8||RT=37 |Home='''Lions''' |H1=10||H2=14||H3=7||H4=7||HT=38 |stadium= [[Ford Field]], [[Detroit, Michigan]] |time= 1:00 pm [[North American Eastern Time Zone|EST]] |weather= None (Domed Stadium) |attendance= 43,170 |referee= [[Terry McAulay]] |TV=[[NFL on CBS|CBS]] |TVAnnouncers= [[Don Criqui]] & [[Randy Cross]] |titlestyle=background-color: #DE6108; color: white; |scoring= '''First quarter''' * 11:34 CLE – [[Phil Dawson|Dawson]] 44-yard field goal 3–0 CLE * 9:17 DET – [[Jason Hanson|Hanson]] 31-yard field goal 3–3 * 9:05 CLE – [[Mohamed Massaquoi|Massaquoi]] 59-yard pass from [[Brady Quinn|Quinn]] (Dawson kick) 10–3 CLE * 4:10 CLE – [[Chansi Stuckey|Stuckey]] 40-yard pass from Quinn (Dawson kick) 17–3 CLE * 2:57 CLE – [[Josh Cribbs|Cribbs]] 4-yard pass from Quinn 24–3 CLE * 0:37 DET – [[Aaron Brown (running back)|Brown]] 26-yard pass from [[Matthew Stafford|Stafford]] (Hanson kick) 24–10 CLE '''Second quarter''' * 11:52 DET – [[Kevin Smith (running back)|Smith]] 25-yard pass from Stafford (Hanson kick) 24–17 CLE * 5:12 DET – [[Calvin Johnson (American football)|Johnson]] 75-yard pass from Stafford (Hanson kick) 24–24 * 0:06 CLE – Dawson 29-yard field goal 27–24 CLE '''Third quarter''' * 2:52 DET – [[Will Heller|Heller]] 1-yard pass from Stafford (Hanson kick) 31–27 DET * 0:47 CLE – intentional grounding in the end zone 31–29 DET '''Fourth quarter''' * 5:51 CLE – [[Michael Gaines|Gaines]] 2-yard pass from Quinn ([[Jamal Lewis|Lewis]] run) 37–31 CLE * 0:00 DET – [[Brandon Pettigrew|Pettigrew]] 1-yard pass from Stafford (Hanson kick) 38–37 DET }} Looking to snap a four-game losing streak, the 1–8 Browns flew to [[Ford Field]] for a Week 11 interconference duel with the 1–8 [[Detroit Lions]]. Both teams began the game with field goals, as Cleveland kicker [[Phil Dawson]] made a 44-yard field goal while Lions kicker [[Jason Hanson]] got a 31-yard field goal. Afterwards, the Browns' offense exploded as quarterback [[Brady Quinn]] completed a 59-yard touchdown pass to rookie wide receiver [[Mohamed Massaquoi]], a 40-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver [[Chansi Stuckey]], and a 4-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Josh Cribbs. Detroit would answer with quarterback [[Matthew Stafford]] completing a 26-yard touchdown pass to running back [[Aaron Brown (running back)|Aaron Brown]]. The Lions would tie the game in the second quarter as Stafford hooked up with running back [[Kevin Smith (running back)|Kevin Smith]] on a 25-yard touchdown pass, followed by a 75-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver [[Calvin Johnson (American football)|Calvin Johnson]]. Afterwards, Cleveland would end the half with Dawson nailing a 29-yard field goal. Detroit would take the lead in the third quarter with Stafford's 1-yard touchdown pass to tight end [[Will Heller]], the Browns would pick up a safety after Stafford was called for intentional grounding from his own end zone. In the fourth quarter, Cleveland regained the lead with Quinn's 2-yard touchdown pass to tight end [[Michael Gaines]] (followed by running back [[Jamal Lewis]] getting a 2-point conversion run). The Lions would take over, and with no time left, Browns safety [[Brodney Pool]] intercepted the ball. However, cornerback [[Hank Poteat]] was flagged for pass interference in the end zone. Since the game cannot end on a defensive penalty, Detroit was given one un-timed down from the Browns' 1-yard line and Stafford completed the game-winning touchdown pass to tight end [[Brandon Pettigrew]]. With the loss in the 1–8 battle, Cleveland fell to 1–9 assuring them that they would finish last in their division. ==== Week 12: at Cincinnati Bengals ==== {{Americanfootballbox| |Road=Browns |R1=0||R2=0||R3=7||R4=0||RT=7 |Home='''Bengals''' |H1=3||H2=10||H3=3||H4=0||HT=16 |stadium= [[Paul Brown Stadium]], [[Cincinnati, Ohio]] |time= 1:00 pm [[North American Eastern Time Zone|EST]] |weather= 59 °F (Partly Cloudy) |attendance= 64,553 |referee= [[Mike Carey (American football)|Mike Carey]] |TV=[[NFL on CBS|CBS]] |TVAnnouncers= [[Ian Eagle]] & [[Rich Gannon]] |titlestyle=background-color: #DE6108; color: white; |scoring= '''First quarter''' * 3:11 CIN – [[Shayne Graham|Graham]] 37-yard field goal 3–0 CIN '''Second quarter''' * 1:18 CIN – [[J. P. The Browns struck first with an 11-yard touchdown reception by [[Mohamed Massaquoi]]. The Chargers took the lead back in the first on a field goal by [[Nate Kaeding]] and a long touchdown reception by [[Mike Tolbert]]. San Diego scored 17 more in the second and third, seemingly putting the game out of reach. The Browns managed to get within a touchdown but their comeback ran out of time. With the loss, the Browns fell to 1–11. ==== Week 14: vs. Pittsburgh Steelers ==== {{Americanfootballbox| |Road=Steelers |R1=0||R2=3||R3=3||R4=0||RT=6 |Home='''Browns''' |H1=3||H2=10||H3=0||H4=0||HT=13 |stadium= [[Cleveland Browns Stadium]], [[Cleveland, Ohio]] |time= 8:20 pm [[North American Eastern Time Zone|EST]] |weather= 6 °F (Clear, very Windy, −15 °F wind chill) |attendance= 69,009 |referee= [[Ron Winter]] |TV=[[NFL Network]] |TVAnnouncers= [[Bob Papa]] & [[Matt Millen]] |titlestyle=background-color: #DE6108; color: white; |scoring= '''First quarter''' * 3:47 CLE – [[Phil Dawson|Dawson]] 29-yard field goal 3–0 CLE '''Second quarter''' * 7:20 CLE – Dawson 29-yard field goal 6–0 CLE * 0:41 CLE – [[Chris Jennings (gridiron football)|Jennings]] 10-yard run (Dawson kick) 13–0 CLE * 0:00 PIT – [[Jeff Reed (American football)|Reed]] 27-yard field goal 13–3 CLE '''Third quarter''' * 0:08 PIT – Reed 42-yard field goal 13–6 CLE }} The Browns hosted the rival [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] on a night with subzero wind chills for a Week 14 duel. In windy conditions, [[Phil Dawson]] hit a pair of 29-yard field goals, and [[Chris Jennings (gridiron football)|Chris Jennings]] had a 10-yard touchdown run to put the Browns up 13. [[Jeff Reed (American football)|Jeff Reed]] nailed a field goal before the half to draw the Steelers within 10, and hit another in the third to bring them within a touchdown. However, a scoreless fourth by both teams led the Browns to their first win against the Steelers since 2003, and the Browns became only the fourth team in NFL history to be at least 10 games under .500 and defeat the defending [[Super Bowl]] champions. With the win, the Browns improved to 2–11, snapped a twelve-game losing streak against the Steelers and won against them for the first time since 2003 when they defeated the team 33–13 in Pittsburgh. The team also won their first home game since an October 2008 victory, interestingly against then-defending [[Super Bowl XLII|Super Bowl champion]] [[New York Giants]]. KR Josh Cribbs was named AFC Special Teams Player of the Week.{{cite web|author=Cabot, Mary Kay |date=December 16, 2009 |title= Browns' Josh Cribbs named AFC Special Teams Player of the Week|work=The Plain Dealer|url=http://www.cleveland.com/browns/index.ssf/2009/12/cleveland_browns_josh_cribbs_n.html|accessdate=December 20, 2009}} ==== Week 15: at Kansas City Chiefs ==== {{Americanfootballbox| |Road='''Browns''' |R1=10||R2=10||R3=7||R4=14||RT=41 |Home=Chiefs |H1=3||H2=21||H3=0||H4=10||HT=34 |stadium= [[Arrowhead Stadium]], [[Kansas City, Missouri]] |time= 1:00 pm [[North American Eastern Time Zone|EST]]/12:00 pm [[Central Time Zone|CST]] |weather= 39 °F (Partly Sunny) |attendance= 53,315 |referee= [[Gene Steratore]] |TV=[[CBS]] |TVAnnouncers= [[Ian Eagle]] & [[Rich Gannon]] |titlestyle=background-color: #DE6108; color: white; |scoring= '''First quarter''' * 10:18 CLE – [[Phil Dawson|Dawson]] 47-yard field goal 3–0 CLE * 4:15 KC – [[Ryan Succop|Succop]] 30-yard field goal 3–3 * 4:12 CLE – [[Josh Cribbs|Cribbs]] 100-yard kickoff return (Dawson kick) 10–3 CLE '''Second quarter''' * 12:36 CLE – Dawson 30-yard field goal 13–3 CLE * 10:09 KC – [[Chris Chambers|Chambers]] 9-yard pass from [[Matt Cassel|Cassel]] (Succop kick) 13–10 CLE * 4:19 KC – [[Jamaal Charles|Charles]] 47-yard run (Succop kick) 17–13 KC * 2:49 KC – [[Andy Studebaker|Studebaker]] fumble recovery in the end zone (Succop kick) 24–13 KC * 2:44 CLE – Cribbs 103-yard kickoff return (Dawson kick) 24–20 KC '''Third quarter''' * 13:27 CLE – [[Jerome Harrison|Harrison]] 71-yard run (Dawson kick) 27–24 CLE '''Fourth quarter''' * 12:14 CLE – Harrison 8-yard run (Dawson kick) 34–24 CLE * 8:12 KC – Succop 27-yard field goal 34–27 CLE * 2:26 KC – [[Mark Bradley|Bradley]] 12-yard pass from Cassel (Succop kick) 34–34 * 0:52 CLE – Harrison 28-yard run (Dawson kick) 41–34 CLE }} The Browns headed into Kansas City for their last road game of the year to take on the Chiefs in Week 15. The Browns and Chiefs traded field goals in the first quarter, and then Josh Cribbs returned the ensuing kickoff 100 yards for a touchdown, setting an NFL record with his 7th kickoff return for a touchdown. After another [[Phil Dawson]] field goal in the second, the Chiefs scored three straight touchdowns to take a 24–13 lead. However, Cribbs again ran a kickoff back for a touchdown, this time for 103 yards and extending his NFL record to eight kickoff return touchdowns. In the second half, [[Jerome Harrison]] rushed for three touchdowns and amassed a [[filibuster]]-proof majority of his 286 rushing yards. This set a Browns' rushing record for a single game, was the record for most rushing yards in the NFL this season, and was the third most rushing yards in a game in NFL history. [[Matt Cassel]]'s final desperation pass ricocheted off the cross bar, and the Browns defeated the Chiefs 41–34, with their highest point total of the season. With the win, the Browns improved to 3–11 and finished the season 2–6 on the road. Cribbs was named the AFC special teams player of the week for the second straight week.{{cite web|date=December 23, 2009|title= Joshua Cribbs named AFC Special Teams Player of the Week|work=Canton Rep|url=http://www.cantonrep.com/browns/x1689179479/Joshua-Cribbs-named-AFC-Special-Teams-Player-of-the-Week|accessdate=December 23, 2009}} {{Dead link|date=September 2010|bot=H3llBot}} ==== Holmgren hired as president ==== On December 21, [[Mike Holmgren]] was hired by the Browns to take over as their president. His duties will include personnel management, and he may hire a general manager to assist him. He also will have the power to replace [[Eric Mangini]] as head coach if he so chooses.{{cite web|author=Walker, James |date=December 21, 2009|title= Holmgren agrees to deal with Browns|work=espn.com|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=4762828|accessdate=December 21, 2009| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20091224093342/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=4762828| archivedate= 24 December 2009 | deadurl= no}} ==== Week 16: vs. Oakland Raiders ==== {{Americanfootballbox| |Road=Raiders |R1=3||R2=6||R3=0||R4=0||RT=9 |Home='''Browns''' |H1=10||H2=7||H3=3||H4=3||HT=23 |stadium= [[Cleveland Browns Stadium]], [[Cleveland, Ohio]] |time= 1:00 pm [[North American Eastern Time Zone|EST]] |weather= 34 °F (Cloudy) |attendance= 67,964 |referee= [[Jeff Triplette]] |TV=[[CBS]] |TVAnnouncers= [[Don Criqui]] & [[Randy Cross]] |titlestyle=background-color: #DE6108; color: white; |scoring= '''First quarter''' * 13:38 CLE – [[Jerome Harrison|Harrison]] 17-yard run ([[Phil Dawson|Dawson]] kick) 7–0 CLE * 8:22 CLE – Dawson 42-yard field goal 10–0 CLE * 2:53 OAK – [[Sebastian Janikowski|Janikowski]] 44-yard field goal 10–3 CLE '''Second quarter''' * 11:16 OAK – Janikowski 34-yard field goal 10–6 CLE * 0:21 CLE – [[Mohamed Massaquoi|Massaquoi]] 19-yard pass from [[Derek Anderson (American football)|Anderson]] (Dawson kick) 17–6 CLE * 0:00 OAK – Janikowski 61-yard field goal 17–9 CLE '''Third quarter''' * 11:11 CLE – Dawson 33-yard field goal 20–9 CLE '''Fourth quarter''' * 8:35 CLE – Dawson 34-yard field goal 23–9 CLE }} The Browns stayed home in Week 16 for a match with the [[Oakland Raiders]], trying to extend their 2-game winning streak. The Browns struck first with a 17-yard run by [[Jerome Harrison]] and a 42-yard field goal from [[Phil Dawson]]. Oakland kicker [[Sebastian Janikowski]] hit 3 field goals in the first half, including a 61 yarder to close out the half. However, the Browns led at halftime, 17–9. The Browns held the Raiders scoreless in the second half, and Dawson hit 2 more field goals to lead the Browns to a 23–9 victory, their third in a row. With the win, the Browns improved to 4–11. ==== Week 17: vs. Jacksonville Jaguars ==== {{Americanfootballbox| |Road=Jaguars |R1=3||R2=0||R3=0||R4=14||RT=17 |Home='''Browns''' |H1=3||H2=10||H3=7||H4=3||HT=23 |stadium= [[Cleveland Browns Stadium]], [[Cleveland, Ohio]] |time= 1:00 pm [[North American Eastern Time Zone|EST]] |weather= 16 °F (Snow Showers, −1 °F Wind Chill) |attendance= 66,935 |referee= [[Pete Morelli]] |TV=[[CBS]] |TVAnnouncers= [[Gus Johnson (sportscaster)|Gus Johnson]] & [[Steve Tasker]] |titlestyle=background-color: #DE6108; color: white; |scoring= '''First quarter''' * 11:00 CLE – [[Phil Dawson|Dawson]] 27-yard field goal 3–0 CLE * 2:23 JAC – [[Josh Scobee|Scobee]] 47-yard field goal 3–3 '''Second quarter''' * 3:58 CLE – [[Josh Cribbs|Cribbs]] 14-yard run (Dawson kick) 10–3 CLE * 1:46 CLE – Dawson 21-yard field goal 13–3 CLE '''Third quarter''' * 4:08 CLE – [[Jerome Harrison|Harrison]] 6-yard run (Dawson kick) 20–3 CLE '''Fourth quarter''' * 10:35 JAC – [[Zach Miller (American football b. 1984)|Miller]] 6-yard pass from [[David Garrard|Garrard]] (Scobee kick) 20–10 CLE * 2:20 CLE – Dawson 33-yard field goal 23–10 CLE * 0:00 JAC – Miller 15-yard pass from Garrard (Scobee kick) 23–17 CLE }} The Browns closed out their season at home with a contest against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], who came into the game with an outside chance of making the playoffs. Cleveland and Jacksonville traded field goals in the first quarter, but Josh Cribbs broke the tie in the second with a 14-yard touchdown run, and [[Phil Dawson]] added another field goal to give the Browns a 10-point lead at the half. In the third, [[Jerome Harrison]] added a 6-yard touchdown run to push the lead to 17. In the fourth, [[Zach Miller (American football b. 1984)|Zach Miller]] caught a 6-yard pass from [[David Garrard]] to close within 10, but Dawson added another field goal. On the final play of the game (and the season), Miller caught another touchdown pass from Garrard but it was not enough, and the Browns won 23–17. The Browns' 4-game winning streak was the longest since 1994. With the win, the Browns improved to finish the season at 5–11, a one-win improvement over the 2008 campaign. They finished 3–5 at home. ==== KR Cribbs honored ==== On January 6, WR/KR Josh Cribbs was named AFC special teams player of the month for December. During the month, Cribbs earned AFC special teams player of the week honors twice, and set an NFL record with eight career kickoff returns for touchdowns.{{cite news|author=Mike Florio |date=January 6, 2010 |title=Cribbs wins special teams player of the month award |agency=Associated Press |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2010/01/06/cribbs-wins-special-teams-player-of-the-month-award//story?id=4616312 |accessdate=January 10, 2010 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426193117/http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2010/01/06/cribbs-wins-special-teams-player-of-the-month-award/story/?id=4616312 |archivedate=April 26, 2012 }} == 2010 Pro Bowl == KR Josh Cribbs and T [[Joe Thomas (American football)|Joe Thomas]] were recognized for individual accomplishments as they were named to the AFC roster for the [[2010 Pro Bowl]].{{cite web|author=Jackson, Zac |date=December 29, 2009 |title=Thomas, Cribbs headed to Pro Bowl |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=10346 |accessdate=December 30, 2009 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100103234620/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=10346 |archivedate=January 3, 2010 |deadurl=yes }} Cribbs, who made his second appearance, was the starting kick and punt returner. Joe Thomas ''(1st team)'' | shortnavlink = Browns seasons }} The '''[[2009 NFL season|2009]] [[Cleveland Browns]] [[List of Cleveland Browns seasons|season]]''' was the team's 61st season as a professional sports franchise and its 57th season as a member of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). The team placed fourth in the [[AFC North]] with a record of 5–11, improving upon its [[2008 Cleveland Browns season|2008]] record of 4–12. This season marked [[George Kokinis]] and [[Eric Mangini]]'s first seasons as the team's [[general manager]] and [[head coach]], respectively; however, Kokinis was fired on November 2 during the team's Week 9 bye week.{{cite web|author=Mortensen, Chris and Adam Schefter |date=November 2, 2009 |title= Browns GM Kokinis ousted|work=ESPN|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=4616312|accessdate=November 2, 2009| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20091105035109/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=4616312| archivedate= 5 November 2009 | deadurl= no}} The Browns played all of their home games at [[Cleveland Browns Stadium]] in [[Cleveland, Ohio]]. The Browns missed the playoffs for the seventh straight season, tying a record set between 1973–79. {{TOC limit|limit=4}} == Offseason == === Personnel changes === On December 29, 2008, the Cleveland Browns announced that the team had fired general manager [[Phil Savage]] and head coach [[Romeo Crennel]] after spending four seasons together in Cleveland.{{cite web|title=Browns announce changes |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9338 |work=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=December 29, 2008 |accessdate=April 26, 2009 |archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/5hgJSXQKM?url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9338 |archivedate=June 20, 2009 |deadurl=no |df= }} Crennel, who joined the Browns with Savage in 2005, left Cleveland with a record of 24–40 (.375) and an 0–8 record against the division rival [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. The team's best record under Crennel was 10–6 during the [[2007 Cleveland Browns season|2007 season]]. On January 7, 2009, the Browns announced that the team had found its replacement for Crennel and that it had reached a contractual agreement with former [[New York Jets]] head coach [[Eric Mangini]], who was fired after three seasons in New York.{{cite web|title=Browns, Mangini reach agreement |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9357 |work=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=January 7, 2009 |accessdate=April 26, 2009 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090218075525/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9357 |archivedate=February 18, 2009 }} Mangini, who joined the Jets in 2006, left New York with a record of 23–25 (.479), including a 10–6 record and a playoff appearance in his [[2006 New York Jets season|first season]]. On January 14, the Browns announced that Mangini had named his coordinators: [[Brian Daboll]] was hired as the offensive coordinator; [[Rob Ryan]] as the defensive coordinator; and [[Brad Seely]] as the special teams coordinator and assistant head coach.{{cite web|author=Jackson, Zac |date=January 22, 2009 |title=Mangini names coordinators |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9371 |work=ClevelandBrowns.com |accessdate=April 26, 2009 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090429101119/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9371 |archivedate=April 29, 2009 |deadurl=yes }} Daboll was most recently the quarterbacks coach for the Jets from 2007–2008; Ryan was the defensive coordinator for the [[Oakland Raiders]] from 2004–2008; and Seely was the special teams coach for the [[New England Patriots]] from 1999–2008. All three worked with Mangini from 2000–2003 as members of New England. Daboll, Ryan, and Seely replace [[Rob Chudzinski]], [[Mel Tucker]], and [[Ted Daisher]], respectively. On January 22, the Browns hired five assistant coaches: [[Bryan Cox]] was hired as the defensive line coach; Andy Dickerson as the defensive quality control coach; [[Jerome Henderson]] as the defensive backs coach; [[Rick Lyle]] as an assistant strength-and-conditioning coach; and [[Carl Smith (American football)|Carl Smith]] as the quarterbacks coach.{{cite web|author=Jackson, Zac |date=January 22, 2009 |title=Browns announce hiring of 5 assistants |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9384 |work=ClevelandBrowns.com |accessdate=April 26, 2009 }}{{dead link|date=April 2017|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Cox, Dickerson, Henderson, and Lyle spent the past three seasons with Mangini in New York. Smith was the Browns' quarterbacks coach from 2001–2003 and was most recently the offensive coordinator for the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] from 2005–2006. On January 25, the Browns hired former [[Baltimore Ravens]] director of pro personnel [[George Kokinis]] as general manager.{{cite web|title=Browns announce hiring of Kokinis |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9385 |work=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=January 25, 2009 |accessdate=April 26, 2009 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090414054503/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=9385 |archivedate=April 14, 2009 |deadurl=yes }} Kokinis spent five seasons in the Browns' scouting department from 1991–1995, and after the team moved to Baltimore, he was a member of the Ravens' scouting department from 1996–1999. He was the Ravens' assistant director of pro personnel from 2000–2002 and was the director of pro personnel from 2003–2008. On February 4, the Browns hired three more assistant coaches: [[Alan DeGennaro]] was hired as an assistant strength-and-conditioning coach; [[Tom Myslinski]] as the strength-and-conditioning coach; |archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/5hgJWAujb?url=http://www.ohio.com/sports/zips/48112542.html |archivedate=June 20, 2009 |deadurl=no |df= }} |} === Legal troubles for WR Stallworth === On March 14, Browns wide receiver [[Donté Stallworth]] was involved in a fatal accident in which he struck and killed pedestrian Mario Reyes with his car in the early morning in [[Miami]], [[Florida]].{{cite web|author=Associated Press|date=March 14, 2009|title=Stallworth involved in fatal accident|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=3980182|work=ESPN.com|accessdate=April 27, 2009| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20090317094141/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=3980182| archivedate= 17 March 2009 | deadurl= no}} Stallworth then stopped his vehicle and called 9–1–1. Reports showed that Stallworth was driving under the influence; his blood-alcohol level was 0.12%, above Florida's legal limit of 0.08%.{{cite web|author=Associated Press|date=April 2, 2009|title=Stallworth charged in man's death|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=4033632|work=ESPN.com|accessdate=April 27, 2009| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20090413151241/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=4033632| archivedate= 13 April 2009 | deadurl= no}} He was charged with DUI manslaughter and a warrant was issued for his arrest on April 1 and he surrendered to police on April 2. On June 16, Stallworth pleaded guilty. He was sentenced to 30 days in prison, two years' house arrest, and eight years probation.{{cite web|author=Anderson, Curt |date=June 16, 2009 |title=WR Stallworth pleads guilty, gets 30 days in jail |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/news;_ylt=Ag03K74khn3mP_D7G55jtBU5nYcB?slug=ap-stallworth-pedestriankilled&prov=ap&type=lgns |accessdate=June 16, 2009 |archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/5hgJVlEno?url=http://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/news?slug%3Dap-stallworth-pedestriankilled%26prov%3Dap%26type%3Dlgns |archivedate=June 20, 2009 |deadurl=no |df= }} Many believed that the sentence Stallworth received was too lenient{{Citation needed|date=June 2009}} as he could have served up to 15 years in jail. Stallworth also reached an undisclosed financial settlement with the victim's family. On June 18, the NFL suspended Stallworth indefinitely{{cite news|author=Smith, Joe |date=June 18, 2009 |title=Browns WR Stallworth suspended indefinitely by NFL |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/news;_ylt=ArPmU93kTVuOTqFy0pAd0GY5nYcB?slug=ap-browns-stallworthsuspended&prov=ap&type=lgns |agency=Associated Press |accessdate=June 18, 2009}} On August 13, the NFL officially suspended Stallworth for the entire 2009 season, and made plans to reinstate him after the Super Bowl. === Uniform changes === In 2009, the Cleveland Browns wore brown pants for games in which they wear white jerseys. These were worn in the 2008 pre-season.
