{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2013}} {{Infobox writer | name = Jorge Amado | image = Jorge Amado, 1935.jpg | image_size = 200px | alt = | caption = Jorge Amado in 1935. | pseudonym = | birth_name = Jorge Leal Amado de Faria | birth_date = {{Birth date|1912|8|10|df=y}} | birth_place = [[Itabuna]], [[Bahia]], Brazil | death_date = {{Death date and age|2001|8|6|1912|8|10|df=y}} | death_place = [[Salvador, Bahia]], Brazil | occupation = Writer, professor | nationality = Brazilian | citizenship = | education = | alma_mater = [[Federal University of Rio de Janeiro Faculty of Law]] | period = | genre = | subject = | movement = [[Modernism]] | notableworks = ''[[Gabriela, Clove and Cinnamon]]'', ''[[Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands (novel)|Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands]]'', ''[[Tieta]]'', ''[[Captains of the Sands]]'' | spouse = [[Zélia Gattai]] (1945–2001) (his death) | partner = | children = | relatives = [[Véra Clouzot]] (cousin) | influences = | influenced = | awards = | signature = Jorge Amado Signature.jpg | website = | portaldisp = }} '''Jorge Leal Amado de Faria''' ({{IPA-pt|ˈʒɔʁʒi lɛˈaw ɐˈmadu dʒi fɐˈɾi.ɐ|br}}, 10 August 1912 – 6 August 2001) was a Brazilian writer of the [[Modernism|modernist]] school. He remains the best known of modern Brazilian writers, with his work having been translated into some 49 languages and popularized in film, notably ''[[Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands (novel)|Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands]]'' in 1978. His work reflects the image of a [[Mestiço]] Brazil and is marked by religious [[syncretism]]. He depicted a cheerful and optimistic country that was beset, at the same time, with deep social and economic differences. He occupied the 23rd chair of the [[Academia Brasileira de Letras|Brazilian Academy of Letters]] from 1961 until his death in 2001. ==Biography== Amado was born on a farm near the inland city of [[Itabuna]], in the south of the Brazilian state of [[Bahia]]. He was the eldest of four sons of João Amado de Faria and D. Eulália Leal. The farm was located in the village of Ferradas, which, though today is a district of Itabuna, was at the time administered by the coastal city of [[Ilhéus]]. For this reason he considered himself a citizen of Ilhéus. From his exposure to the large [[Theobroma cacao|cocoa]] plantations of the area, Amado knew the misery and the struggles of the people working the land and living in almost slave conditions. This was to be a theme present in several of his works (for example, ''[[The Violent Land]]'' of 1944). As a result of a smallpox epidemic, his family moved to Ilhéus when he was one year old, and he spent his childhood there.{{cite web |title=Bis!: Clássicos de Jorge Amado adaptados para cinema, TV e teatro (in Portuguese) |url=http://redeglobo.globo.com/globoteatro/bis/noticia/2013/09/jorge-amado-classicos-adaptados-para-cinema-televisao-e-teatro.html |website=Rede Globo |accessdate=17 December 2015}} He attended high school in [[Salvador, Bahia|Salvador]], the capital of the state. By the age of 14 Amado had begun to collaborate with several magazines and took part in literary life, as one of the founders of the Modernist "Rebels' Academy". He was the cousin of Brazilian [[lawyer]], [[writer]], [[journalist]] and [[politician]] [[:pt:Gilberto Amado|Gilberto Amado]],{{cite news|url=http://www.brasil247.com/pt/247/cultura/15216/Recordando-Gilberto-Amado.htm|title=Recordando Gilberto Amado |work=Brasil 247 | language=Portuguese | date=14 September 2011|accessdate=9 May 2017}} and of Brazilian [[actress]] and [[screenwriter]] [[Véra Clouzot]].{{cite news|url=http://www.oexplorador.com.br/vera-amado-clouzot-atriz-de-cinema-de-as-diabolicas-e-o-salario-do-medo/|title=Vera Amado Clouzot, atriz de cinema de (As Diabólicas, e O Salário do Medo) |work=O Explorador | language=Portuguese | date=7 August 2012|accessdate=9 May 2017}} Amado published his first novel, ''[[The Country of Carnival]]'', in 1931, at age 18. He married Matilde Garcia Rosa and had a daughter, Lila, in 1933. The same year he published his second novel, ''[[Cacau (novel)|Cacau]]'', which increased his popularity. He studied law at the [[Federal University of Rio de Janeiro Faculty of Law]] but never became a practising lawyer.{{cite web |title=Jorge Amado (in Portuguese) |url=http://educacao.uol.com.br/biografias/jorge-amado.htm |website=UOL |accessdate=17 December 2015}} His [[leftist]] activities made his life difficult under the dictatorial regime of [[Getúlio Vargas]]. In 1935 he was arrested for the first time, and two years later his books were publicly burned. His works were banned from Portugal, but in the rest of Europe he gained great popularity with the publication of ''[[Jubiabá]]'' in France. The book had enthusiastic reviews, including that of [[Nobel prize|Nobel Prize]] Award winner [[Albert Camus]]. In the early 1940s, Amado edited a literary supplement for the [[Nazism|Nazi]]-funded political newspaper "Meio-Dia".{{cite web |url=http://www.observatoriodaimprensa.com.br/artigos/mt200499.htm |publisher=Observatório da Imprensa |language=Portuguese |title=Os intelectuais e o Estado Novo (interview with Joel Silveira)}}{{cite news |language=Portuguese |url=http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/folha/ilustrada/ult90u16403.shtml |publisher=Folha On Line |title=Jorge Amado foi o autor mais espionado |author=Mario Magalhães |accessdate=2010-05-21 |date=8 August 2001}} Being a communist militant, from 1941 to 1942 Amado was compelled to go into exile to [[Argentina]] and [[Uruguay]]. When he returned to Brazil he separated from Matilde Garcia Rosa. In 1945 he was elected to the National Constituent Assembly, as a representative of the [[Brazilian Communist Party]] (PCB) (he received more votes than any other candidate in the state of [[São Paulo]]). He signed a law granting freedom of religious faith. He remarried in 1945, to the writer [[Zélia Gattai]]. In 1947 they had a son, João Jorge. The same year his party was declared illegal, and its members arrested and persecuted. Amado chose exile once again, this time in France, where he remained until he was expelled in 1950. His daughter from his first marriage, Lila, died in 1949. From 1950 to 1952 Amado and Gattai lived in [[Czechoslovakia]], where another daughter, Paloma, was born. He also travelled to the [[Soviet Union]], winning the [[Lenin Peace Prize|Stalin Peace Prize]] in 1951.{{cite book |author=Zélia Gattai |title=Jardim de Inverno |year=1988 |publisher=Editora Record |isbn=85-1-033969-4}} Recently released documents show that in this period he was investigated by CIA.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/ilustrada/2017/02/1857598-documentos-da-cia-revelam-investigacoes-sobre-jorge-amado.shtml|title=Documentos da CIA revelam investigações sobre Jorge Amado - 11/02/2017 - Ilustrada - Folha de S.Paulo|website=www1.folha.uol.com.br|access-date=2017-02-28}} On his return to Brazil in 1954, Amado abandoned active political life, leaving the Communist Party one year later. From that period on he dedicated himself solely to literature. His second creative phase began in 1958 with ''[[Gabriela, Clove and Cinnamon]]'', which was described by [[Jean-Paul Sartre]] as "the best example of a folk novel". Amado abandoned, in part, the realism and the social themes of his early works, producing a series of novels focusing mainly on feminine characters, devoted to a kind of smiling celebration of the traditions and the beauties of Bahia. In addition to ''Gabriela'' these novels included ''Tereza Batista: Home from the Wars'' and ''Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands''. His depiction of the sexual customs of his land was scandalous to much of 1950s Brazilian society and for several years Amado could not even enter [[Ilhéus]], where ''Gabriela'' was set, due to threats received for the alleged offense to the morality of the city's women. Besides the turning point, the Soviet Union kept publishing Amado's works shortly after their release in Portuguese.{{Cite journal|last=Darmaros|first=Marina|date=2017-01-24|title=Por que ler Jorge Amado em russo: a cultura soviética revelada na tradução de Gabriela|url=http://www.revistas.usp.br/tradterm/article/view/125561|journal=Tradterm|language=pt|volume=28|issue=0|pages=223–248|doi=10.11606/issn.2317-9511.v28i0p223-248|issn=2317-9511}} On 6 April 1961, he was elected to the [[Academia Brasileira de Letras|Brazilian Academy of Letters]]. On his death his wife was elected to replace him. Amado made the Academy the setting for one of his novels, [[Pen, Sword, Camisole]]. He received the title of Doctor ''honoris causa'' from several universities in Brazil, Portugal, Italy, [[Israel]] and France, as well as other honors in almost every South American country, including ''Obá de Xangô'' (santoon) of the [[Candomblé]], the traditional Afro-Brazilian religion of Bahia. He was finally removed from the French Government blacklist in 1965 following the intervention of the then Minister of Culture, [[André Malraux]]. In 1984 he was awarded the French [[Legion of Honour|Légion d’Honneur]] by President [[François Mitterrand]]. [[File:Fundacaocasajorgeamado.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Jorge Amado Foundation in Salvador da Bahia]] Amado's popularity as a writer has never declined. His books have been translated into 49 languages in 55 countries, and adapted into films, theatrical works and TV programs. They even inspired some [[samba]] schools of the [[Brazilian Carnival]]. In 1987, the ''House of Jorge Amado Foundation'' was created, in Salvador. It promotes the protection of Amado's estate and the development of culture in [[Bahia]]. The recently renovated building on the [[Pelourinho]] in Salvador contains a small museum and wall panels with the covers of international editions of his books. Amado died on 6 August 2001. His ashes were spread in the garden of his house four days later. In December 4, 2014 he received (posthumously) from the [[Legislative Assembly of Bahia]] appointment as Commander of [[Meritorious Citizen of the Freedom and Social Justice João Mangabeira (CBJM)]], due to his work in defense of social rights, the State's highest honor.{{cite web |url=http://www.gplsalvador.com.br/noticia/samurai-da-voz-recebe-o-titulo-de-cidadao-benemerito-na-assembleia-legislativa/ |title=Taurino Araújo receives the title of Meritorious Citizen in the {{Use dmy dates|date=July 2013}} {{Infobox writer | name = Jorge Amado | image = Jorge Amado, 1935.jpg | image_size = 200px | alt = | caption = Jorge Amado in 1935. | pseudonym = | birth_name = Jorge Leal Amado de Faria | birth_date = {{Birth date|1912|8|10|df=y}} | birth_place = [[Itabuna]], [[Bahia]], Brazil | death_date = {{Death date and age|2001|8|6|1912|8|10|df=y}} | death_place = [[Salvador, Bahia]], Brazil | occupation = Writer, professor | nationality = Brazilian | citizenship = | education = | alma_mater = [[Federal University of Rio de Janeiro Faculty of Law]] | period = | genre = | subject = | movement = [[Modernism]] | notableworks = ''[[Gabriela, Clove and Cinnamon]]'', ''[[Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands (novel)|Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands]]'', ''[[Tieta]]'', ''[[Captains of the Sands]]'' | spouse = [[Zélia Gattai]] (1945–2001) (his death) | partner = | children = | relatives = [[Véra Clouzot]] (cousin) | influences = | influenced = | awards = | signature = Jorge Amado Signature.jpg | website = | portaldisp = }} '''Jorge Leal Amado de Faria''' ({{IPA-pt|ˈʒɔʁʒi lɛˈaw ɐˈmadu dʒi fɐˈɾi.ɐ|br}}, 10 August 1912 – 6 August 2001) was a Brazilian writer of the [[Modernism|modernist]] school. He remains the best known of modern Brazilian writers, with his work having been translated into some 49 languages and popularized in film, notably ''[[Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands (novel)|Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands]]'' in 1978. His work reflects the image of a [[Mestiço]] Brazil and is marked by religious [[syncretism]]. He depicted a cheerful and optimistic country that was beset, at the same time, with deep social and economic differences. He occupied the 23rd chair of the [[Academia Brasileira de Letras|Brazilian Academy of Letters]] from 1961 until his death in 2001. ==Biography== Amado was born on a farm near the inland city of [[Itabuna]], in the south of the Brazilian state of [[Bahia]]. He was the eldest of four sons of João Amado de Faria and D. Eulália Leal. The farm was located in the village of Ferradas, which, though today is a district of Itabuna, was at the time administered by the coastal city of [[Ilhéus]]. For this reason he considered himself a citizen of Ilhéus. From his exposure to the large [[Theobroma cacao|cocoa]] plantations of the area, Amado knew the misery and the struggles of the people working the land and living in almost slave conditions. This was to be a theme present in several of his works (for example, ''[[The Violent Land]]'' of 1944). As a result of a smallpox epidemic, his family moved to Ilhéus when he was one year old, and he spent his childhood there.{{cite web |title=Bis!: Clássicos de Jorge Amado adaptados para cinema, TV e teatro (in Portuguese) |url=http://redeglobo.globo.com/globoteatro/bis/noticia/2013/09/jorge-amado-classicos-adaptados-para-cinema-televisao-e-teatro.html |website=Rede Globo |accessdate=17 December 2015}} He attended high school in [[Salvador, Bahia|Salvador]], the capital of the state. By the age of 14 Amado had begun to collaborate with several magazines and took part in literary life, as one of the founders of the Modernist "Rebels' Academy". He was the cousin of Brazilian [[lawyer]], [[writer]], [[journalist]] and [[politician]] [[:pt:Gilberto Amado|Gilberto Amado]],{{cite news|url=http://www.brasil247.com/pt/247/cultura/15216/Recordando-Gilberto-Amado.htm|title=Recordando Gilberto Amado |work=Brasil 247 | language=Portuguese | date=14 September 2011|accessdate=9 May 2017}} and of Brazilian [[actress]] and [[screenwriter]] [[Véra Clouzot]].{{cite news|url=http://www.oexplorador.com.br/vera-amado-clouzot-atriz-de-cinema-de-as-diabolicas-e-o-salario-do-medo/|title=Vera Amado Clouzot, atriz de cinema de (As Diabólicas, e O Salário do Medo) |work=O Explorador | language=Portuguese | date=7 August 2012|accessdate=9 May 2017}} Amado published his first novel, ''[[The Country of Carnival]]'', in 1931, at age 18. He married Matilde Garcia Rosa and had a daughter, Lila, in 1933. The same year he published his second novel, ''[[Cacau (novel)|Cacau]]'', which increased his popularity. He studied law at the [[Federal University of Rio de Janeiro Faculty of Law]] but never became a practising lawyer.{{cite web |title=Jorge Amado (in Portuguese) |url=http://educacao.uol.com.br/biografias/jorge-amado.htm |website=UOL |accessdate=17 December 2015}} His [[leftist]] activities made his life difficult under the dictatorial regime of [[Getúlio Vargas]]. In 1935 he was arrested for the first time, and two years later his books were publicly burned. His works were banned from Portugal, but in the rest of Europe he gained great popularity with the publication of ''[[Jubiabá]]'' in France. The book had enthusiastic reviews, including that of [[Nobel prize|Nobel Prize]] Award winner [[Albert Camus]]. In the early 1940s, Amado edited a literary supplement for the [[Nazism|Nazi]]-funded political newspaper "Meio-Dia".{{cite web |url=http://www.observatoriodaimprensa.com.br/artigos/mt200499.htm |publisher=Observatório da Imprensa |language=Portuguese |title=Os intelectuais e o Estado Novo (interview with Joel Silveira)}}{{cite news |language=Portuguese |url=http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/folha/ilustrada/ult90u16403.shtml |publisher=Folha On Line |title=Jorge Amado foi o autor mais espionado |author=Mario Magalhães |accessdate=2010-05-21 |date=8 August 2001}} Being a communist militant, from 1941 to 1942 Amado was compelled to go into exile to [[Argentina]] and [[Uruguay]]. When he returned to Brazil he separated from Matilde Garcia Rosa. In 1945 he was elected to the National Constituent Assembly, as a representative of the [[Brazilian Communist Party]] (PCB) (he received more votes than any other candidate in the state of [[São Paulo]]). He signed a law granting freedom of religious faith. He remarried in 1945, to the writer [[Zélia Gattai]]. In 1947 they had a son, João Jorge. The same year his party was declared illegal, and its members arrested and persecuted. Amado chose exile once again, this time in France, where he remained until he was expelled in 1950. His daughter from his first marriage, Lila, died in 1949. From 1950 to 1952 Amado and Gattai lived in [[Czechoslovakia]], where another daughter, Paloma, was born. He also travelled to the [[Soviet Union]], winning the [[Lenin Peace Prize|Stalin Peace Prize]] in 1951.{{cite book |author=Zélia Gattai |title=Jardim de Inverno |year=1988 |publisher=Editora Record |isbn=85-1-033969-4}} Recently released documents show that in this period he was investigated by CIA.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/ilustrada/2017/02/1857598-documentos-da-cia-revelam-investigacoes-sobre-jorge-amado.shtml|title=Documentos da CIA revelam investigações sobre Jorge Amado - 11/02/2017 - Ilustrada - Folha de S.Paulo|website=www1.folha.uol.com.br|access-date=2017-02-28}} On his return to Brazil in 1954, Amado abandoned active political life, leaving the Communist Party one year later. From that period on he dedicated himself solely to literature. His second creative phase began in 1958 with ''[[Gabriela, Clove and Cinnamon]]'', which was described by [[Jean-Paul Sartre]] as "the best example of a folk novel". Amado abandoned, in part, the realism and the social themes of his early works, producing a series of novels focusing mainly on feminine characters, devoted to a kind of smiling celebration of the traditions and the beauties of Bahia. In addition to ''Gabriela'' these novels included ''Tereza Batista: Home from the Wars'' and ''Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands''. His depiction of the sexual customs of his land was scandalous to much of 1950s Brazilian society and for several years Amado could not even enter [[Ilhéus]], where ''Gabriela'' was set, due to threats received for the alleged offense to the morality of the city's women. Besides the turning point, the Soviet Union kept publishing Amado's works shortly after their release in Portuguese.{{Cite journal|last=Darmaros|first=Marina|date=2017-01-24|title=Por que ler Jorge Amado em russo: a cultura soviética revelada na tradução de Gabriela|url=http://www.revistas.usp.br/tradterm/article/view/125561|journal=Tradterm|language=pt|volume=28|issue=0|pages=223–248|doi=10.11606/issn.2317-9511.v28i0p223-248|issn=2317-9511}} On 6 April 1961, he was elected to the [[Academia Brasileira de Letras|Brazilian Academy of Letters]]. On his death his wife was elected to replace him. Amado made the Academy the setting for one of his novels, [[Pen, Sword, Camisole]]. He received the title of Doctor ''honoris causa'' from several universities in Brazil, Portugal, Italy, [[Israel]] and France, as well as other honors in almost every South American country, including ''Obá de Xangô'' (santoon) of the [[Candomblé]], the traditional Afro-Brazilian religion of Bahia. He was finally removed from the French Government blacklist in 1965 following the intervention of the then Minister of Culture, [[André Malraux]]. In 1984 he was awarded the French [[Legion of Honour|Légion d’Honneur]] by President [[François Mitterrand]]. [[File:Fundacaocasajorgeamado.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Jorge Amado Foundation in Salvador da Bahia]] Amado's popularity as a writer has never declined. His books have been translated into 49 languages in 55 countries, and adapted into films, theatrical works and TV programs. They even inspired some [[samba]] schools of the [[Brazilian Carnival]]. In 1987, the ''House of Jorge Amado Foundation'' was created, in Salvador. It promotes the protection of Amado's estate and the development of culture in [[Bahia]]. The recently renovated building on the [[Pelourinho]] in Salvador contains a small museum and wall panels with the covers of international editions of his books. Amado died on 6 August 2001. His ashes were spread in the garden of his house four days later. In December 4, 2014 he received (posthumously) from the [[Legislative Assembly of Bahia]] appointment as Commander of [[Meritorious Citizen of the Freedom and Social Justice João Mangabeira (CBJM)]], due to his work in defense of social rights, the State's highest honor.{{cite web |url=http://www.gplsalvador.com.br/noticia/samurai-da-voz-recebe-o-titulo-de-cidadao-benemerito-na-assembleia-legislativa/ |title=Taurino Araújo receives the title of Meritorious Citizen in the {{Use dmy dates|date=July 2013}} {{Infobox writer | name = Jorge Amado | image = Jorge Amado, 1935.jpg | image_size = 200px | alt = | caption = Jorge Amado in 1935. | pseudonym = | birth_name = Jorge Leal Amado de Faria | birth_date = {{Birth date|1912|8|10|df=y}} | birth_place = [[Itabuna]], [[Bahia]], Brazil | death_date = {{Death date and age|2001|8|6|1912|8|10|df=y}} | death_place = [[Salvador, Bahia]], Brazil | occupation = Writer, professor | nationality = Brazilian | citizenship = | education = | alma_mater = [[Federal University of Rio de Janeiro Faculty of Law]] | period = | genre = | subject = | movement = [[Modernism]] | notableworks = ''[[Gabriela, Clove and Cinnamon]]'', ''[[Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands (novel)|Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands]]'', ''[[Tieta]]'', ''[[Captains of the Sands]]'' | spouse = [[Zélia Gattai]] (1945–2001) (his death) | partner = | children = | relatives = [[Véra Clouzot]] (cousin) | influences = | influenced = | awards = | signature = Jorge Amado Signature.jpg | website = | portaldisp = }} '''Jorge Leal Amado de Faria''' ({{IPA-pt|ˈʒɔʁʒi lɛˈaw ɐˈmadu dʒi fɐˈɾi.ɐ|br}}, 10 August 1912 – 6 August 2001) was a Brazilian writer of the [[Modernism|modernist]] school. He remains the best known of modern Brazilian writers, with his work having been translated into some 49 languages and popularized in film, notably ''[[Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands (novel)|Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands]]'' in 1978. His work reflects the image of a [[Mestiço]] Brazil and is marked by religious [[syncretism]]. He depicted a cheerful and optimistic country that was beset, at the same time, with deep social and economic differences. He occupied the 23rd chair of the [[Academia Brasileira de Letras|Brazilian Academy of Letters]] from 1961 until his death in 2001. ==Biography== Amado was born on a farm near the inland city of [[Itabuna]], in the south of the Brazilian state of [[Bahia]]. He was the eldest of four sons of João Amado de Faria and D. Eulália Leal. The farm was located in the village of Ferradas, which, though today is a district of Itabuna, was at the time administered by the coastal city of [[Ilhéus]]. For this reason he considered himself a citizen of Ilhéus. From his exposure to the large [[Theobroma cacao|cocoa]] plantations of the area, Amado knew the misery and the struggles of the people working the land and living in almost slave conditions. This was to be a theme present in several of his works (for example, ''[[The Violent Land]]'' of 1944). As a result of a smallpox epidemic, his family moved to Ilhéus when he was one year old, and he spent his childhood there.{{cite web |title=Bis!: Clássicos de Jorge Amado adaptados para cinema, TV e teatro (in Portuguese) |url=http://redeglobo.globo.com/globoteatro/bis/noticia/2013/09/jorge-amado-classicos-adaptados-para-cinema-televisao-e-teatro.html |website=Rede Globo |accessdate=17 December 2015}} He attended high school in [[Salvador, Bahia|Salvador]], the capital of the state. By the age of 14 Amado had begun to collaborate with several magazines and took part in literary life, as one of the founders of the Modernist "Rebels' Academy". He was the cousin of Brazilian [[lawyer]], [[writer]], [[journalist]] and [[politician]] [[:pt:Gilberto Amado|Gilberto Amado]],{{cite news|url=http://www.brasil247.com/pt/247/cultura/15216/Recordando-Gilberto-Amado.htm|title=Recordando Gilberto Amado |work=Brasil 247 | language=Portuguese | date=14 September 2011|accessdate=9 May 2017}} and of Brazilian [[actress]] and [[screenwriter]] [[Véra Clouzot]].{{cite news|url=http://www.oexplorador.com.br/vera-amado-clouzot-atriz-de-cinema-de-as-diabolicas-e-o-salario-do-medo/|title=Vera Amado Clouzot, atriz de cinema de (As Diabólicas, e O Salário do Medo) |work=O Explorador | language=Portuguese | date=7 August 2012|accessdate=9 May 2017}} Amado published his first novel, ''[[The Country of Carnival]]'', in 1931, at age 18. He married Matilde Garcia Rosa and had a daughter, Lila, in 1933. The same year he published his second novel, ''[[Cacau (novel)|Cacau]]'', which increased his popularity. He studied law at the [[Federal University of Rio de Janeiro Faculty of Law]] but never became a practising lawyer.{{cite web |title=Jorge Amado (in Portuguese) |url=http://educacao.uol.com.br/biografias/jorge-amado.htm |website=UOL |accessdate=17 December 2015}} His [[leftist]] activities made his life difficult under the dictatorial regime of [[Getúlio Vargas]]. In 1935 he was arrested for the first time, and two years later his books were publicly burned. His works were banned from Portugal, but in the rest of Europe he gained great popularity with the publication of ''[[Jubiabá]]'' in France. The book had enthusiastic reviews, including that of [[Nobel prize|Nobel Prize]] Award winner [[Albert Camus]]. In the early 1940s, Amado edited a literary supplement for the [[Nazism|Nazi]]-funded political newspaper "Meio-Dia".{{cite web |url=http://www.observatoriodaimprensa.com.br/artigos/mt200499.htm |publisher=Observatório da Imprensa |language=Portuguese |title=Os intelectuais e o Estado Novo (interview with Joel Silveira)}}{{cite news |language=Portuguese |url=http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/folha/ilustrada/ult90u16403.shtml |publisher=Folha On Line |title=Jorge Amado foi o autor mais espionado |author=Mario Magalhães |accessdate=2010-05-21 |date=8 August 2001}} Being a communist militant, from 1941 to 1942 Amado was compelled to go into exile to [[Argentina]] and [[Uruguay]]. When he returned to Brazil he separated from Matilde Garcia Rosa. In 1945 he was elected to the National Constituent Assembly, as a representative of the [[Brazilian Communist Party]] (PCB) (he received more votes than any other candidate in the state of [[São Paulo]]). He signed a law granting freedom of religious faith. He remarried in 1945, to the writer [[Zélia Gattai]]. In 1947 they had a son, João Jorge. The same year his party was declared illegal, and its members arrested and persecuted. Amado chose exile once again, this time in France, where he remained until he was expelled in 1950. His daughter from his first marriage, Lila, died in 1949. From 1950 to 1952 Amado and Gattai lived in [[Czechoslovakia]], where another daughter, Paloma, was born. He also travelled to the [[Soviet Union]], winning the [[Lenin Peace Prize|Stalin Peace Prize]] in 1951.{{cite book |author=Zélia Gattai |title=Jardim de Inverno |year=1988 |publisher=Editora Record |isbn=85-1-033969-4}} Recently released documents show that in this period he was investigated by CIA.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/ilustrada/2017/02/1857598-documentos-da-cia-revelam-investigacoes-sobre-jorge-amado.shtml|title=Documentos da CIA revelam investigações sobre Jorge Amado - 11/02/2017 - Ilustrada - Folha de S.Paulo|website=www1.folha.uol.com.br|access-date=2017-02-28}} [[File:Jorge Amado, 1972.tif|left|thumb|Jorge Amado, 1972. [[Brazilian National Archives|National Archives of Brazil.]]]] On his return to Brazil in 1954, Amado abandoned active political life, leaving the Communist Party one year later. From that period on he dedicated himself solely to literature. His second creative phase began in 1958 with ''[[Gabriela, Clove and Cinnamon]]'', which was described by [[Jean-Paul Sartre]] as "the best example of a folk novel". Amado abandoned, in part, the realism and the social themes of his early works, producing a series of novels focusing mainly on feminine characters, devoted to a kind of smiling celebration of the traditions and the beauties of Bahia. In addition to ''Gabriela'' these novels included ''Tereza Batista: Home from the Wars'' and ''Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands''. His depiction of the sexual customs of his land was scandalous to much of 1950s Brazilian society and for several years Amado could not even enter [[Ilhéus]], where ''Gabriela'' was set, due to threats received for the alleged offense to the morality of the city's women. Besides the turning point, the Soviet Union kept publishing Amado's works shortly after their release in Portuguese.{{Cite journal|last=Darmaros|first=Marina|date=2017-01-24|title=Por que ler Jorge Amado em russo: a cultura soviética revelada na tradução de Gabriela|url=http://www.revistas.usp.br/tradterm/article/view/125561|journal=Tradterm|language=pt|volume=28|issue=0|pages=223–248|doi=10.11606/issn.2317-9511.v28i0p223-248|issn=2317-9511}} On 6 April 1961, he was elected to the [[Academia Brasileira de Letras|Brazilian Academy of Letters]]. On his death his wife was elected to replace him. Amado made the Academy the setting for one of his novels, [[Pen, Sword, Camisole]]. He received the title of Doctor ''honoris causa'' from several universities in Brazil, Portugal, Italy, [[Israel]] and France, as well as other honors in almost every South American country, including ''Obá de Xangô'' (santoon) of the [[Candomblé]], the traditional Afro-Brazilian religion of Bahia. He was finally removed from the French Government blacklist in 1965 following the intervention of the then Minister of Culture, [[André Malraux]]. In 1984 he was awarded the French [[Legion of Honour|Légion d’Honneur]] by President [[François Mitterrand]]. [[File:Fundacaocasajorgeamado.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Jorge Amado Foundation in Salvador da Bahia]] Amado's popularity as a writer has never declined. His books have been translated into 49 languages in 55 countries, and adapted into films, theatrical works and TV programs. They even inspired some [[samba]] schools of the [[Brazilian Carnival]]. In 1987, the ''House of Jorge Amado Foundation'' was created, in Salvador. It promotes the protection of Amado's estate and the development of culture in [[Bahia]]. The recently renovated building on the [[Pelourinho]] in Salvador contains a small museum and wall panels with the covers of international editions of his books. Amado died on 6 August 2001. His ashes were spread in the garden of his house four days later. In December 4, 2014 he received (posthumously) from the [[Legislative Assembly of Bahia]] appointment as Commander of [[Meritorious Citizen of the Freedom and Social Justice João Mangabeira (CBJM)]], due to his work in defense of social rights, the State's highest honor.{{cite web |url=http://www.gplsalvador.com.br/noticia/samurai-da-voz-recebe-o-titulo-de-cidadao-benemerito-na-assembleia-legislativa/ |title=Taurino Araújo receives the title of Meritorious Citizen in the His work reflects the image of a [[Mestiço]] Brazil and is marked by religious [[syncretism]]. He depicted a cheerful and optimistic country that was beset, at the same time, with deep social and economic differences. He occupied the 23rd chair of the [[Academia Brasileira de Letras|Brazilian Academy of Letters]] from 1961 until his death in 2001. ==Biography== Amado was born on a farm near the inland city of [[Itabuna]], in the south of the Brazilian state of [[Bahia]]. He was the eldest of four sons of João Amado de Faria and D. Eulália Leal. The farm was located in the village of Ferradas, which, though today is a district of Itabuna, was at the time administered by the coastal city of [[Ilhéus]]. For this reason he considered himself a citizen of Ilhéus. From his exposure to the large [[Theobroma cacao|cocoa]] plantations of the area, Amado knew the misery and the struggles of the people working the land and living in almost slave conditions. This was to be a theme present in several of his works (for example, ''[[The Violent Land]]'' of 1944). As a result of a smallpox epidemic, his family moved to Ilhéus when he was one year old, and he spent his childhood there.{{cite web |title=Bis!: Clássicos de Jorge Amado adaptados para cinema, TV e teatro (in Portuguese) |url=http://redeglobo.globo.com/globoteatro/bis/noticia/2013/09/jorge-amado-classicos-adaptados-para-cinema-televisao-e-teatro.html |website=Rede Globo |accessdate=17 December 2015}} He attended high school in [[Salvador, Bahia|Salvador]], the capital of the state. By the age of 14 Amado had begun to collaborate with several magazines and took part in literary life, as one of the founders of the Modernist "Rebels' Academy". He was the cousin of Brazilian [[lawyer]], [[writer]], [[journalist]] and [[politician]] [[:pt:Gilberto Amado|Gilberto Amado]],{{cite news|url=http://www.brasil247.com/pt/247/cultura/15216/Recordando-Gilberto-Amado.htm|title=Recordando Gilberto Amado |work=Brasil 247 | language=Portuguese | date=14 September 2011|accessdate=9 May 2017}} and of Brazilian [[actress]] and [[screenwriter]] [[Véra Clouzot]].{{cite news|url=http://www.oexplorador.com.br/vera-amado-clouzot-atriz-de-cinema-de-as-diabolicas-e-o-salario-do-medo/|title=Vera Amado Clouzot, atriz de cinema de (As Diabólicas, e O Salário do Medo) |work=O Explorador | language=Portuguese | date=7 August 2012|accessdate=9 May 2017}} Amado published his first novel, ''[[The Country of Carnival]]'', in 1931, at age 18. He married Matilde Garcia Rosa and had a daughter, Lila, in 1933. The same year he published his second novel, ''[[Cacau (novel)|Cacau]]'', which increased his popularity. He studied law at the [[Federal University of Rio de Janeiro Faculty of Law]] but never became a practising lawyer.{{cite web |title=Jorge Amado (in Portuguese) |url=http://educacao.uol.com.br/biografias/jorge-amado.htm |website=UOL |accessdate=17 December 2015}} His [[leftist]] activities made his life difficult under the dictatorial regime of [[Getúlio Vargas]]. In 1935 he was arrested for the first time, and two years later his books were publicly burned. His works were banned from Portugal, but in the rest of Europe he gained great popularity with the publication of ''[[Jubiabá]]'' in France. The book had enthusiastic reviews, including that of [[Nobel prize|Nobel Prize]] Award winner [[Albert Camus]]. In the early 1940s, Amado edited a literary supplement for the [[Nazism|Nazi]]-funded political newspaper "Meio-Dia".{{cite web |url=http://www.observatoriodaimprensa.com.br/artigos/mt200499.htm |publisher=Observatório da Imprensa |language=Portuguese |title=Os intelectuais e o Estado Novo (interview with Joel Silveira)}}{{cite news |language=Portuguese |url=http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/folha/ilustrada/ult90u16403.shtml |publisher=Folha On Line |title=Jorge Amado foi o autor mais espionado |author=Mario Magalhães |accessdate=2010-05-21 |date=8 August 2001}} Being a communist militant, from 1941 to 1942 Amado was compelled to go into exile to [[Argentina]] and [[Uruguay]]. When he returned to Brazil he separated from Matilde Garcia Rosa. In 1945 he was elected to the National Constituent Assembly, as a representative of the [[Brazilian Communist Party]] (PCB) (he received more votes than any other candidate in the state of [[São Paulo]]). He signed a law granting freedom of religious faith. He remarried in 1945, to the writer [[Zélia Gattai]]. In 1947 they had a son, João Jorge. The same year his party was declared illegal, and its members arrested and persecuted. Amado chose exile once again, this time in France, where he remained until he was expelled in 1950. His daughter from his first marriage, Lila, died in 1949. From 1950 to 1952 Amado and Gattai lived in [[Czechoslovakia]], where another daughter, Paloma, was born. He also travelled to the [[Soviet Union]], winning the [[Lenin Peace Prize|Stalin Peace Prize]] in 1951.{{cite book |author=Zélia Gattai |title=Jardim de Inverno |year=1988 |publisher=Editora Record |isbn=85-1-033969-4}} Recently released documents show that in this period he was investigated by CIA.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/ilustrada/2017/02/1857598-documentos-da-cia-revelam-investigacoes-sobre-jorge-amado.shtml|title=Documentos da CIA revelam investigações sobre Jorge Amado - 11/02/2017 - Ilustrada - Folha de S.Paulo|website=www1.folha.uol.com.br|access-date=2017-02-28}} On his return to Brazil in 1954, Amado abandoned active political life, leaving the Communist Party one year later. From that period on he dedicated himself solely to literature. His second creative phase began in 1958 with ''[[Gabriela, Clove and Cinnamon]]'', which was described by [[Jean-Paul Sartre]] as "the best example of a folk novel". Amado abandoned, in part, the realism and the social themes of his early works, producing a series of novels focusing mainly on feminine characters, devoted to a kind of smiling celebration of the traditions and the beauties of Bahia. In addition to ''Gabriela'' these novels included ''Tereza Batista: Home from the Wars'' and ''Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands''. His depiction of the sexual customs of his land was scandalous to much of 1950s Brazilian society and for several years Amado could not even enter [[Ilhéus]], where ''Gabriela'' was set, due to threats received for the alleged offense to the morality of the city's women. Besides the turning point, the Soviet Union kept publishing Amado's works shortly after their release in Portuguese.{{Cite journal|last=Darmaros|first=Marina|date=2017-01-24|title=Por que ler Jorge Amado em russo: a cultura soviética revelada na tradução de Gabriela|url=http://www.revistas.usp.br/tradterm/article/view/125561|journal=Tradterm|language=pt|volume=28|issue=0|pages=223–248|doi=10.11606/issn.2317-9511.v28i0p223-248|issn=2317-9511}} On 6 April 1961, he was elected to the [[Academia Brasileira de Letras|Brazilian Academy of Letters]]. On his death his wife was elected to replace him. Amado made the Academy the setting for one of his novels, [[Pen, Sword, Camisole]]. He received the title of Doctor ''honoris causa'' from several universities in Brazil, Portugal, Italy, [[Israel]] and France, as well as other honors in almost every South American country, including ''Obá de Xangô'' (santoon) of the [[Candomblé]], the traditional Afro-Brazilian religion of Bahia. He was finally removed from the French Government blacklist in 1965 following the intervention of the then Minister of Culture, [[André Malraux]]. In 1984 he was awarded the French [[Legion of Honour|Légion d’Honneur]] by President [[François Mitterrand]]. [[File:Fundacaocasajorgeamado.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Jorge Amado Foundation in Salvador da Bahia]] Amado's popularity as a writer has never declined. His books have been translated into 49 languages in 55 countries, and adapted into films, theatrical works and TV programs. They even inspired some [[samba]] schools of the [[Brazilian Carnival]]. In 1987, the ''House of Jorge Amado Foundation'' was created, in Salvador. It promotes the protection of Amado's estate and the development of culture in [[Bahia]]. The recently renovated building on the [[Pelourinho]] in Salvador contains a small museum and wall panels with the covers of international editions of his books. Amado died on 6 August 2001. His ashes were spread in the garden of his house four days later. In December 4, 2014 he received (posthumously) from the [[Legislative Assembly of Bahia]] appointment as Commander of [[Meritorious Citizen of the Freedom and Social Justice João Mangabeira (CBJM)]], due to his work in defense of social rights, the State's highest honor.{{cite web |url=http://www.gplsalvador.com.br/noticia/samurai-da-voz-recebe-o-titulo-de-cidadao-benemerito-na-assembleia-legislativa/ |title=Taurino Araújo receives the title of Meritorious Citizen in the '''Gerald Reive''' (born 10 March 1937) is a [[New Zealand]]-based [[Falkland Islands]] athlete who represented his country at the [[2010 Commonwealth Games]] in [[New Delhi]], [[India]] in [[Lawn Bowls]] in the men's pairs event, alongside his playing partner [[George Paice (bowls)|George Paice]]. They achieved wins against [[Samoa]] and [[Guernsey]]. Reive was the flag bearer for the Falkland Islands at the closing ceremony. He currently plays lawn bowls at the [[Papatoetoe Hunters Corner Bowling Club]] in [[Auckland]] He attended his second Commonwealth Games in [[2014 Commonwealth Games| Glasgow 2014]] where he entered the men's fours with Michael Reive, Patrick Morrison, and Barry Ford.<ref name="Delhi 2010 Official Website">{{cite web|url=http://www.cwgdelhi2010.org/news/islanders_prove_age_no_barrier|title=XIX Commonwealth Games 2010 Delhi -|website=www.cwgdelhi2010.org}}</ref>

'''Gerald Reive''' (born 10 March 1937) is a [[New Zealand]]-based [[Falkland Islands]] lawn bowler.

==Bowls career==
He represented his country at the [[2010 Commonwealth Games]] in [[New Delhi]], [[India]] in [[Lawn Bowls]] in the men's pairs event, alongside his playing partner [[George Paice (bowls)|George Paice]]. It is listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]] and is a constituent of the [[FTSE 100 Index]]. It specialises in the selling of clothing, home products and [[Luxury good|luxury]] food products. M&S was founded in 1884 by [[Michael Marks]] and [[Thomas Spencer (Marks and Spencer)|Thomas Spencer]] in [[Leeds]].{{cite news|title=M&S launches underwear boutiques|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/986292.stm|accessdate=15 March 2017|agency=BBC|issue=Business|publisher=BBC|date=23 October 2000|location=United Kingdom|language=English}} The company also began to sell branded goods like [[Kellogg's Corn Flakes]] in November 2008.{{cite news |author=Hiscott, Graham |url=http://www.mirror.co.uk/news/city-news/2009/11/04/marks-and-spencer-to-start-selling-top-brands-115875-21796883/ |title=Marks and Spencer to start selling top brands |work=Daily Mirror |location=London |accessdate=18 April 2011}} M&S currently has 959 stores across the U.K including 615 that only sell food products.{{Cite news|url=http://www.bbc.com/news/business-39743611|title=M&S online food delivery service will be no piece of cake|last=Plummer|first=Robert|date=28 April 2017|work=BBC News|access-date=28 April 2017|language=en-GB}} In 1998, the company became the first British retailer to make a pre-tax profit of over £1 billion,{{Cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/business/96531.stm |title=Marks & Spencer profits top expectations |publisher=BBC News |date=19 May 1998 |accessdate=7 November 2009}} although subsequently it went into a sudden slump, which took the company, its shareholders, who included hundreds of thousands of small investors, and nearly all retail analysts and business journalists, by surprise. In November 2009, it was announced that [[Marc Bolland]], formerly of [[Morrisons]],{{Cite news|author1=Zoe Wood |author2=Julia Finch |lastauthoramp=yes |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2009/nov/22/bolland-marks-spencer-problems |title=A new face, but the same old problems at Marks & Spencer |work=The Guardian |location=UK |date= 22 November 2009|accessdate=18 April 2011}} would take over as chief executive from executive chairman [[Stuart Rose]] in early 2010; Rose remained in the role of non-executive chairman until he was replaced by Robert Swannell in January 2011.{{Cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2009/nov/18/marc-bolland-marks-spencer|title=Marc Bolland appointed as chief executive of Marks & Spencer| last=Wearden |first=Graeme |date=18 November 2009 |work=The Guardian |location=London |accessdate=18 November 2009}}{{Cite news |url=http://www.ft.com/cms/s/0/8d85cb20-d438-11de-990c-00144feabdc0.html |title=M&S names Bolland as new chief|last=Stafford|first=Philip|date=18 November 2009 |work=Financial Times |accessdate=18 November 2009 |location=London}} M&S have 959 stores throughout the UK, as well as many international stores; 58 stores in [[India]], 48 stores in [[Turkey]], 37 in [[Russia]], 27 in [[Greece]], 17 in [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]], 14 in [[France]], 11 in [[Poland]], 6 in [[Hungary]] and [[Finland]] and 5 in [[Spain]]. In recent years its clothing sales have fallen whilst food sales have increased after the axing of [[St Michael (brand)|"St. Michael's"]] naming for their own brand. ==History== ===Establishment=== [[File:Marks & Spencer, Briggate, Leeds.jpg|thumb|Marks and Spencer on [[Briggate, Leeds|Briggate]] not far from their original branch in [[Leeds]].]] The company was founded by a partnership between [[Michael Marks]], a [[History of the Jews in Poland|Polish Jew]]{{cite web|url=http://www.bournemouth.ac.uk/facilitiesandresources/diversity/events/documents/multiculturalism_poster_m_s.pdf |title=Marks and Spencer – a Great British institution. |publisher=[[Bournemouth University]] |accessdate=4 December 2012 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130509144611/http://www.bournemouth.ac.uk/facilitiesandresources/diversity/events/documents/multiculturalism_poster_m_s.pdf |archivedate=9 May 2013 |df= }}{{harvtxt|Paul Burns|2008|pp=}} from [[Słonim]] (Marks was born into a Polish-Jewish family, a Polish refugee living in the Russian Empire, now in [[Belarus]]), and [[Thomas Spencer (Marks and Spencer)|Thomas Spencer]], a cashier from the English market town of [[Skipton]] in [[North Yorkshire]].{{cite web|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/dna/h2g2/A43825629 |title=The History of Marks and Spencer |publisher=BBC News |accessdate=18 April 2011}}{{cite web|url=http://theskiptonpress.co.uk/skiptons-illustrious-citizen-thomas-spencer-co-founder-marks-spencer/|title=Skipton’s Most Illustrious Citizen: Thomas Spencer, Co-Founder Of Marks & Spencer|publisher=Skipton Press|accessdate=25 February 2017}} On his arrival in England, Marks worked for a company in Leeds, called Barran, which employed refugees (see [[Sir John Barran, 1st Baronet]]). In 1884 he met Isaac Jowitt Dewhirst while looking for work. Dewhirst lent Marks £5 which he used to establish his Penny Bazaar on [[Leeds Kirkgate Market|Kirkgate Market]], in Leeds. Dewhirst also taught him a little English. Dewhirst's cashier was Tom Spencer, a bookkeeper, whose second wife, Agnes, helped improve Marks' English. In 1894, when Marks acquired a permanent stall in Leeds' covered market, he invited Spencer to become his partner.{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/gallery/2008/jul/09/marksandspencer.history|title=The history of Marks and Spencer|date=9 July 2008|publisher=The Guardian|accessdate=9 April 2017}} In 1901 Marks moved to the [[Birkenhead]] open market where he amalgamated with Spencer. The pair were allocated stall numbers 11 & 12 in the centre aisle in 1903, and there they opened the famous Penny Bazaar. The company left Birkenhead Market on 24 February 1923.{{cite web|url=http://www.upton-wirral.co.uk/wir3.php |title=Birkenhead Market Fire |work=upton-wirral.co.uk |accessdate=20 March 2015 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130427143731/http://www.upton-wirral.co.uk/wir3.php |archivedate=27 April 2013 |df=dmy }} The next few years saw Michael Marks and Tom Spencer open market stalls in many locations around the North West of England and move the original Leeds Penny Bazaar to 20, Cheetham Hill Road, [[Manchester]].{{cite web|url=http://www.spartacus.schoolnet.co.uk/BUmarks.htm |title=Spartacus: Michael Marks |publisher=Spartacus.schoolnet.co.uk |date=31 December 1907 |accessdate=18 April 2011 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605081542/http://www.spartacus.schoolnet.co.uk/BUmarks.htm |archivedate=5 June 2011 |df= }} ===Domestic growth=== [[File:Marks and Spencer shop, Bekonscot.JPG|thumb|Representation of historic store from the 1930s, [[Bekonscot]] model village, UK]] Marks and Spencer, known colloquially as "Marks and Sparks",''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' – [http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,919169,00.html "Business: Marks & Sparks Trades Up"], 28 November 1977 or "M&S", made its reputation in the early 20th century with a policy of only selling British-made goods (it started to back down from this policy in the 1990s.{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/analysis-and-features/mampss-uturns-will-the-latest-plans-last-2133453.html |title=M&S's U-turns: Will the latest plans last? |work=The Independent |location=London |accessdate=20 March 2015}}) It entered into long-term relationships with British manufacturers, and sold clothes and food under the "[[St Michael (brand)|St Michael]]" brand, which was introduced in 1928. The brand honours [[Michael Marks]]. It also accepted the return of unwanted items, giving a full cash refund if the receipt was shown, no matter how long ago the product was purchased, which was unusual for the time. M&S staff raised £5,000 to pay for a [[Supermarine Spitfire]] fighter aircraft called ''The Marksman'' in 1941.{{cite book | title = Marks in Time: 125 Years of Marks & Spencer | date = 3 September 2009 | last = Chislett | first = Helen | publisher=Weidenfeld and Nicolson | isbn = 978-0-297-85873-7 }} By 1950, virtually all goods were sold under the "St Michael" label. M&S lingerie, women's clothes and girls' school uniform were branded under the "St Margaret" label until the whole range of general merchandise became "St Michael". [[Simon Marks]], son of Michael Marks, died in 1964, after fifty-six years' service. [[Israel Sieff]], the son-in-law of Michael Marks, took over as chairman and in 1968, [[John Salisse]] became the company Director. A cautious international expansion began with the introduction of Asian food in 1974. M&S opened stores in continental Europe in 1975 and in Ireland four years later. The company put its main emphasis on quality, including a 1957 stocking size measuring system. For most of its history, it also had a reputation for offering fair value for money. When this reputation began to waver, it encountered serious difficulties. Arguably, M&S has historically been an iconic retailer of 'British Quality Goods'. The uncompromising attitude towards customer relations was summarised by the 1953 slogan: "The customer ''is'' always and completely right!" Energy efficiency was improved by the addition of thermostatically controlled refrigerators in 1963. M&S began selling [[Christmas cake]]s and [[Christmas pudding]]s in 1958. In an effort to improve the quality of their [[Swiss roll]]s, they hired the food expert Nat Goldberg, who made a major improvement across their entire cake range, which had lost the public's favour a few years earlier. As a later measure to improve food quality, food labelling was improved and "sell by dates" were phased in between 1970 and 1972. Smoking was banned from all M&S shops in 1959 because of the fire hazards it posed. In 1972, [[Marcus Sieff, Baron Sieff of Brimpton|Marcus Sieff]] became Chairman, remaining in place until 1984, and emphasising the importance of good staff relations to the tradition of the store, while extending staff benefits to areas such as restaurants and chiropody.{{cite news |url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/1323890/Lord-Sieff-of-Brimpton.html |title=Obituary - Marcus sieff |date=26 February 2001 |work=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |access-date=22 October 2014}} ===International expansion=== [[File:Central Tower Marks & Spencer 2009.jpg|thumb|A Marks & Spencer store in [[Central, Hong Kong]].]] [[File:Marks & Spencer in Times Square HK 201507.jpg|thumb|A Marks & Spencer store in [[Times Square (Hong Kong)|Times Square]], Causeway Bay, Hong Kong.]] M&S expanded into Canada in 1973, and at one point had forty seven stores across Canada. Despite various efforts to improve its image, the chain was never able to move beyond its reputation there as a stodgy retailer, one that catered primarily to senior citizens and expatriate Britons. The shops in Canada were smaller than British outlets, and did not carry the same selection. In the late 1990s, further efforts were made to modernise them and also expand the customer base. Unprofitable locations were closed. Nonetheless, the Canadian operations continued to lose money, and the last 38 shops in Canada were closed in 1999.{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbc.ca/money/story/1999/07/14/marks990714.html |title=Marks and Spencer close ahead of schedule |publisher=Canadian Broadcasting Corporation |date=10 November 2000 |accessdate=18 April 2011 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100826234315/http://www.cbc.ca/money/story/1999/07/14/marks990714.html |archivedate=26 August 2010 }} Expansion into France began with shops opening in Paris at [[Boulevard Haussmann]] and [[Lyon]] in 1975, followed by a second Paris shop at Rosny 2 in 1977. Further expansion into other French and Belgian cities followed into the 1980s. Although the Paris shops remained popular and profitable, the Western European operation as a whole did not fare as well and eighteen shops were sold in 2001.{{cite web|last=Pfanner |first=Eric |url=http://www.iht.com/articles/2001/10/18/t15_14.php |title=Galeries Lafayette buying 18 stores |work=International Herald Tribune |date=18 October 2001 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} However, in April 2011, M&S changed directions again with an announcement to reopen a store that will not only sell clothing but food as well. In addition the group will also open several food outlets throughout the French capital. The first branch opened on 24 November 2011 at the [[Champs-Élysées]] in a ceremony attended by the company's CEO [[Marc Bolland]], the model [[Rosie Huntington-Whiteley]] and the British Ambassador to France, Sir [[Peter Westmacott]].{{cite news| url=http://www.dailymail.co.uk/femail/article-2065504/Marks--Spencer-returns-France-Rosie-Huntington-Whiteley-attends-Paris-relaunch.html| location=London | work=[[Daily Mail]] | first1=Kim | last1=Willsher | title=M&S part deux: Rosie Huntington-Whiteley attends relaunch as retail chain returns to France...ten years after it left| date=25 November 2011}} The ''[[Daily Mail]]'' reported that 1,000 customers queued outside for over 2 hours at the opening of the {{convert|1400|m2|sqft|abbr=on}} store. In 1988, the company acquired [[Brooks Brothers]], an American clothing company{{cite web|url=http://www.brooksbrothers.com/aboutus/heritage3.tem |title=Brooks Brothers Heritage |publisher=Brooksbrothers.com |accessdate=18 April 2011}} and [[Kings Super Markets]], a US food chain.{{cite web|url=http://www.allbusiness.com/sector-44-45-retail-trade/clothing-clothing/1181357-1.html |title=Kings Supermarkets |publisher=Allbusiness.com |date=1 May 2006 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} In 2016 M&S expanded to sell through European marketplace [[Zalando]] on their German, French, Dutch, Belgian and Austrian sites with a range of kidswear and lingerie.{{Cite web|url=https://www.zalando.de/ms-london/|title=Marks & Spencer London Online-Shop {{!}} Marks & Spencer London versandkostenfrei bei Zalando|website=www.zalando.de|access-date=26 August 2016}} ===Financial decline=== [[File:M & S, Inverness (1998).png|thumb|M&S shop in [[Inverness]] in 1998]] M&S's profits peaked in the financial year 1997/1998. At the time it was seen as a continuing success story, but with hindsight it is considered that during Sir [[Richard Greenbury]]'s tenure as head of the company, profit margins were pushed to untenable levels, and the loyalty of its customers was seriously eroded. The rising cost of using British suppliers was also a burden, as rival retailers increasingly imported their goods from low-cost countries, but M&S's belated switch to overseas suppliers undermined a core part of its appeal to the public. Another factor was the company's refusal until 2001 to accept any credit cards except its own chargecard.{{cite web|url=http://www.ciao.co.uk/Marks_Spencer_Chargecard__Review_5001590 |title=Marks & Spencer storecard fading value |publisher=Ciao.co.uk |accessdate=18 April 2011}} These factors combined to plunge M&S into a sudden slump, which took the company, its shareholders, who included hundreds of thousands of small investors, and nearly all retail analysts and business journalists, by surprise. The company's share price fell by more than two thirds, and its profits fell from more than a billion pounds in 1997 and 1998 to £145 million in the year ended 31 March 2001.[http://www.telegraph.co.uk/money/main.jhtml?xml=/money/2008/07/02/bcnmshist102.xml Marks & Spencer: A Recent History] ''The Daily Telegraph'' Marks & Spencer launched an online shopping service in 1999.{{cite news| url=http://www.dailymail.co.uk/femail/article-17227/The-highs-lows-M-S.html | location=London | work=Daily Mail | title=The highs and lows of M&S}} In 2001, with changes in its business focus such as accepting credit cards, the introduction of the "Per Una" clothing range designed by [[George Davies (retailer)|George Davies]], and a redesign of its underlying business model, profits recovered somewhat.{{cite web|url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/newsbysector/retailandconsumer/2794432/Marks-and-Spencer-loses-Per-Una-design-director.html|title=Marks & Spencer loses Per Una design director|publisher=The Telegraph|date=7 August 2008|accessdate=9 April 2017}} In 2004, M&S was in the throes of an attempted takeover by [[Arcadia Group]] and [[British Home Stores|BHS]] boss, [[Philip Green]].{{Cite news|url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0DQA/is_2000_Feb_17/ai_59870857 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151016211356/http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0DQA/is_2000_Feb_17/ai_59870857 |dead-url=yes |archive-date=16 October 2015 |title=Green drops Marks & Spencer bid |publisher=Findarticles.com |accessdate=18 April 2011 |year=2000 }} On 12 July a recovery plan was announced which would involve selling off its financial services business [[M&S Bank|M&S Money]] to [[HSBC Bank (Europe)|HSBC Bank plc]], buying control of the ''Per Una'' range, closing the [[Gateshead]] Lifestore and stopping the expansion of its Simply Food line of shops. [[Philip Green]] withdrew his takeover bid after failing to get sufficient backing from shareholders.The book- "Marks in time" by Orionbooks.co.uk (2009) In February 2007, M&S announced the opening of the world's largest M&S shop outside the UK at [[Dubai Festival City]].{{cite web|url=http://dubai.mconet.biz/index.php?action=fullnews&id=282535&category=884&category_name= |title=Dubai Online |publisher=Dubai.mconet.biz |accessdate=7 November 2009 }}{{dead link|date=June 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} On 2 October 2008, M&S opened its first mainland China shop in [[Shanghai]]. Problems with the supply chain for the first few months of opening led Stuart Rose, M&S chairman, to describe failures in "basic shopkeeping".{{cite web|url=http://www.ft.com/cms/s/0/2bac61ae-f6e2-11dd-8a1f-0000779fd2ac.html |title=M&S admits Shanghai errors |first = Patti | last = Waldmeir |work=Financial Times |date=9 February 2009 |accessdate=19 December 2009}} ===Restructuring=== Twenty-two unprofitable and minor food stores, such as the ones at [[Ripon]] and [[Balham]], were closed in early 2009 as part of a cost cutting measure. In August 2010, it was confirmed that the [[Grantham]] branch of M&S would close, along with two other [[Lincolnshire]] branches in [[Skegness]] and [[Scunthorpe]] due to low sales in these older format stores. The closures were met with protests from the local communities and petitions were signed in support of retaining the stores, although they went ahead.BBC New Lincolnshire 25 August 2010 [http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-lincolnshire-11076135 'M&S confirms three store closures in Lincolnshire'] Retrieved 25 August 2010 The Retail Knowledge Bank conducted an audit of the company's brands in August 2010, and revealed that sales of womenswear were at a 10-year low. The audit covered both the Limited Collection, Autograph, Autograph Weekend, Classic Collection, Per Una, Portfolio and Indigo. ''Draper'' magazine claimed that Per Una was the only clothing brand not at risk of being axed while Marc Bolland considered which brands would be retained. Per Una was planned to stay due to its successful and distinctive flair, but Portfolio and Indigo were planned to go due to poor sales. Both the Limited Collection, Autograph, Autograph Weekend, Classic Collection brands were being considered for the cull during mid-2010, but were later given a reprieve.{{cite web|author=Isak Halfon, expansion director, Mango |url=http://www.just-style.com/news/bolland-review-to-streamline-ms-clothing-brands_id108648.aspx |title=UK: Bolland review to streamline M&S clothing brands?: Apparel and textile news & analysis |publisher=Just-style.com |date=17 August 2010 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} On 9 November 2010, chief executive Marc Bolland revealed plans to strengthen the company’s overall brand image and targeting sales of between £800m and £1bn for which company will increase capital expenditure to £850m to £900m over the next three years to fund the plans.{{Cite news| url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSLDE6A70V420101109 |agency=Reuters | first=Mark | last=Potter | title=UPDATE 5-Marks & Spencer's new CEO lifts investment | date=9 November 2010}} The plan also involved the discontinuation of its 'Portfolio' fashion brand and the sale of electrical products. The company also announced a new marketing strapline, 'Only at M&S', and that it would revamp its website.{{cite web|title=M&S plans £900m capital expenditure to boost sales|url=http://www.newstatesman.com/economy/2010/11/sales-plans-1bn-operations|work=2010 plans for expansion|accessdate=11 November 2010}} Bolland ordered a new store design in May 2011, and it was announced that the company would spend around £600 million between 2011 and 2014 on its UK stores, involving the launch of a range of different store formats based on the age, affluence and demographics of people in those areas. The design also included the trial of a new in-store "navigation scheme", which followed research showing that shoppers found M&S store layouts confusing and "difficult to shop [in]". It also confirmed that the amount of money-off promotions and deals offered would be increased, and that it would replace the Marks & Spencer label on clothing with "M&S Woman" and "M&S Man".{{cite news| url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/newsbysector/retailandconsumer/8534666/2bn-Marks-and-Spencer-makeover-less-than-inspiring.html | title=£2bn Marks & Spencer makeover 'less than inspiring'|date=25 May 2011|work=The Daily Telegraph|accessdate=25 March 2012|first=James|last=Hall|location=London}} By 2013, M&S's clothing division had an 11% market share in the UK.{{cite news|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-22605609 |title=Marks and Spencer profits fall as clothing disappoints |publisher=BBC News |date=21 May 2013 |accessdate=22 July 2013}}{{cite news|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-22546823 |title=M&S tries to boost sales with new clothing range |publisher=BBC News |date=15 May 2013 |accessdate=22 July 2013}}{{cite news|author=Emma Simpson |url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-22533986 |title=M&S tries to lure back shoppers with new fashion ranges |publisher=BBC News |date=14 May 2013 |accessdate=22 July 2013}} In May 2013 saw the launch of the ''Best of British'' range as well as the overhaul of ''Per Una'' and ''Indigo''.{{cite web |url=http://www.mirror.co.uk/money/city-news/marks-spencer-fashion-launch-slick-1889943 |title=Marks and Spencer fashion launch was slick but what matters is what core customers think |work=Daily Mirror |author=Hiscott, Graham |date=15 May 2013 |accessdate=22 July 2013}} Patrick Bousquet-Chavanne became the new marketing director, succeeding Steven Sharp in July. Mark Bolland also vowed to bring "quality and style back" M&S also stated it intended to increase its number of UK suppliers from the 20 it had at the time. In November 2013, it was revealed that Bill Adderley, founder of homeware chain [[Dunelm Group]], had amassed a £250m stake in M&S over the past 18 months. This disclosure was made as stock market rules mean that any holding over 3 per cent share must be made public.{{cite web|url=http://www.yorkshireeveningpost.co.uk/news/business-news/business-headlines/yorkshire-retail-entrepreneur-builds-up-250m-stake-in-m-s-1-6212162|title=Yorkshire retail entrepreneur builds up £250m stake in M&S|publisher=Yorkshire Evening Post|accessdate=12 March 2014}} On 7 January 2016 it was announced that [[Marc Bolland]], who has been CEO since 2010 would step down on 2 April 2016, and be replaced by [[Steve Rowe (businessman)|Steve Rowe]], head of clothing, and previously head of the food business.{{cite news|last1=Butler|first1=Sarah|last2=Kollewe|first2=Julia|title=M&S boss Marc Bolland to step down|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2016/jan/07/ms-boss-marc-bolland-to-step-down|accessdate=7 January 2016|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=7 January 2016}} ===2015 / 2016 store cull=== Stores identified for closure in July 2015 included [[Woolwich]], [[Walsall]], [[Erdington]], [[Aldershot]] (which was there since 1922), [[Pontypridd]] in Wales, [[Hounslow]] in west London, and [[Royal Quays]] in [[North Shields]], the three full-line stores in [[Stevenage]], [[Wood Green]] in north London, and The Fort shopping park in [[Castle Bromwich]] and the Simply Food in Castle Bromwich.{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2015/jul/29/marks-spencer-local-anger-confirming-store-closures-nine-shops|title=Marks & Spencer triggers local anger after confirming store closures|first=Graham|last=Ruddick|date=29 July 2015|publisher=|via=The Guardian}}{{cite web|url=http://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/11252488.UPDATE__Woolwich_M_S_to_close__with_Lewisham_store_losing_a_floor/|title=UPDATE: Woolwich M&S to close, with Lewisham store losing a floor|publisher=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2016/nov/08/m-and-s-marks-spencer-close-80-stores-major-overhaul|title=M&S to close 30 UK stores and cut back on clothing|first=Zoe|last=Wood|date=8 November 2016|publisher=|via=The Guardian}} The [[Lewisham]] store also lost a floor. The closures in 2015 also included three traditional food and clothing shops, one Simply Food store and four Outlet stores that sell end-of-season clothing. Some 430 workers were affected by the closures. The cull cost up to £200m to implement; the closure included loss-making stores in European markets such as France, Belgium and the Netherlands as well as outposts in China. ==Corporate affairs== ===Head office locations=== [[File:Paddington Waterside geograph-2790569-by-Colin-Smith.jpg|thumb|Waterside House, 35 North Wharf Road, London]] The headquarters of M&S was for a hundred years at Michael House, [[55 Baker Street]], London. In 2004 the company moved to a new headquarters designed by [[Michel Mossessian|mossessian & partners]] at Waterside House, in the new [[Paddington Basin]], London.{{cite web|url=http://www.marksandspencer.com/gp/node/n/46005031 |title=Paddington Basin registered business address |publisher=Marks & Spencer |accessdate=18 April 2011}} As well as the main offices in London, there are a number of other head office sites across the UK; Stockley Park (IT Services), [[Salford Quays]] and [[Spinningfields]], Greater Manchester (Marks & Spencer Shared Services Ltd. which provides human resources, and finance administration)"[http://www.marksandspencer.com/gp/node/n/45867031/026-7667460-4435653?ie=UTF8&mnSBrand=core Shared Services Recruitment Page]". Company Website{{cite web|url=http://www.liveherenw.co.uk/working/man/sha.asp |title=Living and Working in the North West – Working in Manchester: Shared Services |publisher=Liveherenw.co.uk |accessdate=18 April 2011 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090213163329/http://www.liveherenw.co.uk/working/man/sha.asp |archivedate=13 February 2009 |df= }} and [[Chester]] (HSBC's M&S Money and Retail Customer Services).{{cite web|url=http://www.lexdon.com/article/HSBC_and_Marks_&_Spencer/92.html |title=Lexdon Business Library – HSBC and Marks & Spencer complete the sale of M&S Money |publisher=Lexdon.com |accessdate=18 April 2011}} The company has overseas sourcing offices in Malaysia, Hong Kong, Thailand, India, Bangladesh, Turkey, China, Italy, Indonesia and Sri Lanka.[http://english.people.com.cn/200509/29/eng20050929_211522.html UK's leading retailer launches Asian Sourcing Office in Hong Kong] English People. 29 September 2005 ===Financial performance=== M&S is listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]] and is a constituent of the [[FTSE 100 Index]]. Financial performance has been as follows: ''Until 1999 M&S's financial year ended on 31 March. Since then, the company has changed to reporting for 52- or 53-week periods, ending on variable dates.''

Chief executive Marc Bolland described the current market as "challenging". ===Social and environmental policy=== ===="Look Behind the Label"==== In 2006, the ''Look Behind the Label'' marketing campaign was introduced."[http://www.paddingtonwaterside.co.uk/timeforpaddington/ti_news_detail.asp?newsID=63 M&S launches new ‘Look behind the label' campaign] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928024224/http://www.paddingtonwaterside.co.uk/timeforpaddington/ti_news_detail.asp?newsID=63 |date=28 September 2007 }}". Paddington Waterside Partnership – 21 February 2006 The aim of this campaign was to highlight to customers the various ethical and environmentally friendly aspects of the production and sourcing methods engaged in by M&S including: [[Fairtrade]] products, [[sustainable fishing]] and environmentally friendly textile dyes. All coffee and tea sold in M&S stores is now Fairtrade."[http://www.foodnavigator.com/news/ng.asp?id=66333-marks-spencer-fairtrade-coffee Marks & Spencer dives into ethical consumer market]" Fletcher, Anthony – 10 March 2006 – Food Navigator.com (Europe) In addition, the company offers clothing lines made from Fairtrade cotton in selected departments."[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/business/4660410.stm M&S set to launch Fairtrade range]". BBC News Online – 30 January 2006 At Christmas, the company introduces a range of food products to support the housing charity [[Shelter (charity)|Shelter]]."[http://england.shelter.org.uk/howtohelp/howtohelp-682.cfm Marks & Spencer raises money for Shelter this Christmas]" (dead link) ===="Plan A"==== [[File:MarksAndSpencerBirmingham.jpg|thumb|M&S store on [[Birmingham]] High Street]] On 15 January 2007, M&S launched an initiative, known as "Plan A",{{cite web|url=http://plana.marksandspencer.com/ |title=Plan A |publisher=Plana.marksandspencer.com |accessdate=18 April 2011}} to dramatically increase the environmental [[sustainability]] of the business within 5 years and expected to cost £200 million.{{Cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/business/6261939.stm |title=Business | M&S unveils carbon-neutral target |publisher=BBC News |date=15 January 2007 |accessdate=7 November 2009}} The plan covers "100 commitments over 5 years to address the key social and environmental challenges facing M&S today and in the future" with the tag-line "Because there is no Plan B". The commitments span five themes: [[climate change]], [[waste]], sustainable raw materials, 'fair partnership' and health, with the aim that, by 2012, it will:[http://plana.marksandspencer.com/index.php?action=PublicPillarDisplay Marks & Spencer: Plan A – The Five Pillars], Marks & Spencer * Become carbon neutral * Send no waste to landfill * Extend sustainable sourcing * Help improve the lives of people in their supply chain * Help customers and employees live a healthier life-style Despite an 18% fall in the share price in January 2008, following publication of their latest [[trading statement]], the company confirmed that they would be continuing with the plan, saying that there were 'compelling commercial — as well as moral — reasons to do so'.[https://web.archive.org/web/20081206094008/http://www.hbrgreen.org/2008/03/the_hard_economics_of_green.html?cm_mmc=npv-_-listserv-_-MAR_2008-_-HBRGreen0305 The hard economics of green], [[Harvard Business Review]], [[Stuart Rose|Sir Stuart Rose]], published 4 March 2008 M&S introduced a reusable [[Hessian (cloth)|hessian]] bag in 2007 as part of the plan, aiming to reduce the number of plastic bags used within five years. This was followed in May 2008 by the introduction of a 5p charge for standard sized carrier bags used for food purchases (before this charge became compulsory).{{Cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/uk/7268283.stm |title=M&S to charge 5p for plastic bags |publisher=BBC News |date=28 February 2008 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} All profits from the sale of food
