However, as of 2012 the store has now been fully refurbished with the so-called "Light Touch" re-fit.]] M&S core shops typically feature a selection of the company's clothing ranges and an M&S [[food hall]]. The range of clothing sold and the space given to it depends on the location and customer demographic (an example would be that some London shops do not stock the Classic Collection, but stock Limited Collection and a full Autograph range). Most core shops feature a Food hall. ====New store format==== A new store format designed by Urban Salon Architects was introduced in 2009.{{Cite news|url=http://news.independent.co.uk/uk/this_britain/article2586665.ece |title=Marks and sparks: Shopping in the 21st century |work=The Independent |location=UK |date=27 May 2007 |accessdate=7 November 2009 |first=Paul |last=Rodgers |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080118145633/http://news.independent.co.uk/uk/this_britain/article2586665.ece |archivedate=18 January 2008 |df= }} ===M&S Foodhall=== [[File:M&S Food Hall, SUTTON, Surrey, Greater London.jpg|thumb|An M&S Food Hall in the [[Sutton, London]] branch]] All the '''St Michael Food hall''' supermarkets were renamed ''M&S Food hall'' when Marks & Spencer dropped the ''St Michael'' brand in 2000. Each M&S Foodhall sells groceries, which are all under the Marks & Spencer brand. However, in 2009 the company began selling a limited range of other brands, such as [[Coca-Cola]] and [[Stella Artois]], without reducing the number of M&S goods they sold. This marked the first time in its 125-year history that Marks & Spencer had sold any brands other than its own.{{Cite news|url= http://www.brandrepublic.com/News/950570/M-S-sell-brands-first-time-125-years/|title= M&S to sell other brands for the first time in 125 years|publisher=Brand Republic|first= James|last= Quilfer|date= 4 November 2009|accessdate=22 November 2009}} M&S introduced [[self check-out]] tills in the food-halls of a small number of trial stores in 2002. Self check-out was implemented in the general merchandise sections in three trial stores in 2006.[http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_hb5245/is_200209/ai_n19869452 M&S to test self-scan tills]{{dead link|date=April 2011}} ===Hospitality=== Many large shops, such as Lisburn Sprucefield, [[Westfield London|Westfield, White City]], Cribbs Causeway and [[Newcastle-upon-Tyne]], also offer other hospitality outlets, such as a modern ''Deli Bar'' (champagne, canapés, seafood), ''Restaurant'' (table service—the first of which was opened in Newcastle) ''M&S Kitchen'' (traditional home cooking & lunches) or ''Hot Food To Go'' (burgers, chips, soups). Many of these outlets are run in conjunction with [[Compass Group]] under franchise arrangements.{{cite web|url=http://www.catererandhotelkeeper.co.uk/articles/19/4/2013/348189/compass-group-signs-m-s-franchise-agreement.htm|title=Compass Group signs M&S franchise agreement|publisher=Caterer and Hotelkeeper|date=19 April 2013|accessdate=12 March 2014}} ===Home stores=== In 2007, M&S announced that new, dedicated shops for home furnishings were to be launched. Shops have now been opened in [[Cheltenham]] in Gloucestershire, [[Tunbridge Wells]] in Kent, [[Lisburn]] Sprucefield in Northern Ireland[http://www.retail-week.com/Stores/theres_no_place_like_home.html There is no place like home] Retail Week and in the Barton Square section of [[Trafford Centre|The Trafford Centre]], Manchester.{{cite web|url=http://www.shopping-centre.co.uk/news/fullstory.php/aid/2591/Trafford_extends_Barton_Square_homewares_offer.html |title=Trafford extends Barton Square homewares offer |publisher=Shopping-centre.co.uk |date=19 May 2008 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} ===Outlet stores=== As of 2010, M&S have 50 outlet stores and growth expansion plans for future.{{cite web|url=http://annualreport.marksandspencer.com/about/uk-international.aspx |title=Annual Report 2009 |year=2009 |publisher=Marks & Spencer |accessdate=25 September 2009 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090723122137/http://annualreport.marksandspencer.com/about/uk-international.aspx |archivedate=23 July 2009 }} The Outlet division offers M&S products with the majority of them discounting at least 30% from the original selling price.{{cite web|url=http://www2.marksandspencer.com/thecompany/our_stores/outlet.shtml |title=Outlet |publisher=Marks and Spencer |accessdate=18 April 2011 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110714041208/http://www2.marksandspencer.com/thecompany/our_stores/outlet.shtml |archivedate=14 July 2011 |df= }} The first of these stores opened at [[Ashford, Kent|Ashford]] in Kent in 2000. Many of the Outlet shops are in locations such as retail parks and outlet centres, though some, including the shop in [[Woolwich]], South London{{cite web|url=http://www.misterwhat.co.uk/company/146221-marks-spencer-outlet-london |title=Woolwich outlet from |publisher=MisterWhat |date=12 May 2014}} and [[Newton Abbot]], Devon were previously main M&S shops which converted to the Outlet format. Meadow Bank Outlet Store in Edinburgh became the model for all the Marks and Spencer Outlet shop in the early months of 2010. There are now also stores which combine a mainline M&S store and an Outlet store to create a store which offers both the main current full-price M&S ranges and the discounted Outlet ranges: one such store is at the [[Lewisham Shopping Centre]], where the previously closed upper level of the M&S store was reopened in January 2009 as an Outlet format sub-store;{{cite web|url=http://www.lewishamcentre.co.uk/stores/atozofstores/20314.aspx |title=M&S Outlet on Lewisham Shopping Centre website |publisher=Lewishamcentre.co.uk |accessdate=18 April 2011}} ===M&S Simply Food=== [[File:Marks and Spencer, Banstead, Surrey - geograph.org.uk - 339773.jpg|thumb|M&S Simply Food in [[Banstead]], Surrey]] [[File:M&S Food to Go, SUTTON, Surrey, Greater London.jpg|thumb|An M&S Food to Go store in Sutton station, [[Sutton, London]]]] M&S launched a convenience format, branded ''Simply Food'' in 2001, with the first stores opening in [[Twickenham]] and [[Surbiton]]. The stores predominantly sell food but also carry a small selection of general merchandise.{{cite news|last1=Finch|first1=Julia|title=Simply Food to triple in size with restaurant plan|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2006/nov/08/marksspencer.supermarkets|accessdate=20 January 2015|work=The Guardian|date=8 November 2006}} A number of these are run under [[franchising|franchise]] agreements: * [[SSP Group]] runs the stores at mainline railway stations and airports.[http://www.ssp-intl.com/SSPInternet/Content/Brands/National.htm Select Service Partner]. Company Website * [[Moto Hospitality|Moto]] has stores at 37 of its motorway service stations.[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/business/6136684.stm Perils of the motorway pit stops] May, Maurice — BBC News Online – 10 November 2006 * [[BP]] has over 120 petrol stations with ''Simply Food'' offerings.{{cite web|url=http://www.bp.com/retail/sectiongenericarticle.do?categoryId=9036797&contentId=7067920|title=M&S Simply Food at BP Connect|accessdate=9 July 2011}} Orders from M&S accounted for more than half of [[Uniq plc|Uniq]]'s food product supplies to UK retailers in 2010 after several years service as a major M&S food product supplier.{{cite web|url=http://www.foodmanufacture.co.uk/Business-News/Uniq-Brands-will-drive-footfall-at-M-S-but-not-in-the-desserts-fixture |title=Uniq: Brands will drive footfall at M&S, but not in the desserts fixture |publisher=Foodmanufacture.co.uk |date=23 July 2010 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} In 2011 it was noted that M&S were operating [[express pricing]]; i.e., charging more in their Simply Food branches than in regular branches. A spokesperson stated that "prices are a little higher than at our high street stores but this reflects the fact that these stores are open longer and are highly convenient for customers on the move".{{cite web|url=http://www.confused.com/money/articles/mystery-shop-how-much-more-do-you-pay-in-m-s-simply-food#ixzz2V8aHbrYr|title=Mystery shop: How much do you pay in M&S Simply Food?|publisher=[[Confused.com]]|accessdate=3 June 2013}} The Simply Food brand has been phased out in all stand-alone larger stores since the rebrand in 2015 and the stores have now been branded as "M&S Foodhall."{{Cite news|url=http://www.bathchronicle.co.uk/marks-spencer-open-m-s-foodhall-bath/story-28652896-detail/story.html|title=Marks & Spencer to open an M&S Foodhall in Bath|date=2 February 2016|work=Bath Chronicle|access-date=21 March 2017|language=en}} ===Online services=== Products could be ordered online since the mid-2000s, in response to [[Tesco]] launching their pioneering [[Tesco.com]] home shopping delivery service in the early 2000s. Both Tesco, M&S and others are expanding rapidly into this new niche market.{{Cite news|url=http://www.bbc.com/news/business-39743611|title=M&S online food delivery service will be no piece of cake|last=Plummer|first=Robert|date=28 April 2017|work=BBC News|access-date=5 May 2017|language=en-GB}} The online flower service was accused of unfair trading and using [[Google]] to piggy-back advertise on online searches aimed at [[Interflora]] online in 2010.{{Cite news| url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-11531677 |publisher=BBC News | title=Interflora sues Marks & Spencer over Google ad links | date=13 October 2010}} The [[John Lewis (department store)|John Lewis]] shopping chain beat M&S to the title of the UK's best high-street website by late 2010.{{cite web|last=Bold |first=Ben |url=http://www.marketingmagazine.co.uk/channel/DigitalMedia/article/1035596/John-Lewis-beats-M-S-UKs-best-high-street-website/ |title=John Lewis beats M&S as UK's best high-street website |work=Marketing magazine |date=19 October 2010 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} As of May 2013, the Republic of Ireland now handles more than 50% of online trade. ==Product line history== {{Main article|List of Marks & Spencer brands}} [[File:PercyPigs.jpeg|thumb|Marks & Spencer Percy Pigs]] The company's ranges include clothing for men, woman and children, as well as home products and food.{{Cite web|url=http://www.marksandspencer.com/|title=Welcome to Marks & Spencer|website=www.marksandspencer.com|language=en|access-date=5 May 2017}} Within these ranges, M&S use a number of own brands, such as those used within its womenswear division, including Indigo Collection Junior, Indigo Collection and Portfolio. Indigo Collection is aimed at women over 30s, while Portfolio is aimed at those aged over 45. By 2010, M&S had 10 sub-brands within womenswear and 6 sub-brands within menswear, following a reduction in brands.{{Cite news| url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/newsbysector/retailandconsumer/8098977/MandS-plans-to-take-Twiggy-international.html | location=London | work=The Daily Telegraph | first=James | last=Hall | title=M&S plans to take Twiggy international | date=30 October 2010}} Marks & Spencer were selling clothes under the ''St Margaret'' and ''St Michael'' label by the mid-1950s and launched their [[school uniforms]] in the early 1950s, but would be scrapped in the early 2000s as part of the corporate modernisation plan. Within Marks & Spencer's food ranges, it first pioneered boil-in-the-bag and sachet meals in 1972. The company also sells main meals, lunches, sweets and other savoury items. It launched its "[[Percy Pig]]s" sweets in 1995,{{Cite news| url=https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/food-and-drink/features/high-on-the-hog-how-percy-pig-came-to-dominate-the-sweetie-market-and-win-the-nations-hearts-1989583.html | location=London | work=The Independent | date=6 June 2010 | title=High on the hog: How Percy Pig came to dominate the sweetie market, and win the nation's hearts}} and the billionth "Percy Pig" sweet was sold by October 2007. M&S also has an extensive wine and beer range,{{cite web|url=http://www.marksandspencer.com/Wine-Food-Wine/b/44092030?ie=UTF8&intid=gnav_food-wine_wine |title=Wine : Food & Wine |publisher=Marks & Spencer |accessdate=7 November 2009}} which was first started in 1973. In 2006 and 2007, M&S entered over a hundred of its own wines into two wine competitions, ''[[Decanter (magazine)|The Decanter World Wine Awards]]'' and the International Wine Challenge. Both years, almost every wine won an award, ranging from the 2005 Secano Pinot Noir, Leyda Valley, Chile (Best Pinot Noir in the world for under £10) to the Rosada Cava (Commended).{{cite web|url=http://www.decanter.com/worldwineawards/2007/dwwa_search.php?rsearch=M%26S |title=Decanter World Wine Awards 2007 |publisher=Decanter.com |accessdate=18 April 2011}}'' M&S's relatively successful interior design 'Home' brand was launched in 2005 and featured products like vases, furniture and beds. The children's online only 'Living the Dream' range of [[Lewis Hamilton]] and [[Heikki Kovalainen]] memorabilia and merchandise was launched in September 2009.{{cite web|url=http://www.lewishamilton.com/news/2009/09/mandslaunch09 |title=Pit-stop press! M&S launches 'Living the Dream' boyswear collection |publisher=Lewis Hamilton.com |date=17 September 2009 |accessdate=18 April 2011 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713203035/http://www.lewishamilton.com/news/2009/09/mandslaunch09 |archivedate=13 July 2011 |df= }}{{cite web|url=http://www.lewishamilton.com/news/2009/09/mandswestfields09 |title=News : Lewis, Heikki and M&S take over Westfields in London |publisher=Lewis Hamilton.com |date=19 September 2009 |accessdate=18 April 2011 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713203115/http://www.lewishamilton.com/news/2009/09/mandswestfields09 |archivedate=13 July 2011 |df= }} Merchandise also relating to fellow racing driver [[Jenson Button]] was added to the range during April 2010.{{cite web|last=Thomas |first=Joe |url=http://www.marketingmagazine.co.uk/news/rss/995553/M-S-supports-clothing-range-Lewis-Hamilton-Jenson-Button/ |title=M&S supports clothing range with Lewis Hamilton and Jenson Button |work=Marketing magazine |date=8 April 2010 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} M&S launched its "Plus Fit" range for overweight children in selected stores in July 2010. It has proven to be a popular line.{{cite web|url=http://www.thefamilygp.com/M-and-S-trials-plus-fit-schoolwear-for-overweight-children.htm |title=M&S launches school-wear for obese kids, sells out |publisher=Thefamilygp.com |accessdate=18 April 2011}} ===Per Una=== [[File:Women peruna.jpg|thumb|Per Una's logo, three hearts]] "Per Una" was launched on 28 September 2001 as a joint venture between M&S and [[Next plc|Next]] founder [[George Davies (retailer)|George Davies]] with the contribution of Julie Strang. The ''Per Una'' brand has been a major success for the company,{{Cite news |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/business/4329412.stm |title=M&S sales rise but Davies resigns |date=11 October 2005 |accessdate=4 April 2011 |publisher=BBC News }} and in October 2004, M&S bought the brand in a £125 million, two-year service contract with George Davies.{{Cite news |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/business/3715654.stm |title=M&S completes Per Una purchase |date=5 October 2004 |accessdate=4 April 2011 |publisher=BBC News }} Mr Davies was to stay on for at least two years to run the company, with 12 months notice required if he wished to leave. ===Old labels=== The "St Michael" brand was introduced by Simon Marks in 1928 in honour of his father and co-founder of Marks & Spencer, [[Michael Marks]]. By 1950, virtually all goods were sold under the St Michael brand. M&S lingerie, women's clothing and girls' uniform were branded under the ''St Margaret'' brand, until the whole range of general merchandise became St Michael. The synthetic fibre Tricell was first used in 1957 and lasted until the 1970s. and another synthetic fibre called Courtelle was first launched, nationally, by Marks & Spencer during 1960 and also lasted well into the 1970s. Machine washable wool first appeared in 1972 and [[Lycra]] hosiery first came in during 1986. M&S launched their own brands of domestic products, such as [[washing powder]] and [[aluminium foil]] in 1972, under the brand name of 'House-care'. The 1996–1997 'Orient Express Tagged' brand was the first of numerous new brands, most of which were in feminine and children's clothes. The 'Orient Express Tagged' brand was part of the inspiration behind the 'Portfolio' brand. The men's Autograph brand was then launched in 2000 and continues to this day.{{cite web|url=http://www.marksandspencer.com/c/men/autograph |title=Autograph |publisher=Marks & Spencer |accessdate=19 January 2015}} In 2004, Sir Stuart Rose axed a number of brands including the menswear brand "SP Clothing", the "View From" sportswear range, the [[David Beckham]] children's range "DB07" and several food lines as he thought the company's stock inventory management had become 'too complicated'.{{cite web|author=David Birnbaum |url=http://www.just-style.com/analysis/sir-stuart-hands-over-golden-baton_id108297.aspx |title=Sir Stuart hands over golden baton: Apparel and textile news & analysis |publisher=Just-style.com |accessdate=18 April 2011}} A version of Per Una aimed at teenagers, "Per Una Due", was also discontinued, despite having launched earlier in the year, due to poor sales.{{Cite news |last=Craven |first=Neil |date=15 August 2010 |accessdate=4 April 2011 |title=M&S clothing brands set for overhaul |url=http://www.thisismoney.co.uk/news/article.html?in_article_id=512068&in_page_id=2 |work=This is Money}}{{Cite news| url=http://www.dailymail.co.uk/money/article-1303143/Bollands-bonfire-M-S-brands.html |location=London |work=Daily Mail | first=Neil | last=Craven | title=Bolland's bonfire of the M&S brands | date=16 August 2010}}{{Cite news|last=Hayes |first=David |date=7 February 2004 |accessdate=4 April 2011 |url=http://www.thisislondon.co.uk/news/article-11737114-ms-and-teenage-frills.do |archive-url=https://archive.is/20130421120827/http://www.thisislondon.co.uk/news/article-11737114-ms-and-teenage-frills.do |dead-url=yes |archive-date=21 April 2013 |title=M&S and teenage frills |work=[[Evening Standard]] |location=London }} The company also began to sell branded goods like [[Kellogg's Corn Flakes]] in November 2008. Following a review by Marc Bolland in 2011, M&S confirmed it would begin to reduce the number of branded items on sale, instead offering only those that it did not have an M&S alternative for.{{Cite news| url=http://www.ausfoodnews.com.au/2010/10/19/marks-and-spencer-may-cut-sales-of-name-brands.html|title=Marks and Spencer may cut sales of name brands|publisher=Food News|date=19 October 2010|accessdate=25 March 2012 }} ==Marketing== ===New logo=== [[File:Marks & Spencer corporate logo.svg|thumbnail|The older logo, used from 2000 to 2007]] During the height of the company's troubles at the beginning of the 21st century, the ''St Michael'' brand used as the selling label for all M&S products was discontinued in favour of ''Marks & Spencer'' and a new logo in the [[Optima]] typeface was introduced and began to appear in place of ''St Michael'' on product packaging. The same logo was also applied to store fascias and carrier bags. The ''St Michael'' name was subsequently adopted as a 'quality guarantee' and appeared as the ''St Michael Quality Promise'' on the back of food products, on the side of delivery vehicles and on in-store ordering receipts. This has since been phased out, although receipts for made-to-order furniture still feature this 'seal of approval' on the bottom. ===Your M&S=== [[File:Your M&S logo.svg|thumb|''Your M&S'' promotional logo 2004–2014.]] When Steve Sharp joined as marketing director in 2004, after being hired by new Chief Executive Sir Stuart Rose, he introduced a new promotional brand under the ''Your M&S'' banner, with a corresponding logo."[https://www.theguardian.com/marks/story/0,,1804124,00.html Steve Sharp: Shy marketing whizz creating sparks at Marks]". Martinson, Jane – ''The Guardian'', 23 June 2006 ===High-profile media campaigns=== [[File:Marks & Spencer new logo.svg|thumbnail|Logo 2007-2015]] M&S has always run newspaper and/or Magazine ads since the early 1950s, but the introduction of some famous stars such as [[Twiggy]]{{Cite news|url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/tvandradio/6636506/Supermodel-Erin-OConnor-told-to-have-cosmetic-surgery.html |title=Supermodel Erin O’Connor told to have cosmetic surgery |work=The Daily Telegraph |date=24 November 2009 |accessdate=19 December 2009 | location=London | first=Urmee | last=Khan}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/video/2009/may/15/marks-spencer-anniversary-ad |title=Video: Watch Twiggy in Marks & Spencer's 125th birthday ad |work=The Guardian |location=UK |date= 18 May 2009|accessdate=19 December 2009 }} and [[David Jason]] in various TV ads has helped raise the company's profile. Twiggy first appeared in 1967, returning later in 1995 and 2005. Anne Grierson first featured in adverts during the late 1950s and most of the 1960s. In later years, [[Erin O'Connor]], [[Myleene Klass]], Tanja Nadjila, Peter Kay, [[David Beckham]], [[Antonio Banderas]], [[Claudia Schiffer]], [[Helena Christensen]], [[Tatjana Patitz]], [[Lisa Snowdon]], [[Dannii Minogue]], [[V V Brown]] and [[Carmen Kass]] have also featured in a few ads, along with many others. [[John Sergeant (journalist)|John Sergeant]], David Jason and [[Joanna Lumley]] have either appeared in or voiced over adverts since 2008. The new look has been instrumental in the company's recent resurgence, particularly with the success of a new clothing campaign featuring the celebrated model, [[Twiggy]], and younger models associated with the [[Boho-chic#The influence of boho|bohemian]] styles of 2005–6, and the new TV ad campaign for its food range. These adverts have the tag-line "This is not just food, this is M&S food" and feature slow motion, close-up footage of various food products, described in a sultry [[voice-over]] by [[Dervla Kirwan]], to an enticing instrumental song — most notably Fleetwood Mac's "[[Albatross (instrumental)|Albatross]]" as well as [[Santana (band)|Santana]]'s "[[Samba Pa Ti (instrumental)|Samba Pa Ti]]", [[Olly Murs]]' "[[Busy (Olly Murs song)|Busy]]", [[Groove Armada]]'s "[[At the River]]" or [[Spandau Ballet]]'s "[[True (Spandau Ballet song)|True]]". These adverts have been referred to by both fans and critics as being ''[[food porn]]'', with a number of other companies copying the idea, such as [[Aldi]] and, most recently, [[Waitrose]].{{Cite news|author=Kollewe, Julia |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2008/jul/04/marksspencer |title=Food porn for every hedonist in the world |work=The Guardian |location=London |date= 4 July 2008|accessdate=18 April 2011}} The 2009 TV advertising campaign drew complaints, leading to national press coverage, regarding sexism.{{cite news |url=http://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/news/local-national/sexism-complaints-over-marks-and-spencer-christmas-ad-14566626.html |title=Sexism complaints over Marks and Spencer's Christmas ad |work=Belfast Telegraph |date=19 November 2009 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} In 2010, it was confirmed that Dannii Minogue would be one of the new faces of Marks & Spencer. She filmed her first commercial in South Africa, which featured [[Cheryl Lynn]]'s "[[Got to Be Real]]", for their Spring campaign that aired on 24 March.{{cite news| url=http://www.dailymail.co.uk/femail/article-1249431/Dannii-Minogue-announced-new-face-M-S.html | location=London | work=Daily Mail | title='I'm a very happy M&S girl': Dannii Minogue announced as new face of High Street chain | first=Maysa | last=Rawi | date=9 February 2010}} Dannii travelled to [[Miami]], Florida in January 2011 to shoot the commercial for M&S for the 2011 Spring collection, prior to her contractual termination. In August 2011, M&S announced the new faces of their campaigns would be [[Rosie Huntington-Whiteley]], [[Ryan Reynolds]] and [[David Gandy]].{{cite news|url=http://fashion.telegraph.co.uk/Article.aspx?Id=TMG8731621 |title=David Gandy and Ryan Reynolds Join Rosie Huntington-Whiteley for M&S |location=London |work=The Daily Telegraph |date=30 August 2011 |accessdate=22 July 2013 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140313062227/http://fashion.telegraph.co.uk/Article.aspx?Id=TMG8731621 |archivedate=13 March 2014 |df=dmy }} Marks & Spencer dropped a series of planned television adverts in the July 2011, featuring [[Twiggy]], [[Dannii Minogue]] and [[VV Brown]] as it started its corporate image revamp. It confirmed that Twiggy, [[Lisa Snowden]] and [[Jamie Redknapp]] would return for future advertising.{{cite news| url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/newsbysector/retailandconsumer/8643936/MandS-drops-ad-featuring-Twiggy-Minogue-and-VV-Brown.html | location=London | work=The Daily Telegraph | first=Louisa | last=Peacock | title=M&S drops ad featuring Twiggy, Minogue and VV Brown | date=18 July 2011}} On 31 March 2014, M&S launched the new iteration of its 'Leading Ladies' marketing campaign featuring figures including [[Emma Thompson]], [[Annie Lennox]], [[Rita Ora]] and [[Baroness Lawrence]].{{cite web | url = http://www.campaignlive.co.uk/news/1286622/emma-thompson-annie-lennox-rita-ora-unveiled-marks-spencer-leading-ladies/ | title = Emma Thompson, Annie Lennox and Rita Ora unveiled as Marks & Spencer 'Leading Ladies' | publisher = Campaign Live | accessdate = 25 March 2014}} ==Controversies== ===Israel=== Marks & Spencer has been criticised by pro-Palestinian activists over what they claim is its past support for [[Zionism]], and for fruit trading with Israel.{{cite web|url=http://www.boycott-israel.co.uk/business-links/133-marks-and-spencer |title=Boycott Israel Website |publisher=Boycott-israel.co.uk |date=21 September 1941 |accessdate=18 April 2011 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110911025551/http://www.boycott-israel.co.uk/business-links/133-marks-and-spencer |archivedate=11 September 2011 |df= }} A shop in [[Brighton]] was vandalised in 2004 with pro-Palestinian and anti-Zionist graffiti."[http://www.indymedia.org.uk/en/2004/10/299453.html?c=on#c103995 Brighton Activists deface Marks and Spencer store] The company states, "We deal with politicians and officials, in government and opposition. We do not support or align ourselves to political parties and make no political donations".[http://corporate.marksandspencer.com/howwedobusiness/working_with_government Working with Government] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130604154054/http://corporate.marksandspencer.com/howwedobusiness/working_with_government |date=4 June 2013 }} Marks & Spencer ===Comprehensive Spending Review=== {{see also|2010 Spending Review}} In October 2010, chairman Sir Stuart Rose was a signatory to a controversial letter to ''The Daily Telegraph''{{Cite news|author=18 October 2010 Comments |url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/comment/letters/8069609/Osbornes-cuts-will-strengthen-Britains-economy-by-allowing-the-private-sector-to-generate-more-jobs.html |title=Osborne’s cuts will strengthen Britain’s economy by allowing the private sector to generate more jobs |work=The Daily Telegraph |location=UK |date=18 October 2010 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} which claimed that "The private sector should be more than capable of generating additional jobs to replace those lost in the public sector, and the redeployment of people to more productive activities will improve economic performance, so generating more employment opportunities", despite recent job cuts of 1,000 staff.[http://business.timesonline.co.uk/tol/business/economics/article5455026.ece M&S cuts 1,000 jobs as fashion sales dive], Helen Power and Marcus Leroux, ''The Times'', 6 January 2009 {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110612031348/http://business.timesonline.co.uk/tol/business/economics/article5455026.ece |date=12 June 2011 }} This prompted calls for a boycott of Marks & Spencer and the companies represented by the other signatories to the letter.{{cite web|url=http://liberalconspiracy.org/2010/10/24/why-im-boycotting-the-35-businesses-who-support-the-cuts/ |title=Why I’m boycotting the 35 businesses who support the cuts, Kate Belgrave |publisher=Liberalconspiracy.org |date=24 October 2010 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} ===Contactless payment issues=== Some Marks & Spencer customers claim that the chain's [[contactless payment]] terminals have taken money from cards other than the ones intended for payment. Contactless cards are supposed to be within about 4 cm of the front of the terminal to work. M&S investigated the incident and confirmed the new system had been extensively tested and was robust. It had recently rolled out the contactless payments system, provided by Visa Europe, to 644 UK stores.{{cite news|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-22545804|title=Contactless 'charging errors' at Marks and Spencer|date=18 May 2013|accessdate=12 March 2014|work=BBC News}} ===Muslim checkout-staff policy=== In December 2013, Marks & Spencer announced that Muslim checkout staff in the UK could refuse to sell pork products or alcohol to customers at their till.{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/ms-says-muslim-staff-may-refuse-to-serve-customers-pork-and-alcohol-9020982.html |title=M&S says Muslim staff may refuse to serve customers pork and alcohol |work=The Independent |date=22 December 2013 |accessdate=22 December 2013 |location=London |first1=Adam |last1=Withnall |first2=Alex |last2=Delmar-Morgan}} The policy was announced after at least one news outlet reported that customers waiting with goods that included pork or alcohol were refused service, and were told by a Muslim checkout worker to wait until another till became available.{{cite news|url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/newsbysector/retailandconsumer/10532782/Muslim-staff-at-Marks-and-Spencer-can-refuse-to-sell-alcohol-and-pork.html |title=Muslim staff at Marks & Spencer can refuse to sell alcohol and pork |work=The Daily Telegraph |date=21 December 2013 |accessdate=22 December 2013 |location=London |first=Robert |last=Mendick}} The policy applied across all 703 UK M&S stores and prompted a strong backlash by customers.{{cite news |title=M&S faces furious backlash from customers over Muslim policy |url=http://uk.finance.yahoo.com/news/m-faces-furious-backlash-customers-174843463.html |work=Yahoo News |date=22 December 2013}} A company spokesman subsequently apologised and stated that they will attempt to reassign staff whose beliefs may impact their work to different departments, such as clothing.{{cite news|url=http://bbc.co.uk/news/business-25488259 |title=M&S apology over Muslim alcohol Steve Rowe {{small|(CEO)}} | revenue = [[Pound sterling|£]]10,622.0 million (2017){{cite web|url=http://annualreport.marksandspencer.com/M&S_AR2017_FinancialStatements.pdf|title=Annual Report 2017|publisher=Marks & Spencer|accessdate=18 August 2017}} | operating_income = [[Pound sterling|£]]690.6 million (2017) | net_income = [[Pound sterling|£]]115.7 million (2017) | num_employees = 84,939 (2017){{cite web|url=http://corporate.marksandspencer.com/aboutus/key-facts|title=M&S Key Facts|accessdate=9 April 2017}} | footnotes = | intl = yes | homepage = {{url|marksandspencer.com}} }} '''Marks and Spencer plc''' (also known as '''M&S''') is a major British multinational retailer headquartered in the [[City of Westminster]], London. It is listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]] and is a constituent of the [[FTSE 100 Index]]. It specialises in the selling of clothing, home products and [[Luxury good|luxury]] food products. M&S was founded in 1884 by [[Michael Marks]] and [[Thomas Spencer (Marks and Spencer)|Thomas Spencer]] in [[Leeds]].{{cite news|title=M&S launches underwear boutiques|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/986292.stm|accessdate=15 March 2017|agency=BBC|issue=Business|publisher=BBC|date=23 October 2000|location=United Kingdom|language=English}} The company also began to sell branded goods like [[Kellogg's Corn Flakes]] in November 2008.{{cite news |author=Hiscott, Graham |url=http://www.mirror.co.uk/news/city-news/2009/11/04/marks-and-spencer-to-start-selling-top-brands-115875-21796883/ |title=Marks and Spencer to start selling top brands |work=Daily Mirror |location=London |accessdate=18 April 2011}} M&S currently has 979 stores across the U.K including 615 that only sell food products.{{Cite news|url=http://www.bbc.com/news/business-39743611|title=M&S online food delivery service will be no piece of cake|last=Plummer|first=Robert|date=28 April 2017|work=BBC News|access-date=28 April 2017|language=en-GB}} In 1998, the company became the first British retailer to make a pre-tax profit of over £1 billion,{{Cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/business/96531.stm |title=Marks & Spencer profits top expectations |publisher=BBC News |date=19 May 1998 |accessdate=7 November 2009}} although subsequently it went into a sudden slump, which took the company, its shareholders, who included hundreds of thousands of small investors, and nearly all retail analysts and business journalists, by surprise. In November 2009, it was announced that [[Marc Bolland]], formerly of [[Morrisons]],{{Cite news|author1=Zoe Wood |author2=Julia Finch |lastauthoramp=yes |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2009/nov/22/bolland-marks-spencer-problems |title=A new face, but the same old problems at Marks & Spencer |work=The Guardian |location=UK |date= 22 November 2009|accessdate=18 April 2011}} would take over as chief executive from executive chairman [[Stuart Rose]] in early 2010; Rose remained in the role of non-executive chairman until he was replaced by Robert Swannell in January 2011.{{Cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2009/nov/18/marc-bolland-marks-spencer|title=Marc Bolland appointed as chief executive of Marks & Spencer| last=Wearden |first=Graeme |date=18 November 2009 |work=The Guardian |location=London |accessdate=18 November 2009}}{{Cite news |url=http://www.ft.com/cms/s/0/8d85cb20-d438-11de-990c-00144feabdc0.html |title=M&S names Bolland as new chief|last=Stafford|first=Philip|date=18 November 2009 |work=Financial Times |accessdate=18 November 2009 |location=London}} M&S have 959 stores throughout the UK, as well as many international stores; 58 stores in [[India]], 48 stores in [[Turkey]], 37 in [[Russia]], 27 in [[Greece]], 17 in [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]], 14 in [[France]], 11 in [[Poland]], 6 in [[Hungary]] and [[Finland]] and 5 in [[Spain]]. In recent years its clothing sales have fallen whilst food sales have increased after the axing of [[St Michael (brand)|"St. Michael's"]] naming for their own brand. ==History== ===Establishment=== [[File:Marks & Spencer, Briggate, Leeds.jpg|thumb|Marks and Spencer on [[Briggate, Leeds|Briggate]] not far from their original branch in [[Leeds]].]] The company was founded by a partnership between [[Michael Marks]], a [[History of the Jews in Poland|Polish Jew]]{{cite web|url=http://www.bournemouth.ac.uk/facilitiesandresources/diversity/events/documents/multiculturalism_poster_m_s.pdf |title=Marks and Spencer – a Great British institution. |publisher=[[Bournemouth University]] |accessdate=4 December 2012 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130509144611/http://www.bournemouth.ac.uk/facilitiesandresources/diversity/events/documents/multiculturalism_poster_m_s.pdf |archivedate=9 May 2013 |df= }}{{harvtxt|Paul Burns|2008|pp=}} from [[Słonim]] (Marks was born into a Polish-Jewish family, a Polish refugee living in the Russian Empire, now in [[Belarus]]), and [[Thomas Spencer (Marks and Spencer)|Thomas Spencer]], a cashier from the English market town of [[Skipton]] in [[North Yorkshire]].{{cite web|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/dna/h2g2/A43825629 |title=The History of Marks and Spencer |publisher=BBC News |accessdate=18 April 2011}}{{cite web|url=http://theskiptonpress.co.uk/skiptons-illustrious-citizen-thomas-spencer-co-founder-marks-spencer/|title=Skipton’s Most Illustrious Citizen: Thomas Spencer, Co-Founder Of Marks & Spencer|publisher=Skipton Press|accessdate=25 February 2017}} On his arrival in England, Marks worked for a company in Leeds, called Barran, which employed refugees (see [[Sir John Barran, 1st Baronet]]). In 1884 he met Isaac Jowitt Dewhirst while looking for work. Dewhirst lent Marks £5 which he used to establish his Penny Bazaar on [[Leeds Kirkgate Market|Kirkgate Market]], in Leeds. Dewhirst also taught him a little English. Dewhirst's cashier was Tom Spencer, a bookkeeper, whose second wife, Agnes, helped improve Marks' English. In 1894, when Marks acquired a permanent stall in Leeds' covered market, he invited Spencer to become his partner.{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/gallery/2008/jul/09/marksandspencer.history|title=The history of Marks and Spencer|date=9 July 2008|publisher=The Guardian|accessdate=9 April 2017}} In 1901 Marks moved to the [[Birkenhead]] open market where he amalgamated with Spencer. The pair were allocated stall numbers 11 & 12 in the centre aisle in 1903, and there they opened the famous Penny Bazaar. The company left Birkenhead Market on 24 February 1923.{{cite web|url=http://www.upton-wirral.co.uk/wir3.php |title=Birkenhead Market Fire |work=upton-wirral.co.uk |accessdate=20 March 2015 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130427143731/http://www.upton-wirral.co.uk/wir3.php |archivedate=27 April 2013 |df=dmy }} The next few years saw Michael Marks and Tom Spencer open market stalls in many locations around the North West of England and move the original Leeds Penny Bazaar to 20, Cheetham Hill Road, [[Manchester]].{{cite web|url=http://www.spartacus.schoolnet.co.uk/BUmarks.htm |title=Spartacus: Michael Marks |publisher=Spartacus.schoolnet.co.uk |date=31 December 1907 |accessdate=18 April 2011 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605081542/http://www.spartacus.schoolnet.co.uk/BUmarks.htm |archivedate=5 June 2011 |df= }} ===Domestic growth=== [[File:Marks and Spencer shop, Bekonscot.JPG|thumb|Representation of historic store from the 1930s, [[Bekonscot]] model village, UK]] Marks and Spencer, known colloquially as "Marks and Sparks",''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' – [http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,919169,00.html "Business: Marks & Sparks Trades Up"], 28 November 1977 or "M&S", made its reputation in the early 20th century with a policy of only selling British-made goods (it started to back down from this policy in the 1990s.{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/analysis-and-features/mampss-uturns-will-the-latest-plans-last-2133453.html |title=M&S's U-turns: Will the latest plans last? |work=The Independent |location=London |accessdate=20 March 2015}}) It entered into long-term relationships with British manufacturers, and sold clothes and food under the "[[St Michael (brand)|St Michael]]" brand, which was introduced in 1928. The brand honours [[Michael Marks]]. It also accepted the return of unwanted items, giving a full cash refund if the receipt was shown, no matter how long ago the product was purchased, which was unusual for the time. M&S staff raised £5,000 to pay for a [[Supermarine Spitfire]] fighter aircraft called ''The Marksman'' in 1941.{{cite book | title = Marks in Time: 125 Years of Marks & Spencer | date = 3 September 2009 | last = Chislett | first = Helen | publisher=Weidenfeld and Nicolson | isbn = 978-0-297-85873-7 }} By 1950, virtually all goods were sold under the "St Michael" label. M&S lingerie, women's clothes and girls' school uniform were branded under the "St Margaret" label until the whole range of general merchandise became "St Michael". [[Simon Marks]], son of Michael Marks, died in 1964, after fifty-six years' service. [[Israel Sieff]], the son-in-law of Michael Marks, took over as chairman and in 1968, [[John Salisse]] became the company Director. A cautious international expansion began with the introduction of Asian food in 1974. M&S opened stores in continental Europe in 1975 and in Ireland four years later. The company put its main emphasis on quality, including a 1957 stocking size measuring system. For most of its history, it also had a reputation for offering fair value for money. When this reputation began to waver, it encountered serious difficulties. Arguably, M&S has historically been an iconic retailer of 'British Quality Goods'. The uncompromising attitude towards customer relations was summarised by the 1953 slogan: "The customer ''is'' always and completely right!" Energy efficiency was improved by the addition of thermostatically controlled refrigerators in 1963. M&S began selling [[Christmas cake]]s and [[Christmas pudding]]s in 1958. In an effort to improve the quality of their [[Swiss roll]]s, they hired the food expert Nat Goldberg, who made a major improvement across their entire cake range, which had lost the public's favour a few years earlier. As a later measure to improve food quality, food labelling was improved and "sell by dates" were phased in between 1970 and 1972. Smoking was banned from all M&S shops in 1959 because of the fire hazards it posed. In 1972, [[Marcus Sieff, Baron Sieff of Brimpton|Marcus Sieff]] became Chairman, remaining in place until 1984, and emphasising the importance of good staff relations to the tradition of the store, while extending staff benefits to areas such as restaurants and chiropody.{{cite news |url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/1323890/Lord-Sieff-of-Brimpton.html |title=Obituary - Marcus sieff |date=26 February 2001 |work=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |access-date=22 October 2014}} ===International expansion=== [[File:Central Tower Marks & Spencer 2009.jpg|thumb|A Marks & Spencer store in [[Central, Hong Kong]].]] [[File:Marks & Spencer in Times Square HK 201507.jpg|thumb|A Marks & Spencer store in [[Times Square (Hong Kong)|Times Square]], Causeway Bay, Hong Kong.]] M&S expanded into Canada in 1973, and at one point had forty seven stores across Canada. Despite various efforts to improve its image, the chain was never able to move beyond its reputation there as a stodgy retailer, one that catered primarily to senior citizens and expatriate Britons. The shops in Canada were smaller than British outlets, and did not carry the same selection. In the late 1990s, further efforts were made to modernise them and also expand the customer base. Unprofitable locations were closed. Nonetheless, the Canadian operations continued to lose money, and the last 38 shops in Canada were closed in 1999.{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbc.ca/money/story/1999/07/14/marks990714.html |title=Marks and Spencer close ahead of schedule |publisher=Canadian Broadcasting Corporation |date=10 November 2000 |accessdate=18 April 2011 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100826234315/http://www.cbc.ca/money/story/1999/07/14/marks990714.html |archivedate=26 August 2010 }} Expansion into France began with shops opening in Paris at [[Boulevard Haussmann]] and [[Lyon]] in 1975, followed by a second Paris shop at Rosny 2 in 1977. Further expansion into other French and Belgian cities followed into the 1980s. Although the Paris shops remained popular and profitable, the Western European operation as a whole did not fare as well and eighteen shops were sold in 2001.{{cite web|last=Pfanner |first=Eric |url=http://www.iht.com/articles/2001/10/18/t15_14.php |title=Galeries Lafayette buying 18 stores |work=International Herald Tribune |date=18 October 2001 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} However, in April 2011, M&S changed directions again with an announcement to reopen a store that will not only sell clothing but food as well. In addition the group will also open several food outlets throughout the French capital. The first branch opened on 24 November 2011 at the [[Champs-Élysées]] in a ceremony attended by the company's CEO [[Marc Bolland]], the model [[Rosie Huntington-Whiteley]] and the British Ambassador to France, Sir [[Peter Westmacott]].{{cite news| url=http://www.dailymail.co.uk/femail/article-2065504/Marks--Spencer-returns-France-Rosie-Huntington-Whiteley-attends-Paris-relaunch.html| location=London | work=[[Daily Mail]] | first1=Kim | last1=Willsher | title=M&S part deux: Rosie Huntington-Whiteley attends relaunch as retail chain returns to France...ten years after it left| date=25 November 2011}} The ''[[Daily Mail]]'' reported that 1,000 customers queued outside for over 2 hours at the opening of the {{convert|1400|m2|sqft|abbr=on}} store. In 1988, the company acquired [[Brooks Brothers]], an American clothing company{{cite web|url=http://www.brooksbrothers.com/aboutus/heritage3.tem |title=Brooks Brothers Heritage |publisher=Brooksbrothers.com |accessdate=18 April 2011}} and [[Kings Super Markets]], a US food chain.{{cite web|url=http://www.allbusiness.com/sector-44-45-retail-trade/clothing-clothing/1181357-1.html |title=Kings Supermarkets |publisher=Allbusiness.com |date=1 May 2006 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} In 2016 M&S expanded to sell through European marketplace [[Zalando]] on their German, French, Dutch, Belgian and Austrian sites with a range of kidswear and lingerie.{{Cite web|url=https://www.zalando.de/ms-london/|title=Marks & Spencer London Online-Shop {{!}} Marks & Spencer London versandkostenfrei bei Zalando|website=www.zalando.de|access-date=26 August 2016}} ===Financial decline=== [[File:M & S, Inverness (1998).png|thumb|M&S shop in [[Inverness]] in 1998]] M&S's profits peaked in the financial year 1997/1998. At the time it was seen as a continuing success story, but with hindsight it is considered that during Sir [[Richard Greenbury]]'s tenure as head of the company, profit margins were pushed to untenable levels, and the loyalty of its customers was seriously eroded. The rising cost of using British suppliers was also a burden, as rival retailers increasingly imported their goods from low-cost countries, but M&S's belated switch to overseas suppliers undermined a core part of its appeal to the public. Another factor was the company's refusal until 2001 to accept any credit cards except its own chargecard.{{cite web|url=http://www.ciao.co.uk/Marks_Spencer_Chargecard__Review_5001590 |title=Marks & Spencer storecard fading value |publisher=Ciao.co.uk |accessdate=18 April 2011}} These factors combined to plunge M&S into a sudden slump, which took the company, its shareholders, who included hundreds of thousands of small investors, and nearly all retail analysts and business journalists, by surprise. The company's share price fell by more than two thirds, and its profits fell from more than a billion pounds in 1997 and 1998 to £145 million in the year ended 31 March 2001.[http://www.telegraph.co.uk/money/main.jhtml?xml=/money/2008/07/02/bcnmshist102.xml Marks & Spencer: A Recent History] ''The Daily Telegraph'' Marks & Spencer launched an online shopping service in 1999.{{cite news| url=http://www.dailymail.co.uk/femail/article-17227/The-highs-lows-M-S.html | location=London | work=Daily Mail | title=The highs and lows of M&S}} In 2001, with changes in its business focus such as accepting credit cards, the introduction of the "Per Una" clothing range designed by [[George Davies (retailer)|George Davies]], and a redesign of its underlying business model, profits recovered somewhat.{{cite web|url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/newsbysector/retailandconsumer/2794432/Marks-and-Spencer-loses-Per-Una-design-director.html|title=Marks & Spencer loses Per Una design director|publisher=The Telegraph|date=7 August 2008|accessdate=9 April 2017}} In 2004, M&S was in the throes of an attempted takeover by [[Arcadia Group]] and [[British Home Stores|BHS]] boss, [[Philip Green]].{{Cite news|url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0DQA/is_2000_Feb_17/ai_59870857 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151016211356/http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0DQA/is_2000_Feb_17/ai_59870857 |dead-url=yes |archive-date=16 October 2015 |title=Green drops Marks & Spencer bid |publisher=Findarticles.com |accessdate=18 April 2011 |year=2000 }} On 12 July a recovery plan was announced which would involve selling off its financial services business [[M&S Bank|M&S Money]] to [[HSBC Bank (Europe)|HSBC Bank plc]], buying control of the ''Per Una'' range, closing the [[Gateshead]] Lifestore and stopping the expansion of its Simply Food line of shops. [[Philip Green]] withdrew his takeover bid after failing to get sufficient backing from shareholders.The book- "Marks in time" by Orionbooks.co.uk (2009) In February 2007, M&S announced the opening of the world's largest M&S shop outside the UK at [[Dubai Festival City]].{{cite web|url=http://dubai.mconet.biz/index.php?action=fullnews&id=282535&category=884&category_name= |title=Dubai Online |publisher=Dubai.mconet.biz |accessdate=7 November 2009 }}{{dead link|date=June 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} On 2 October 2008, M&S opened its first mainland China shop in [[Shanghai]]. Problems with the supply chain for the first few months of opening led Stuart Rose, M&S chairman, to describe failures in "basic shopkeeping".{{cite web|url=http://www.ft.com/cms/s/0/2bac61ae-f6e2-11dd-8a1f-0000779fd2ac.html |title=M&S admits Shanghai errors |first = Patti | last = Waldmeir |work=Financial Times |date=9 February 2009 |accessdate=19 December 2009}} ===Restructuring=== Twenty-two unprofitable and minor food stores, such as the ones at [[Ripon]] and [[Balham]], were closed in early 2009 as part of a cost cutting measure. In August 2010, it was confirmed that the [[Grantham]] branch of M&S would close, along with two other [[Lincolnshire]] branches in [[Skegness]] and [[Scunthorpe]] due to low sales in these older format stores. The closures were met with protests from the local communities and petitions were signed in support of retaining the stores, although they went ahead.BBC New Lincolnshire 25 August 2010 [http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-lincolnshire-11076135 'M&S confirms three store closures in Lincolnshire'] Retrieved 25 August 2010 The Retail Knowledge Bank conducted an audit of the company's brands in August 2010, and revealed that sales of womenswear were at a 10-year low. The audit covered both the Limited Collection, Autograph, Autograph Weekend, Classic Collection, Per Una, Portfolio and Indigo. ''Draper'' magazine claimed that Per Una was the only clothing brand not at risk of being axed while Marc Bolland considered which brands would be retained. Per Una was planned to stay due to its successful and distinctive flair, but Portfolio and Indigo were planned to go due to poor sales. Both the Limited Collection, Autograph, Autograph Weekend, Classic Collection brands were being considered for the cull during mid-2010, but were later given a reprieve.{{cite web|author=Isak Halfon, expansion director, Mango |url=http://www.just-style.com/news/bolland-review-to-streamline-ms-clothing-brands_id108648.aspx |title=UK: Bolland review to streamline M&S clothing brands?: Apparel and textile news & analysis |publisher=Just-style.com |date=17 August 2010 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} On 9 November 2010, chief executive Marc Bolland revealed plans to strengthen the company’s overall brand image and targeting sales of between £800m and £1bn for which company will increase capital expenditure to £850m to £900m over the next three years to fund the plans.{{Cite news| url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSLDE6A70V420101109 |agency=Reuters | first=Mark | last=Potter | title=UPDATE 5-Marks & Spencer's new CEO lifts investment | date=9 November 2010}} The plan also involved the discontinuation of its 'Portfolio' fashion brand and the sale of electrical products. The company also announced a new marketing strapline, 'Only at M&S', and that it would revamp its website.{{cite web|title=M&S plans £900m capital expenditure to boost sales|url=http://www.newstatesman.com/economy/2010/11/sales-plans-1bn-operations|work=2010 plans for expansion|accessdate=11 November 2010}} Bolland ordered a new store design in May 2011, and it was announced that the company would spend around £600 million between 2011 and 2014 on its UK stores, involving the launch of a range of different store formats based on the age, affluence and demographics of people in those areas. The design also included the trial of a new in-store "navigation scheme", which followed research showing that shoppers found M&S store layouts confusing and "difficult to shop [in]". It also confirmed that the amount of money-off promotions and deals offered would be increased, and that it would replace the Marks & Spencer label on clothing with "M&S Woman" and "M&S Man".{{cite news| url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/newsbysector/retailandconsumer/8534666/2bn-Marks-and-Spencer-makeover-less-than-inspiring.html | title=£2bn Marks & Spencer makeover 'less than inspiring'|date=25 May 2011|work=The Daily Telegraph|accessdate=25 March 2012|first=James|last=Hall|location=London}} By 2013, M&S's clothing division had an 11% market share in the UK.{{cite news|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-22605609 |title=Marks and Spencer profits fall as clothing disappoints |publisher=BBC News |date=21 May 2013 |accessdate=22 July 2013}}{{cite news|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-22546823 |title=M&S tries to boost sales with new clothing range |publisher=BBC News |date=15 May 2013 |accessdate=22 July 2013}}{{cite news|author=Emma Simpson |url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-22533986 |title=M&S tries to lure back shoppers with new fashion ranges |publisher=BBC News |date=14 May 2013 |accessdate=22 July 2013}} In May 2013 saw the launch of the ''Best of British'' range as well as the overhaul of ''Per Una'' and ''Indigo''.{{cite web |url=http://www.mirror.co.uk/money/city-news/marks-spencer-fashion-launch-slick-1889943 |title=Marks and Spencer fashion launch was slick but what matters is what core customers think |work=Daily Mirror |author=Hiscott, Graham |date=15 May 2013 |accessdate=22 July 2013}} Patrick Bousquet-Chavanne became the new marketing director, succeeding Steven Sharp in July. Mark Bolland also vowed to bring "quality and style back" M&S also stated it intended to increase its number of UK suppliers from the 20 it had at the time. In November 2013, it was revealed that Bill Adderley, founder of homeware chain [[Dunelm Group]], had amassed a £250m stake in M&S over the past 18 months. This disclosure was made as stock market rules mean that any holding over 3 per cent share must be made public.{{cite web|url=http://www.yorkshireeveningpost.co.uk/news/business-news/business-headlines/yorkshire-retail-entrepreneur-builds-up-250m-stake-in-m-s-1-6212162|title=Yorkshire retail entrepreneur builds up £250m stake in M&S|publisher=Yorkshire Evening Post|accessdate=12 March 2014}} On 7 January 2016 it was announced that [[Marc Bolland]], who has been CEO since 2010 would step down on 2 April 2016, and be replaced by [[Steve Rowe (businessman)|Steve Rowe]], head of clothing, and previously head of the food business.{{cite news|last1=Butler|first1=Sarah|last2=Kollewe|first2=Julia|title=M&S boss Marc Bolland to step down|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2016/jan/07/ms-boss-marc-bolland-to-step-down|accessdate=7 January 2016|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=7 January 2016}} ===2015 / 2016 store cull=== Stores identified for closure in July 2015 included [[Woolwich]], [[Walsall]], [[Erdington]], [[Aldershot]] (which was there since 1922), [[Pontypridd]] in Wales, [[Hounslow]] in west London, and [[Royal Quays]] in [[North Shields]], the three full-line stores in [[Stevenage]], [[Wood Green]] in north London, and The Fort shopping park in [[Castle Bromwich]] and the Simply Food in Castle Bromwich.{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2015/jul/29/marks-spencer-local-anger-confirming-store-closures-nine-shops|title=Marks & Spencer triggers local anger after confirming store closures|first=Graham|last=Ruddick|date=29 July 2015|publisher=|via=The Guardian}}{{cite web|url=http://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/11252488.UPDATE__Woolwich_M_S_to_close__with_Lewisham_store_losing_a_floor/|title=UPDATE: Woolwich M&S to close, with Lewisham store losing a floor|publisher=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2016/nov/08/m-and-s-marks-spencer-close-80-stores-major-overhaul|title=M&S to close 30 UK stores and cut back on clothing|first=Zoe|last=Wood|date=8 November 2016|publisher=|via=The Guardian}} The [[Lewisham]] store also lost a floor. The closures in 2015 also included three traditional food and clothing shops, one Simply Food store and four Outlet stores that sell end-of-season clothing. Some 430 workers were affected by the closures. The cull cost up to £200m to implement; the closure included loss-making stores in European markets such as France, Belgium and the Netherlands as well as outposts in China. ==Corporate affairs== ===Head office locations=== [[File:Paddington Waterside geograph-2790569-by-Colin-Smith.jpg|thumb|Waterside House, 35 North Wharf Road, London]] The headquarters of M&S was for a hundred years at Michael House, [[55 Baker Street]], London. In 2004 the company moved to a new headquarters designed by [[Michel Mossessian|mossessian & partners]] at Waterside House, in the new [[Paddington Basin]], London.{{cite web|url=http://www.marksandspencer.com/gp/node/n/46005031 |title=Paddington Basin registered business address |publisher=Marks & Spencer |accessdate=18 April 2011}} As well as the main offices in London, there are a number of other head office sites across the UK; Stockley Park (IT Services), [[Salford Quays]] and [[Spinningfields]], Greater Manchester (Marks & Spencer Shared Services Ltd. which provides human resources, and finance administration)"[http://www.marksandspencer.com/gp/node/n/45867031/026-7667460-4435653?ie=UTF8&mnSBrand=core Shared Services Recruitment Page]". Company Website{{cite web|url=http://www.liveherenw.co.uk/working/man/sha.asp |title=Living and Working in the North West – Working in Manchester: Shared Services |publisher=Liveherenw.co.uk |accessdate=18 April 2011 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090213163329/http://www.liveherenw.co.uk/working/man/sha.asp |archivedate=13 February 2009 |df= }} and [[Chester]] (HSBC's M&S Money and Retail Customer Services).{{cite web|url=http://www.lexdon.com/article/HSBC_and_Marks_&_Spencer/92.html |title=Lexdon Business Library – HSBC and Marks & Spencer complete the sale of M&S Money |publisher=Lexdon.com |accessdate=18 April 2011}} The company has overseas sourcing offices in Malaysia, Hong Kong, Thailand, India, Bangladesh, Turkey, China, Italy, Indonesia and Sri Lanka.[http://english.people.com.cn/200509/29/eng20050929_211522.html UK's leading retailer launches Asian Sourcing Office in Hong Kong] English People. 29 September 2005 ===Financial performance=== M&S is listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]] and is a constituent of the [[FTSE 100 Index]]. Chief executive Marc Bolland described the current market as "challenging". ===Social and environmental policy=== ===="Look Behind the Label"==== In 2006, the ''Look Behind the Label'' marketing campaign was introduced."[http://www.paddingtonwaterside.co.uk/timeforpaddington/ti_news_detail.asp?newsID=63 M&S launches new ‘Look behind the label' campaign] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928024224/http://www.paddingtonwaterside.co.uk/timeforpaddington/ti_news_detail.asp?newsID=63 |date=28 September 2007 }}". Paddington Waterside Partnership – 21 February 2006 The aim of this campaign was to highlight to customers the various ethical and environmentally friendly aspects of the production and sourcing methods engaged in by M&S including: [[Fairtrade]] products, [[sustainable fishing]] and environmentally friendly textile dyes. All coffee and tea sold in M&S stores is now Fairtrade."[http://www.foodnavigator.com/news/ng.asp?id=66333-marks-spencer-fairtrade-coffee Marks & Spencer dives into ethical consumer market]" Fletcher, Anthony – 10 March 2006 – Food Navigator.com (Europe) In addition, the company offers clothing lines made from Fairtrade cotton in selected departments."[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/business/4660410.stm M&S set to launch Fairtrade range]". BBC News Online – 30 January 2006 At Christmas, the company introduces a range of food products to support the housing charity [[Shelter (charity)|Shelter]]."[http://england.shelter.org.uk/howtohelp/howtohelp-682.cfm Marks & Spencer raises money for Shelter this Christmas]" (dead link) ===="Plan A"==== [[File:MarksAndSpencerBirmingham.jpg|thumb|M&S store on [[Birmingham]] High Street]] On 15 January 2007, M&S launched an initiative, known as "Plan A",{{cite web|url=http://plana.marksandspencer.com/ |title=Plan A |publisher=Plana.marksandspencer.com |accessdate=18 April 2011}} to dramatically increase the environmental [[sustainability]] of the business within 5 years and expected to cost £200 million.{{Cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/business/6261939.stm |title=Business | M&S unveils carbon-neutral target |publisher=BBC News |date=15 January 2007 |accessdate=7 November 2009}} The plan covers "100 commitments over 5 years to address the key social and environmental challenges facing M&S today and in the future" with the tag-line "Because there is no Plan B". The commitments span five themes: [[climate change]], [[waste]], sustainable raw materials, 'fair partnership' and health, with the aim that, by 2012, it will:[http://plana.marksandspencer.com/index.php?action=PublicPillarDisplay Marks & Spencer: Plan A – The Five Pillars], Marks & Spencer * Become carbon neutral * Send no waste to landfill * Extend sustainable sourcing * Help improve the lives of people in their supply chain * Help customers and employees live a healthier life-style Despite an 18% fall in the share price in January 2008, following publication of their latest [[trading statement]], the company confirmed that they would be continuing with the plan, saying that there were 'compelling commercial — as well as moral — reasons to do so'.[https://web.archive.org/web/20081206094008/http://www.hbrgreen.org/2008/03/the_hard_economics_of_green.html?cm_mmc=npv-_-listserv-_-MAR_2008-_-HBRGreen0305 The hard economics of green], [[Harvard Business Review]], [[Stuart Rose|Sir Stuart Rose]], published 4 March 2008 M&S introduced a reusable [[Hessian (cloth)|hessian]] bag in 2007 as part of the plan, aiming to reduce the number of plastic bags used within five years. This was followed in May 2008 by the introduction of a 5p charge for standard sized carrier bags used for food purchases (before this charge became compulsory).{{Cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/uk/7268283.stm |title=M&S to charge 5p for plastic bags |publisher=BBC News |date=28 February 2008 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} All profits from the sale of food part of the 'Plan A' initiative. Hundreds of volunteers worked for "...24 hours on 24 projects" at a variety of charities across the UK.{{cite news| url=http://www.dailymail.co.uk/femail/article-3181459/David-Gandy-helps-launch-M-S-new-Spark-Good-campaign.html| newspaper=Daily Mail| title=Launch of M&S' new Spark Something Good campaign| date=5 August 2015| first=Bianca| last=London| accessdate=5 August 2015}} ===Senior management=== The following have served as the Chairman of the company since it was founded: * 1884–1907: [[Michael Marks]] (set up first stall in Leeds in 1884) * 1907–1916: William Chapman.{{cite web|url=http://www.answers.com/topic/marks-and-spencer-p-l-c |title=Marks and Spencer plc |publisher=answers.com |accessdate=18 April 2011}} * 1916–1964: [[Simon Marks]] (Lord Marks) * 1964–1967: [[Israel Sieff]] (Lord Sieff) * 1967–1972: [[Edward Sieff]] * 1972–1984: [[Marcus Sieff]] (Lord Sieff) * 1984–1991: [[Derek Rayner, Baron Rayner|Derek Rayner]] (Lord Rayner) * 1991–1999: [[Richard Greenbury|Sir Richard Greenbury]] * 2000–2004: Luc Vandevelde * 2004–2006: [[Paul Myners]] * 2006–2009: [[Terence Burns, Baron Burns|Lord Burns]] * 2009–2010: [[Sir Stuart Rose]] * 2011 – present: Robert Swannell ==Stores== ===UK and Ireland=== [[File:A picture of M&S White City branch in Westfield London 2014-01-17 17-26.jpg|thumb|M&S White City in [[Westfield London]] is one of the company's largest stores.]] The largest shop is at [[Marble Arch]], on [[Oxford Street]] in London, which has around {{convert|16000|m2}} of [[shop floor]]. The second largest is in Cheshire Oaks, [[Ellesmere Port]], which is the largest outside London.{{cite web|url=http://www.propertyweek.com/story.asp?sectioncode=36&storycode=3103910&c=1 |title=M&S megastore for Leeds — Property Week |publisher=Property Week|accessdate=7 November 2009}} The third largest shop is at the Gemini Retail Park in [[Warrington]]. In 1999 M&S opened its shop in [[Manchester]]'s [[Exchange Square (Manchester)|Exchange Square]], which was destroyed in the [[1996 Manchester bombing]] and rebuilt. At re-opening, it was the largest M&S shop with {{convert|250000|sqft|m2|abbr=on|disp=flip}} of retail space, but half was subsequently sold to [[Selfridges]], the company's second site in Manchester. The smallest branch is an outlet located in the [[Grainger Market]] in Newcastle upon Tyne.{{cite web|url=http://www.newcastlegateshead.com/things-to-do/grainger-market-p433811|title=Grainger Market|publisher=Newcastle Gateshead|accessdate=20 March 2015}} M&S has opened a number of stores at out of town locations since the trend to build shopping centres away from town centres became popular in the 1980s. The first was at the [[MetroCentre (shopping centre)|MetroCentre]], [[Gateshead]], [[Tyne and Wear]], which opened in 1986. Another notable example is the store at the [[Merry Hill Shopping Centre]] at [[Brierley Hill]], West Midlands. This store opened on 23 October 1990 shortly after the closure of stores in the nearby town centres of [[Dudley]] and [[West Bromwich]]; the Merry Hill store was not originally intended to replace these two town centre stores, but both the Dudley and West Bromwich stores had experienced a downturn in trade as the opening of the Merry Hill store loomed, and both stores were closed on 25 August 1990.[https://web.archive.org/web/20120106032922/http://www.sthelens.oxon.sch.uk/Geography/Downloads/Geopress%20Factsheets/Geo%20factsheets/11%20out%20of%20town%20shopping%20centres.pdf Out Of Town Shopping Centres] Geofactsheet No. 11 Before Christmas 2006, twenty-two M&S shops were open for 24-hour trading including the recently opened new retail park stores at [[Bolton]] Middlebrook and at the Abbey Centre, [[Newtownabbey]], Northern Ireland."[http://www.marksandspencer.com/gp/browse.html/ref=sc_fe_c_1/026-7667460-4435653?ie=UTF8&node=51065031&no=51237031&mnSBrand=core&me=A2BO0OYVBKIQJM Marks & Spencer announces pre Christmas opening hours]" Press Release – 8 December 2006"[http://icwales.icnetwork.co.uk/0750expats/expats/tm_headline=-m-s--opens-for-24hrs-and-other-department-stores-extend-hours-to-boost-slow-trading-&method=full&objectid=18289095&siteid=50082-name_page.html M&S opens for 24hrs and other department stores extend hours to boost slow trading]{{dead link|date=June 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}". Watson, Molly — icWales.co.uk – 20 December 2006 The company's website has received criticism for having its prices in [[Pound sterling]] and not in euro, and for providing a search for its Irish stores through a "UK Store Finder".{{cite web|url=http://www.sbpost.ie/post/pages/p/story.aspx-qqqt=COMPUTERS+IN+BUSINESS-qqqs=computersinbusiness-qqqid=37099-qqqx=1.asp |title=Sunday Business Post | Irish Business News |publisher=Sbpost.ie |date=2 November 2008 |accessdate=7 November 2009}} ''[[The Irish Times]]'' pointed out that M&S failed to explain why the company is in a position to deliver goods ordered from its website to Brazil, Argentina, Iraq and Afghanistan but not to Ireland. M&S did not comment.{{cite news|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/pricewatch/2010/0111/1224262050906.html |title=M&S Vouchers |work=The Irish TImes |date=1 January 2010 |accessdate=18 April 2011}} ===International=== [[File:Marks & Spencer, The Mall Athens.JPG|thumb|A Marks & Spencer branch in [[Athens]]]] The company reopened its store in Paris on 24 November 2011, following the launch of a new French website on 11 October 2011.Rigby, Chloe [http://www.internetretailing.net/2011/10/ms-launches-new-french-website/ ''M&S launches new French website''] 11 October 2011, internetretailing.net In the Philippines there are 18 M&S shops, the largest of which is located in [[Greenbelt (Ayala Center)|Greenbelt Mall]]. A new store opened on 17 April 2013 in [[Kalverstraat]] in [[Amsterdam]], [[Netherlands]], more than 10 years after closure of the previous store. On 17 September 2013 the British ambassador to the Netherlands, Sir Geoffrey Adams, opened the first Dutch Marks & Spencer Food pilot store at a BP petrol station in Bijleveld beside the A12 motorway.BP press release [http://www.bp.com/genericarticle.do?categoryId=16002516&contentId=7086707 ''BP opent vandaag eerste Marks & Spencer Food pilot in Nederland''] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927092216/http://www.bp.com/genericarticle.do?categoryId=16002516&contentId=7086707 |date=27 September 2013 }} 10 September 2013, BPHorecatrends website [http://www.horecatrends.com/en/retail/marks-and-spencer-food-pilot-bij-bp-tankstation "Marks and Spencer Food pilot at BP gas station"] 12 September 2013, Horeca Trends There are over 300 stores in some 40 overseas locations.{{Cite news| url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2010/nov/07/bolland-strategy-marks-spencer | location=London | work=The Guardian | first=Julia | last=Finch | title=Bolland looks to middle England and overseas for Marks & Spencer blueprint | date=7 November 2010}} On 11 November 2013, Marks & Spencer announced "that it is set to have about 80 stores open in the region by 2016 as part of its strategy to become a leading international, multichannel retailer" with partner Reliance Retail.{{cite web | url=http://www.wwd.com/retail-news/mass-off-price/marks-spencer-to-expand-in-india-7272370?src=nl/mornReport/20131112 | title=Marks & Spencer to Expand in India | publisher=WWD | date=11 November 2013 | accessdate=12 November 2013 | author=Conti, Samantha}} It opened a flagship store in Bandra in Mumbai. M&S sales of lingerie accounts for more than a fifth of the sales in the Indian market, with total lingerie sales increasing by a third during the last six months of 2013. In May 2014 Marks & Spencer announced that their intention was now to open 100 stores in the country by 2016.{{cite web|url=http://in.reuters.com/article/2014/05/20/m-s-india-idINKBN0E00TU20140520|title=Marks & Spencer plans to open 100 stores in India by 2016|work=reuters.com|accessdate=20 March 2015}} In the Netherlands, as of 2015, M&S have a supermarket in the expensive [[Kalverstraat]] shopping street in Amsterdam, as well as a larger store including clothing in [[The Hague]].
